metadata.description: English translation of Muqātil ibn Sulaymān's Tafsīr (Qur'anic exegesis) for Sūras 80–114 (ʿAbasa to al-Nās), combined from 80to89.json, 90to99.json and 100-to-114.json. translation_conventions: Each record keeps the original Arabic ('text_ar', 'foot_note_ar') and adds 'text_en' and 'foot_note_en'.
Qur'anic quotations inside the commentary are placed in « » and translated; Qur'anic verse numbers appear in parentheses, e.g. (1).
Footnote markers appear in the text as [n] and correspond to the numbered entries in 'foot_note_en'.
Square brackets [ ] in the English text mark words supplied by the translator or a reading the editor added; folio markers from the manuscript (e.g. [249 a], [250 b]) are kept as in the Arabic.
ﷺ stands for ṣallā llāhu ʿalayhi wa-sallam; 'peace be upon him' renders ʿalayhi l-salām; '(Mighty and Majestic)' renders ʿazza wa-jall; '(Exalted)' renders taʿālā.

A, F and L in the editor's footnotes are the sigla of the manuscript witnesses used by the editor; they are kept as in the original. Arabic variant readings in the footnotes are given in transliteration with a gloss where the sense depends on it.
'[.....]' is an artefact of the digital edition and is kept as is.
'[sic]' and 'obscure' mark places where the Arabic text (or the editor) shows corruption or an uncertain reading; these were translated as literally as the sense allowed.
Verses of poetry are translated line by line; several lines are obscure or textually unsettled in the source.
Records for Sūras 80–99 carry English only; the manuscript sigla Ḥ and M (Ḥamīdiyya, Amāna) also appear in a few footnotes of Sūra 84.
Muqātil's technical term taqdīm (transposition in the order of the verses) is retained in transliteration.
metadata.translator_note: Translated by Claude (AI). Early-Islamic exegetical material, including narrations about the occasions of revelation, is rendered as reported by Muqātil and does not imply the translator's endorsement of its historicity; the editor's own footnotes (e.g. on the ʿgharānīqʾ report in sūra 109 and on magic in sūra 113) are likewise translated as written. For scholarly or citation use, check against the Arabic text.

records.text_en: Sūrat ʿAbasa (He Frowned)

[Sūrat ʿAbasa (80): verses 1 to 42] In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. He frowned and turned away (1) because the blind man came to him (2) And what would make you know — perhaps he might purify himself (3) or be reminded, and the reminder would benefit him (4) As for he who considers himself self-sufficient (5) to him you give attention (6) And it is not upon you if he does not purify himself (7) But as for he who came to you striving (8) while he fears [God] (9) from him you are distracted (10) No! Indeed, it is a reminder (11) So whoever wills may remember it (12) [It is] in honoured scrolls (13) exalted and purified (14) in the hands of scribes (safara) (15) noble and dutiful (16) May man be destroyed; how ungrateful he is! (17) From what thing did He create him? (18) From a sperm-drop He created him and determined him (19) Then He eased the way for him (20) Then He caused him to die and put him in a grave (21) Then when He wills, He will resurrect him (22) No! He has not yet accomplished what He commanded him (23) Let man look at his food (24) That We poured down water in torrents (25) Then We split the earth in clefts (26) And caused to grow within it grain (27) and grapes and vegetables (28) and olives and palm trees (29) and gardens of dense growth (30) and fruit and grass (31) [as] enjoyment for you and your livestock (32) But when the Deafening Blast comes (33) on the Day a man will flee from his brother (34) and his mother and his father (35) and his wife and his children (36) For every person among them, that Day, will be a matter adequate for him (37) Faces, that Day, will be bright (38) laughing, rejoicing at good news (39) And faces, that Day, will have dust upon them (40) Darkness will cover them (41) Those are the disbelievers, the wicked (42)
[Sūrat ʿAbasa [1]] Sūrat al-Aʿmā (the Blind Man) is Meccan; its number is «forty-two» [2] verses, according to the Kufan count [3].
records.foot_note_en:
1. The main purpose of the sūra: explaining the state of the blind man; the mention of the nobility of the Qur'an; the complaint against Abū Jahl and his denial of the resurrection and the Standing; the establishment of proof for the resurrection from the state of [text: «al-thabāt», probably «al-nabāt», «plant growth»], and the giving of life to the dead; the preoccupation of creatures in the plains [of the Gathering]; and the disparity in the states of the people of the [high] degrees and the [low] depths, in His saying: «Faces, that Day, will be bright, laughing, rejoicing at good news. And faces, that Day, will have dust upon them; darkness will cover them. Those are the disbelievers, the wicked» (Sūrat ʿAbasa: 38–42).
2. In A: «ithnān» («two»); the correct is: «ithnatān» or «thintān».
3. In the muṣḥaf: (80) Sūrat ʿAbasa, Meccan, its verses 43; revealed after Sūrat al-Najm. [.....] [Translator's note: the main text says forty-two, whereas this footnote says forty-three.]

records.text_en: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. His saying: «He frowned and turned away» (1) — He says: he frowned with his face and turned away to someone else. It was revealed about ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Sarḥ, the blind man — whose mother was Umm Maktūm; his name was ʿAmr ibn Qabs [sic, for Qays] ibn Zāʾida ibn Rawāḥa ibn al-Aṣamm ibn Ḥajar ibn ʿAbdūd ibn Bughayḍ ibn ʿĀmir ibn Luʾayy ibn Ghālib. As for Umm Maktūm, her name was ʿĀtika bint ʿĀmir ibn ʿAtika ibn ʿĀmir ibn Makhzūm ibn «Yaqaẓa» [1] ibn Murra ibn Kaʿb ibn Luʾayy. That is because one day he was sitting in the Sacred Mosque alone, with no «second» [2] person with him, and he was «a man» [3] blind of sight, when two angels descended from heaven to pray in the Sacred Mosque, and said: Who is this blind man who does not see in this world nor in the Hereafter? One of them said: But I am amazed at Abū Ṭālib, calling people to Islam! — while he does not see the two of them, but he heard that. So ʿAbd Allāh got up until he came to the Messenger of God ﷺ, and with him were Umayya ibn Khalaf [229a] and al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, standing before him as he presented Islam to them. ʿAbd Allāh said: O Muḥammad, I have come to you repenting; is there repentance for me? The Prophet ﷺ turned his face away from him, and turned his face toward al-ʿAbbās and Umayya ibn Khalaf; «so
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A: «laʿaṭa» without dots; in F: «Yaqaẓa» with dots.
2. In A: «thānī».
3. In A: «rajul».

records.text_en: ʿAbd Allāh repeated his speech» [1], but the Prophet ﷺ turned away «his face» [2] and scowled; so ʿAbd Allāh felt ashamed and thought that he had no repentance, and returned to his house. Then God (Mighty and Majestic) revealed concerning him: «He frowned and turned away» — meaning the Prophet ﷺ scowled and turned away «because the blind man came to him» (2). Then He said: «And what would make you know», O Muḥammad, «perhaps he might purify himself» (3) — He says: perhaps he would believe and pray, and reflect upon the Qur'an regarding what he had corrupted; «or be reminded» [3] by the Qur'an, «and the reminder would benefit him» (4) — meaning the admonition; He says: that you present Islam to him and he believes, and that reminder benefits him. And «as for he who considers himself self-sufficient» (5) — of God, in himself — meaning Umayya ibn Khalaf — «to him you give attention» (6) — meaning you call and turn your face to him; «and it is not upon you if he does not purify himself» (7) — He says: it is not upon you that he does not believe and does not set right what he had corrupted — these people. «But as for he who came to you striving» (8) in the heat «while he fears» (9) God, meaning Ibn Umm Maktūm, «from him you, O Muḥammad, are distracted» (10) — meaning you turn your face away from him. Then God (Mighty and Majestic) admonished the Prophet ﷺ «not to turn toward» [4] one who is self-sufficient of him, saying: do not turn toward him, and do not turn away from one who came to you striving; and do not turn toward the one who considers himself self-sufficient while turning away from one who fears his Lord. When this verse was revealed concerning Ibn Umm Maktūm, the Prophet ﷺ honoured him and afterwards appointed him as his deputy over Medina twice during his campaigns [5]. Then the speech was cut off; then He resumed, saying:
records.foot_note_en:
1. An addition required by the context, taken from al-Qurṭubī; it is not in A, nor in F, nor in any of the manuscripts.
2. In A: «wajhahu».
3. «Aw yadhdhakkaru»: missing from A, F.
4. In the original: «yaqbal».
5. Thus in al-Qurṭubī and others; and in A, F: «and he appointed him afterwards over Medina in his campaign, in the campaign of Banū Kināna, twice».

records.text_en: «No! Indeed, it is a reminder» (11) — meaning the verses of the Qur'an; «so whoever wills may remember it» (12) — meaning the Lord (Exalted) Himself; He says: whoever God (Exalted) wills to understand — meaning the Qur'an; He says: whoever wills to remember: that He entrusts the matter to His servants. Then He said: this Qur'an is «in honoured scrolls» (13) — meaning in honoured books — «exalted» — meaning by it the Preserved Tablet, exalted above the fourth heaven; its parallel is in al-Wāqiʿa [1] — with God — «purified» (14) — from polytheism and disbelief — «in the hands of scribes (safara)» (15) — meaning those scrolls are in the hands of noble Muslim scribes. Then He praised the scribe angels, saying: «noble» — meaning Muslims, and they are the angels — «dutiful» (16) — meaning obedient to God (Exalted), pure, righteous, free of sins; and it used to be brought down to them from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven on the Night of Decree, to the scribes among the angels; then Gabriel would bring it down to the Prophet ﷺ. Then the speech was cut off; that is His saying: «May man be destroyed» — meaning man was cursed — «how ungrateful he is!» (17) — He says: what has made him disbelieve! This verse was revealed about ʿUtba ibn Abī Lahab ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib [299b — sic, for 229b]. That is because he had been angry at his father and came to Muḥammad ﷺ and believed in him; «then when his father was pleased with him and reconciled with him» [2], and equipped him and sent him off to Syria with trade goods, «he said» [3]: Convey to Muḥammad from ʿUtba that he has disbelieved in the Star (al-najm). When the Prophet ﷺ heard of that, he said: O God, set upon him Your dog to eat him. So he stopped one night on some stretch of the road, and the lion came and ate him. Then He said, while knowing: «From what thing did He create him?» (18) — so He taught him how He created him, that he might take heed in his creation, saying: «From a sperm-drop He created him and determined him» (19) in
records.foot_note_en:
1. He refers to His saying (Exalted): «and raised couches» (Sūrat al-Wāqiʿa: 34).
2. In A: «fa-lammā raḍiya ʿanhu fa-ṣālaḥahu»; in F: «fa-lammā raḍiya abūhu ʿanhu wa-ṣālaḥahu».
3. «Fa-qāla»: thus in A, F; the more suitable is: «qāla».

records.text_en: the belly of his mother: from a sperm-drop, then from a clot, then from a morsel of flesh, then bone, then spirit; so He determined this creation in the belly of his mother, then he was brought out from the belly of his mother; «Then He eased the way for him» (20) — meaning He made easy his path in coming out of the belly of his mother; He says: He made it easy for him to come out. Does he not take heed, and affirm the oneness of God in the beauty of his creation, and give thanks to God for His blessings? «Then He caused him to die» at his appointed time «and put him in a grave» (21) «Then when He wills, He will resurrect him» (22) in the Hereafter — meaning when He wills, He will raise him after his death. «No!» — man does not believe in the resurrection. Then He resumed, saying: «He has not yet accomplished what He commanded him» (23) — meaning what God covenanted with him: the matter of the first covenant, meaning tawḥīd — meaning by it Adam (peace be upon him). Then He resumed mentioning what He created him upon, «so He mentioned» [1] his provision, that he might take heed, saying: «Let man look» — meaning ʿUtba ibn Abī Lahab — «at his food» (24) — meaning his provision: «That We poured down water in torrents» (25) upon the earth, meaning rain; «Then We split the earth in clefts» (26) — meaning with plants and trees; «and caused to grow within it grain» (27) — meaning all the grains; «and grapes and vegetables (qaḍb)» (28) — meaning by it fresh greens (al-riṭāb); «and olives» — meaning the fresh [plant] from which oil is pressed — «and palm trees» (29) «and gardens of dense growth» (30) — meaning intertwined trees, trees which enter into one another; «and fruit and grass (abb)» (31) — meaning pasture; «[as] enjoyment for you» — He says: in all this is enjoyment for you «and your livestock» (32) — so in this there is a lesson. And the Prophet ﷺ said: You were created from seven, and provided for from seven, and you came out upon seven. «But when the Deafening Blast (al-ṣākhkha) comes» (33) — meaning the cry; the ears of creation «are deafened» [2] by the cry from «the crier» [3], which creation hears. Then the Lord
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A: «dhakara».
2. In A: «sākhat»; in F: «ṣākhat».
3. In A: «lil-ṣāʾiḥ»; in F: «min al-ṣāʾiḥ». [.....]

records.text_en: (Mighty and Majestic) magnified that, saying: «On the Day a man will flee from his brother» (34) — meaning he will not turn to him — «and his mother and his father» (35) «and his wife» — meaning and his woman — «and his children» (36) «For every person among them, that Day, will be a matter adequate for him» (37) — «meaning when there is assigned to every person that which occupies him» [1] from these relatives. «Faces, that Day, will be bright» (38) — meaning joyful, radiant; then He described them, saying: «laughing, rejoicing at good news» (39) for the good and honour they were given. He said: «And faces, that Day, will have dust upon them» (40) — meaning blackness, as in His saying: «We will brand him» with blackness «upon the snout» [2]; «Darkness will cover them» (41) — meaning eclipse covers them, which is gloom. Then God (Mighty and Majestic) informed about them, saying: «Those» — for whom God wrote this evil in the Hereafter — «are the disbelievers» — meaning the deniers and the wrongdoers — «the wicked» (42) — meaning the liars. The Prophet ﷺ said: The Qur'an was sent down on the Night of Decree entirely, all of it, from the Preserved Tablet to the scribes among the angels in the lowest heaven; then Gabriel (peace be upon him) informed [text as printed] of it in twenty months; then Gabriel informed the Prophet of it — peace be upon the two of them — in twenty years.
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A, F: «that is, when there is assigned to every person his occupation, his affair, away from these relatives».
2. Sūrat al-Qalam: 16. [Running mark:] Tafsīr Muqātil ibn Sulaymān, vol. 4 – m. 38

records.text_en: Sūrat al-Takwīr (The Folding Up)

[Sūrat al-Takwīr (81): verses 1 to 29] In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. When the sun is wrapped up (kuwwirat) (1) and when the stars fall away (inkadarat) (2) and when the mountains are set in motion (3) and when the pregnant she-camels (ʿishār) are neglected (4) and when the wild beasts are gathered (5) and when the seas are set aflame (sujjirat) (6) and when the souls are paired (7) and when the girl buried alive (al-mawʾūda) is asked (8) for what sin she was killed (9) and when the pages are spread open (10) and when the sky is stripped away (11) and when the Blaze is set ablaze (12) and when Paradise is brought near (13) each soul will know what it has brought (14) So I swear by the retreating stars (15) that run and hide (16) and by the night when it departs (ʿasʿasa) (17) and by the dawn when it breathes (18) Indeed, it is the word of a noble Messenger (19) possessed of power, with the Owner of the Throne, secure [in position] (20) obeyed there, and trustworthy (21) And your companion is not mad (22) And he certainly saw him on the clear horizon (23) And he is not a withholder of [knowledge of] the unseen (24) And it is not the word of an accursed devil (25) So where are you going? (26) It is not except a reminder to the worlds (27) For whoever wills among you to take a right course (28) And you do not will except that God wills, Lord of the worlds (29)
[Sūrat al-Takwīr [1]] Sūrat al-Takwīr is Meccan; its number is twenty-nine verses, according to the Kufan count [2].
records.foot_note_en:
1. The main purpose of the sūra: explaining the states of the Resurrection and its terrors; the oath that Gabriel is trustworthy regarding the revelation, secure in position with his Lord, and that Muḥammad ﷺ is neither accused nor miserly, [but] speaks the truth; and explaining the reality of will and volition, in His saying: «… except that God wills, Lord of the worlds» (Sūrat al-Takwīr: 29).
2. In the muṣḥaf: (81) Sūrat al-Takwīr, Meccan, its verses 29; revealed after Sūrat al-Masad.

records.text_en: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. «When the sun is wrapped up (kuwwirat)» (1) — so its light goes; «and when the stars fall away (inkadarat)» (2) — meaning the planets darken and scatter; «and when the mountains are set in motion» (3) from their places and are levelled with the earth as they were the first time; «and when the pregnant she-camels (ʿishār) are neglected» (4) — meaning when the pregnant camels are left unattended, meaning the pregnant she-camel is forgotten by her owners; that is because nothing is dearer to the Bedouin than the pregnant she-camel; He says: her owners neglected her because of the matter they witnessed; «and when the wild beasts are gathered» (5) — meaning assembled; «and when the seas are set aflame (sujjirat)» (6) — meaning burst forth, one into the belly of another, the sweet and the salt, and became full — as in «the sea that is filled (al-baḥr al-masjūr)», meaning the full — so all the seas become one sea, like a basin with water in it; «and when the souls are paired» (7) — «the souls of» [1] the believers are paired with the wide-eyed ḥūr, and the souls of the disbelievers are paired with the devils — meaning the son of Adam and his devil, bound together in one chain, a pair — its parallel is in Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt, His saying (Mighty and Majestic): «Gather those who wronged and their spouses …» [2] — meaning their companions (qurīnāʾ); «and when the girl buried alive is asked» (8) — meaning the burying of daughters; that is because among the people of the Jāhiliyya, when a daughter was born «to him» [3], he would bury her in the earth while she was alive; that is His saying: «and when the girl buried alive is asked»,
records.foot_note_en:
1. «Anfus» («souls»): missing from A.
2. Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt: 22.
3. In A: «lahum».

records.text_en: «for what sin she was killed» (9) — her killer is asked for what sin he killed her, while she was alive and had never sinned; «and when the pages are spread open» (10) — that is because when a person dies his page is folded up; and when the Day of Resurrection comes, they are spread open for jinn and humankind, and they are given their books, the recording angels handing them [their books] spread open, in their right hands and in their left; «and when the sky is stripped away» (11) from those in it, for the descent of the Lord (Blessed and Exalted) and the angels; then it is folded up; «and when the Blaze is set ablaze» (12) — meaning kindled for His enemies; «and when Paradise is brought near» (13) — meaning brought close for His friends; «each soul will know what it has brought» (14) — meaning it will know what it did, and be certain, of good or evil, for which it will be recompensed — all of this on the Day of Resurrection. Then the Lord (Exalted) swore, saying: «So I swear» — meaning I swear — «by the retreating stars (khunnas)» (15) — and they are five of the planets: Bahrām [Mars], al-Zuhra [Venus], Zuḥal [Saturn], al-Barjahas — meaning Jupiter — and ʿUṭārid [Mercury]; and the khunnas are those that retreat (khanasat) by day so that they are not seen, and appear at night so that they are seen. He said: «that run «(al-jawār)» [1]» «and hide (al-kunnas)» (16) — because they run in the sky and hide (al-kunnas), meaning they conceal themselves as gazelles conceal themselves in their lairs (kināsihinna); «and by the night when it departs (ʿasʿasa)» (17) — meaning when it grows dark; «and by the dawn when it breathes» (18) — meaning when its colour brightens. So God (Exalted) swore by these signs that this Qur'an «is the word of a noble Messenger» [2] (19) with God — meaning Gabriel (peace be upon him); he taught Muḥammad ﷺ; «possessed of power» — meaning possessed of might; that is because when the Prophet ﷺ was sent, Iblīs said: Who [will deal] with this prophet who has come out of the land of Tihāma? A devil — whose name was al-Abyaḍ, the companion of the prophets — said: I will. So he came to the Prophet ﷺ and found him in
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A: «al-jawārī».
2. «Innahu la-qawlu rasūlin karīm»: missing from A.

records.text_en: the House of al-Ṣafā. When he left, al-Abyaḍ stood in the form of Gabriel (peace be upon him) in order to give him revelation; then Gabriel (peace be upon him) descended and stood between him and the Prophet ﷺ, and Gabriel (peace be upon him) pushed him with his hand, a gentle push, so that he fell from Mecca to the farthest part of India, out of fear. Then He said: «with the Owner of the Throne, secure [in position]» (20) — Gabriel (peace be upon him); He says: he is eminent with God (Mighty and Majestic). Then He said: «obeyed there (thamma)» — meaning there, in the heavens, as in His saying: «… and We brought near» — meaning We drew close — «there (thamma) …» [1] meaning there; and as in His saying: «And when you look there (thamma) …» [2] [3] meaning there. That is because on the night the Prophet ﷺ was taken up to the heavens, he saw Ibrāhīm ﷺ and Mūsā — peace be upon the two of them [4] — and they shook his hand; «and Gabriel took him around among the angels in the heavens, and they rejoiced at him» [5] and shook his hand; «and he saw Mālik» [6], the keeper of the Fire, who did not speak to him nor greet him; so the Prophet ﷺ said to Gabriel (peace be upon him): Who is this? He said: This is Mālik, the keeper of Jahannam, who has never spoken, and these persons are with him; the keepers of Jahannam have had compassion and mercy removed from them, and scowling and anger toward the people of Jahannam cast upon them; but had they spoken to anyone since they were created, they would have spoken to you, because of your honour with God (Mighty and Majestic). The Prophet ﷺ said: Tell him
records.foot_note_en:
1. «Thamma»: missing from the original; the verse is from Sūrat al-Shuʿarāʾ: 64.
2. In A, F: «fī».
3. Sūrat al-Insān: 25 [as printed; the verse is 76:20].
4. In A, F: «ʿalayhim».
5. In F: «and when they saw the angels in the heavens they rejoiced at him»; and in A: «and he took him around among the angels in the heavens, and they rejoiced at him». [.....]
6. In F: «fa-raʾā Mālik»; in A: «wa-raʾā Mālik».

records.text_en: to uncover a door of it; so he uncovered something like the nostril of a bull from it, and it shook, and came with a great matter — they thought it was the Hour — until the Prophet ﷺ was alarmed by it. He said to Gabriel: «Command him to put it back» [1]. Gabriel commanded him, and Mālik (peace be upon him) obeyed him and put it back; that is His saying: «obeyed there» «and trustworthy» (21) — he is called trustworthy because of what God (Mighty and Majestic) entrusted to him of His command among His creation. «And your companion is not mad» (22) — meaning the Prophet ﷺ; that is because the disbelievers of Mecca said: Muḥammad is mad, and he only «says it» [2] on his own. «And he certainly saw him on the clear horizon» (23) — meaning from the direction of the rising [place]; that is because the Prophet ﷺ saw Gabriel (peace be upon him) in his [true] form from the east, over the mountains of Mecca, having filled the horizon, his two feet on the earth and his head in the sky, with a wing from the east and a wing from the west; and the Prophet ﷺ fainted. Then Gabriel (peace be upon him) changed into the form of a human being and said: I am Gabriel, and he began to wipe from his face [3] and to say: I am your brother, I am Gabriel, until he recovered. The believers said: We have not seen you, since you were sent, more beautiful than today. The Prophet ﷺ said: Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to me in his [true] form; and it was he who left this [radiance] clinging to me from his beauty. «And he is not a withholder (bi-ḍanīn) of [knowledge of] the unseen» [4] (24) — «bi-ẓanīn» [5]
records.foot_note_en:
1. «Murhu fa-l-yaruddahā»: from F; it is not in A.
2. In A: «yaqūluhu».
3. That is, from the face of the Prophet ﷺ.
4. In A: «bi-ẓanīn»; and the reading of Ḥafṣ is «bi-ḍanīn».
5. «Bi-ẓanīn»: an addition required by the context.

records.text_en: meaning: Muḥammad ﷺ is not suspected concerning the Qur'an; and whoever reads «bi-ḍanīn» means «miserly». [231a] «And it is not the word of an accursed devil (shayṭān rajīm)» (25) — meaning cursed; that is because the disbelievers of Mecca said: Only al-Riyy brings it — and he is the devil, whose name is al-Riyy — and he casts it upon the tongue of Muḥammad ﷺ. In it there is a taqdīm [transposition in the order of the text]. He says to the disbelievers of Mecca: «So where are you going?» (26) — meaning where are you hastening away from My Book and My command, because of their saying that Muḥammad is mad? «It is not except a reminder to the worlds» (27) — meaning there is nothing in the Qur'an but a reminder and reflection for the worlds, «for whoever wills among you», O people of Mecca, «to take a right course» (28) upon the truth. Then He referred the will back to Himself, saying: «And you do not will «the right course»» [1] «except that God wills, Lord of the worlds» (29). His saying: «and by the night when it departs (ʿasʿasa)» — it grows dark upon every creeping creature: beetles, snakes, scorpions, predators, and «wild beasts» [2].
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A: «al-iqāma».
2. In A: «wa-l-waḥsh»; in F: «wa-l-wuḥūsh»; the sentence is disordered in A, and it is from F.

records.text_en: Sūrat al-Infiṭār (The Cleaving)

[Sūrat al-Infiṭār (82): verses 1 to 19] In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. When the sky breaks apart (1) And when the stars fall, scattering (2) And when the seas are made to burst forth (3) And when the graves are overturned (4) A soul will know what it has put forward and what it has left behind (5) O mankind, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous (6) Who created you, proportioned you, and balanced you (7) In whatever form He willed, He assembled you (8) No! But you deny the Judgment (9) And indeed, over you are keepers (10) Noble, recording (11) They know whatever you do (12) Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss (13) And indeed, the wicked will be in a Blaze (14) They will burn in it on the Day of Judgment (15) And they will not be absent from it (16) And what can make you know what the Day of Judgment is? (17) Then what can make you know what the Day of Judgment is? (18) The Day when a soul will not possess anything for another soul, and the command, that Day, belongs to God (19) Tafsīr Muqātil ibn Sulaymān, vol. 4 – part 39
[Sūrat al-Infiṭār [1]] Sūrat al-Infiṭār is Meccan; its number is «nineteen» [2] verses, according to the Kufan count.
records.foot_note_en:
1. The main purpose of the sūra: the report on the state of the sky and its stars at the end of time, and the explanation of man's heedlessness; the mention of the angels entrusted with what proceeds from the tongue and the limbs; and the explanation of the Real's (Exalted) bringing about the judgment that encompasses the gathering of humans and jinn.
2. In A: «seventeen verses, Kufan». And in the muṣḥaf: (82) Sūrat al-Infiṭār, Meccan, its verses 19; revealed after Sūrat al-Nāziʿāt. And in Baṣāʾir Dhawī al-Tamyīz fī Laṭāʾif al-Kitāb al-ʿAzīz by al-Fīrūzābādī: its verses are nineteen.

records.text_en: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. «When the sky breaks apart» (1) — meaning it is split, meaning it is cleft open from fear at the descent of the Lord (Mighty and Majestic) and the angels; then it is rolled up. «And when the stars fall, scattering» (2) — meaning they fall down. «And when the seas» — meaning the fresh and the salt — «are made to burst forth» (3) — some of them into the interior of others, so the seas become one sea, and it is filled. «And when the graves are overturned» (4) — meaning they are searched out for those of the dead who are in them. «A soul will know what it has put forward» of good «and what it has left behind» (5) of evil. «O mankind, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous?» (6) — It was revealed about Abū al-Ashuddayn, whose name was Usayd ibn Kalada; he was one-eyed and of formidable might; he said: If I take hold of one ring of the gate of Paradise, many people will certainly enter it! He was killed on the day of the conquest of Mecca; meaning Satan deceived him. Then He said: «Who created you, proportioned you, and balanced you» (7) — meaning He set you upright; «In whatever form He willed, He assembled you» (8) — meaning: had He willed, He would have assembled you in a form other than the human form. «No!» — this human being does not believe in the One who created him and fashioned him. Then He said: «But you deny the Judgment» (9) — meaning the Reckoning. «And indeed, over you are keepers» (10) — from among the angels, who preserve your deeds. Then He described them, saying: [231b] «Noble» — meaning Muslims — «recording» (11) — they write down the deeds of the children of Adam in Syriac; so in whatever tongue the son of Adam speaks, they write it only in Syriac, and the reckoning is in Syriac; and when they enter Paradise they speak Arabic, in the tongue of Muḥammad ﷺ. «They know whatever you do» (12) — of good and evil

and so they write it down. «Indeed, the righteous (al-abrār)» — meaning those obedient to God in this world — «will be in bliss» (13) — meaning the bliss of the Hereafter. «And indeed, the wicked (al-fujjār)» — meaning the wrongdoers in this world — «will be in a Blaze» (14) — meaning the Fire: meaning the greater part of it. «They will burn in it» — they will burn in the Blaze — «on the Day of Judgment» (15) — meaning the Day of Reckoning, the Day on which servants are requited for their deeds. «And they will not be absent from it» (16) — meaning the wicked are made present at the Blaze; they will not be absent from it. Then He said: «And what can make you know what the Day of Judgment is?» (17) — in magnification of it; He repeated it, saying: «Then what can make you know what the Day of Judgment is?» (18) — meaning the Day of Reckoning. Then He informed His Prophet ﷺ about the Day of Judgment, saying: «The Day when a soul will not possess» — meaning will not be able — «anything for another soul» — meaning of benefit. Then He said: «and the command, that Day, belongs to God» (19) — meaning the whole Day of Judgment belongs to God alone; meaning no one but Him possesses the command that Day; He alone.
Sūrat al-Muṭaffifīn (The Defrauders)

[Sūrat al-Muṭaffifīn (83): verses 1 to 36] In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Woe to the defrauders (1) Who, when they take a measure from people, take in full (2) But if they measure or weigh for them, they cause loss (3) Do those not think that they will be resurrected (4) For a tremendous Day (5) The Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds (6) No! Indeed, the record of the wicked is in Sijjīn (7) And what can make you know what Sijjīn is? (8) A written record (9) Woe, that Day, to the deniers (10) Who deny the Day of Judgment (11) And none denies it except every sinful transgressor (12) When Our verses are recited to him, he says: Legends of the former peoples (13) No! Rather, what they used to earn has covered their hearts (14) No! Indeed, from their Lord, that Day, they will be veiled (15) Then indeed, they will burn in the Hellfire (16) Then it will be said: This is what you used to deny (17) No! Indeed, the record of the righteous is in ʿIlliyyīn (18) And what can make you know what ʿIlliyyūn is? (19) A written record (20) Those brought near [to God] witness it (21) Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss (22) On adorned couches, observing (23) You will recognize in their faces the radiance of bliss (24) They will be given to drink from a sealed pure wine (25) Its seal is musk — and for that let the competitors compete (26) And its mixture is from Tasnīm (27) A spring from which those brought near drink (28) Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed (29) And when they passed by them, they would exchange winks (30) And when they returned to their people, they would return jesting (31) And when they saw them, they would say: Indeed, those are surely astray (32) But they had not been sent as guardians over them (33) So today those who believed are laughing at the disbelievers (34) On adorned couches, observing (35) Have the disbelievers been rewarded for what they used to do? (36)
[Sūrat al-Muṭaffifīn [1]] Sūrat al-Muṭaffifīn is Medinan; its number is «six» [2] and thirty verses, according to the Kufan count [3].
records.foot_note_en:
1. The main purpose of the sūra: the completion of measure and weight, and guarding against defrauding and shortfall; the mention of Sijjīn for the people of disobedience and of ʿIlliyyīn for the people of faith; the delicate favour shown to the believers and the obedient in the bliss of the Gardens, and the humiliation of the disobedient in the torment of the Fires, and their requital in accordance with their crime and disbelief, in His saying (Exalted): «Have the disbelievers been rewarded for what they used to do?» (Sūrat al-Muṭaffifīn: 36).
2. In A: «sitta» («six», with the final tāʾ).
3. In the muṣḥaf: (83) Sūrat al-Muṭaffifīn, Meccan, its verses 36; revealed after Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt, and it is the last sūra revealed in Mecca. [Translator's note: the main text says Medinan, whereas this footnote says Meccan.]

records.text_en: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. «Woe to the defrauders» (1) — Wayl is a valley in Hell, the extent of which is a journey of seventy years; in it are ninety thousand ravines, in every ravine seventy thousand fissures, in every fissure seventy thousand caves, in every cave seventy thousand palaces, in every palace seventy thousand iron chests, and in the chest seventy thousand trees, on every tree seventy thousand branches of fire, on every branch seventy thousand fruits, and in every fruit a worm seventy cubits long; beneath every tree are seventy thousand serpents «and seventy thousand scorpions. As for the serpents [1]», their length is a month's journey, in thickness like mountains, their fangs like palm trees; and its scorpions are like dark mules, having three hundred and sixty vertebrae, in each vertebra a jar of venom. That was because when the Messenger of God ﷺ went out to Medina, the people in the market of the Jāhiliyya had two measures and two scales «known [2]», for which they were not criticized: when a man bought, he bought with the larger measure, and when he sold, he sold with the deficient one, and they made a profit between the two measures and the two scales. «So when the Prophet ﷺ came to Medina [3]» he said to them: Woe to you for what you do! So God (Exalted) sent down the confirmation upon his tongue
records.foot_note_en:
1. The passage between the guillemets « …. » is from F; it is missing from A. [.....]
2. «Maʿlūma»: thus in A and F; the more fitting is «maʿlūmayn» (the dual).
3. In A: «So when he went out, the Prophet ﷺ came to Medina»; the adopted reading is from F.

records.text_en: and He said: «Woe to the defrauders». Then He mentioned their evil conduct, saying: «Who, when they take a measure from people, take in full» (2) «But if they measure or weigh for them, they cause loss» (3) — meaning they diminish. Then He warned them, saying: «Do those not think» — those who do this — [232] «that they will be resurrected» (4) «for a tremendous Day» (5) «The Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds» (6) — which is the span of three hundred years, when they are brought out of their graves; they wander toward one another, standing, looking on. Then He warned them again, saying: «No!» — it is a threat, like what a person says: By God! — swearing by his Lord; and God (Mighty and Majestic) does not say 'by God', but He says «No!» — «Indeed, the record of the wicked is in Sijjīn» (7) — meaning the deeds of the polytheists, written and sealed with evil, placed beneath the lowest earth, beneath the cheek of Iblīs, because they obeyed him and disobeyed their Lord; that is His saying: «And what can make you know what Sijjīn is?» (8) — in magnification of it. He said: «A written record» (9). He also threatened them, saying: «Woe, that Day, to the deniers» (10) — of the resurrection — «Who deny the Day of Judgment» (11) — meaning the Day of Reckoning, in which deeds are repaid. He said: «And none denies it» — the Reckoning — «except every sinful transgressor» (12) — He says: one who transgresses against his Lord «in that [1]» he doubted His favour and worshipped other than Him; so «he [2]» is the transgressor, «sinful» in his heart. «When Our verses are recited to him» — meaning the Qur'an — «he says: Legends of the former peoples» (13) — meaning by it the book of the ancients, such as the book of Rustam and Isfandiyār. This verse was revealed about al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith «ibn ʿAlqama, who came to al-Ḥīra [3]», and wrote down the story of Rustam and Isfandiyār; when he
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A: «khabīth» («vile»); in F: «ḥabth» (as printed).
2. In A: «fa-hādhā» («so this one»); in F: «fa-huwa» («so he»).
3. «Ibn ʿAlqama, who came to al-Ḥīra»: missing from A; it is from F.

records.text_en: came [1] he said: What does Muḥammad tell you? They said: He tells us about the former generations. He said: And I will tell you the like of what Muḥammad tells you, too. So God (Mighty and Majestic) sent down regarding him: «And among the people is he who buys idle talk to mislead from the way of God without knowledge and takes it in mockery [2]…»; that is His saying: «When Our verses are recited to him, he says: Legends of the former peoples». Then He threatened them, saying: «No! Rather, what they used to earn has covered their hearts» (14) — He says: We have sealed their hearts, «so they do not see their evils [3]» «and desist [4]» from them. Then He threatened them further, saying: «No! Indeed, from their Lord, that Day, they will be veiled» (15) — because the people of Paradise will see Him plainly; nothing veils them from Him, and He speaks to them; whereas the disbeliever is made to stand behind the veil, «and God (Exalted) does not speak to them [5]», nor look at them, nor purify them, until He commands that they be taken to the Fire. «Then indeed they» — meaning when they are veiled from their Lord — «will burn in the Hellfire» (16). «Then it will be said to them: This is what you used to deny» (17) — that is because Mālik, the keeper of the Fire, «says [6]» to the people of the Fire: «This is the Fire which you used to deny [7]», «Is this magic, or do you not see? Burn in it, and be patient or be not patient — it is the same for you. You are only being recompensed for what you used to do [8]»; that is His saying: «Then it will be said: This is what you used to deny». Then He threatened them, saying: «No!» — and then the speech broke off; then He returned to His saying in:
records.foot_note_en:
1. Thus in A and F; the meaning is «when he came from al-Ḥīra to Mecca».
2. Sūrat Luqmān: 6.
3. Thus in A and F («masāwatihim»); the more fitting would have been «masāwiʾahum» («their evils»).
4. In A: «fa-yaqṭaʿūna»; in F: «fa-yaqliʿūna».
5. Thus in A and F; the more fitting is «fa-lā yukallimuhu» («so He does not speak to him»), because the discourse concerns the singular; but he built into «the disbeliever» the sense of the genus, and so returned the plural pronoun to it.
6. In A: «qāla».
7. Sūrat Saba': 42.
8. Sūrat al-Ṭūr: 15–16.

records.text_en: «Woe to the defrauders», and He said: «Indeed, the record of the righteous is in ʿIlliyyīn» (18) — at the leg (sāq) of the Throne — meaning the deeds of the believers and their good deeds. «And what can make you know [232b] what ʿIlliyyūn is?» (19) — in magnification of it. So He said: «A written record» (20) — meaning a book from among the books of good, sealed with a seal of mercy, written with God (Mighty and Majestic). «Witness it» — that is, they witness it — «those brought near» (21) — and they are the angels of every heaven: seven angels from the near ones of the people of each heaven, who escort that deed with which God is pleased until its being established with God (Mighty and Majestic); then each angel returns to his place. «Then He mentioned [1]» the righteous, saying: «Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss» (22) — meaning the bliss of Paradise. Then He explained that bliss, saying: «On adorned couches, observing» (23) — [observing] that bliss — and they are the beds and the canopies; so when there is a «bed [2]» without a canopy upon it, it is a bed then, and when there is a canopy without a bed in it, it is a canopy; and when bed and canopy are combined they are the arāʾik; meaning these are sitting, observing that bliss. He says: «You will recognize in their faces the radiance of bliss» (24) — because the light of joy and bliss clings to his face, so it is not hidden from you, when you look at them, that they are rejoicing. Then He said: «They will be given to drink from a sealed pure wine» (25) — which is white wine when its fragrance reaches its peak — «its seal is musk» — when he drinks and finishes and removes the vessel from his mouth, he finds the taste of musk. «And for that» — meaning for that fragrance and for Paradise — «let the competitors compete» (26) — meaning let those who vie, vie; and it also means: let the desirous desire. Then He said: «And its mixture is from Tasnīm» (27) — «a spring» from the Garden of ʿAdn, which is poured upon them in a stream; that is His saying
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A: «then, also».  [.....]
2. In A: «sarīr»; in F: «sarīran».

records.text_en: «drink [1]» «from it» «those brought near» (28) — He says: they mix the wine with that water; they are the people of the Garden of ʿAdn, which is four gardens, and it is the center of Paradise: the water of Tasnīm comes out of the Garden of ʿAdn, and al-Kawthar, and al-Salsabīl; then the speech broke off. His saying: «Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed» (29) — this verse was revealed about ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and his companions; that is because they used to pass every day by the hypocrites and the Jews while on their way to the Messenger of God ﷺ, and when these saw them, they mocked them and winked at one another about their affair, «and laughed [2]» at them; and when they returned to their companions, they laughed at them. That is because ʿAbd Allāh ibn Nutayl met Bidʿa ibn al-Aqraʿ and said: Did you notice that we saw the bald one today and laughed at him? He said: How so? He said: Because he walks in front of them, and they are behind him, not passing him, as if he were the one guiding them on the way. Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq (may God be pleased with him) heard of that, and it distressed him and his companions, so they abandoned that road and took another road. So God (Mighty and Majestic) sent down regarding them: «Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed». «And when they passed by them, they would exchange winks» (30) «And when they returned to their people, they would return «jesting [3]»» (31) — meaning ʿAbd Allāh ibn Nutayl — meaning [233a] when they returned to their people, they returned pleased with the misguidance they were in, and with what they had done to ʿAlī and his companions (may God have mercy on them). «And when they saw them, they would say: Indeed, those are surely astray (32) But they had not been sent as guardians over them [4]» (33).
records.foot_note_en:
1. «Bihā» («from it»): missing from A.
2. In A: «wa-yaḍḥakūna».
3. In A: «fākihīn».
4. Verses 32 and 33 are missing from A and F, together with their commentary. Tafsīr Muqātil ibn Sulaymān, vol. 4 – part 40.

records.text_en: Then He informed [them] of their recompense from God, saying: «So today those who believed are laughing at the disbelievers» (34) «on the couches» — and the arāʾik are the bed within the canopy; He says: sitting in the canopy, laughing at their enemies; that is because every man of the people of Paradise has an opening (thulma) through which they look at the enemies of God — how they are being tormented. So when they look at the people of the Fire, and at what they themselves have met of the mercy of God (Mighty and Majestic), and they know that God has honored them, they laugh at the people of the Fire and speak with them, until He shuts the doors of the Fire upon the people of the Fire, with pillars [1] of iron, of fire, like mountains; so when these are shut upon them, those windows are «blocked [2]», and God erases their names and «removes them [3]» from the hearts of the believers. That is His saying: «observing» (35) «Have the disbelievers been rewarded for what they used to do?» (36) — «meaning they look from the windows [4]»; so when they see them being tormented, they say: By God, the disbelievers have been rewarded for what they used to do [5].
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A: «ʿamad»; in F: «ʿimād».
2. In A: «asnadat»; in F: «insaddat».
3. In A and F: «wa-akhrajahum».
4. In F: «hal».
5. In F there is an addition: «meaning they look, in the windows».

records.text_en: Sūrat al-Inshiqāq (The Splitting Open)

[Sūrat al-Inshiqāq (84): verses 1 to 25] In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. When the sky is split open (1) And listens to its Lord and is obligated [to do so] (2) And when the earth is stretched out (3) And throws out what is within it and becomes empty (4) And listens to its Lord and is obligated [to do so] (5) O mankind, indeed you are laboring toward your Lord with [great] exertion, and you will meet Him (6) Then as for he who is given his record in his right hand (7) He will be judged with an easy account (8) And return to his people in happiness (9) But as for he who is given his record behind his back (10) He will cry out for destruction (11) And will burn in a Blaze (12) Indeed, he used to be among his people in joy (13) Indeed, he thought that he would never return [to God] (14) Yes! Indeed, his Lord was ever Seeing of him (15) So I swear by the twilight glow (16) And by the night and what it envelops (17) And by the moon when it becomes full (18) You will surely embark upon stage after stage (19) So what is [the matter] with them that they do not believe (20) And when the Qur'an is recited to them, they do not prostrate (21) But those who disbelieve deny (22) And God is most knowing of what they keep within themselves (23) So give them tidings of a painful punishment (24) Except those who believe and do righteous deeds; for them is a reward uninterrupted (25)
[Sūrat al-Inshiqāq [1]] Sūrat al-Inshiqāq is Meccan; its number is «twenty-five [2]» verses, according to the Kufan count [3].
records.foot_note_en:
1. The main purpose of the sūra: the explanation of the state of the earth and the sky in obedience to the Creator (Exalted); the bringing out of the dead for the resurrection; the engagement in piety and kindness; the explanation of the ease of the reckoning for the obedient, and the report of their «qarḥ» [sic; probably «faraḥ», joy] in the bliss of the Gardens; the weeping of the disobedient and the disbelievers and their woe, in their persisting in the levels of the Fires; the oath by the splitting of the moon; the Real's awareness of persistence [in sin] and of open declaration; and the recompense of the obedient without any reproach, in His saying: « …. so for them is a reward uninterrupted» (Sūrat al-Inshiqāq: 25).
2. In A: «forty-five».
3. In the muṣḥaf: (84) Sūrat al-Inshiqāq, Meccan, its verses 25; revealed after Sūrat al-Infiṭār.

records.text_en: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. His saying: «When the sky is split open» (1) — He says: it is split open for the descent of the Lord of Might and the angels; it splits until its two ends [1] are seen, and then it is seen as a worn-out creation. That is because there were two brothers from Banū Umayya, «one of whom was named ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Asad, and the other named al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd al-Asad [2]». One of them believed in God, and his name was ʿAbd Allāh; as for the other, his name was al-Aswad, and he was the disbeliever. He said to his brother ʿAbd Allāh: Have you believed in Muḥammad? He said: Yes. He said: Woe to you! Muḥammad claims that when we die and become dust, we will be resurrected in the Hereafter, and claims that the world will come to an end; so tell me, what will the condition of the earth be then? So God (Mighty and Majestic) sent down: «When the sky is split open», «And listens to its Lord and is obligated» (2) — He says: it split open and listened to its Lord and obeyed, and that was its due. «[3] And when the earth is stretched out» (3) — like stretched-out hide — «and throws out what is within it» of living beings «and becomes empty» (4) «And listens to its Lord and is obligated» (5)
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A: «ṭarafayhā»; in F: «ṭarafāhā». [.....]
2. From F; and in A: «one of them named ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Aswad, and the other named al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd al-Aswad».
3. Verses 3, 4, 5 are missing from A. The sūra contains errors in A, and its photographic reproduction is also shaky in (A); I have relied, in editing it, on F (Fayḍ Allāh), Ḥ (Ḥamīdiyya), M (Amāna), and L (Köprülü).

records.text_en: He says: it listened to its Lord and obeyed, and that was its due. Then He said: «O mankind» — meaning by «mankind» al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd al-Asad — «indeed you are laboring toward your Lord with [great] exertion» — you are striving toward your Lord with striving — «and you will meet Him» (6) with your deed. Then He said: «Then as for he who is given his record in his right hand» (7) — and he is ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Asad, whose kunya is Abū Salama — «he will be judged with an easy account» (8) — He says: with an ease, in that God «will not alter [1]» his good deeds and will not expose him. That is because when God (Mighty and Majestic) gathers the creatures on the Day of Resurrection, they surge into one another for the span of three hundred years, until, when the Lord (Mighty and Majestic) is established upon His Kursī to reckon His creation, the Lord (Blessed and Exalted) comes with the angels, rank upon rank, and they look at Paradise «and at the Fire [2]», and «the Fire is brought [3]» from a distance of five hundred years' journey; upon it are ninety thousand reins, and on every rein seventy thousand angels, holding on, restraining it from the creatures. The length of the neck of one of them is a year's journey, and its thickness a year's journey; between the shoulders of one of them is a journey of fifty years; their faces are like embers and their eyes like lightning; when one of them speaks, fire scatters from his mouth; in the hand of each one of them is a mace on which are three hundred and sixty heads like mountains, yet it is lighter in his hand than a feather. They come with it and drive it until it is set up at the left of the Throne; and Paradise is brought, escorted as a bride is escorted to her husband, until it is set up at the right of the Throne. Then when the creatures behold the Fire and what God has prepared for its people, and look at their Lord, they fall silent, and their voices are cut off at that moment, so no
records.foot_note_en:
1. Thus in F; the meaning is «will not let go to waste».
2. Thus in F and Ḥ; the better would be: «fa-yanṭaliqūna ilā al-nār» («so they go off to the Fire»).
3. In F: «until they come with it».

records.text_en: one of them speaks, out of «dread [1]» of God and His majesty and what they see of wonders from the angels, and the bearers of the Throne, and the people of the heavens, and Hell and its keepers; so their voices are cut off at that moment, «and their joints tremble [2]». And when God knows what has befallen His friends of fear, and the hearts have reached the throats, a caller stands at the right of the Throne and calls: «O My servants, no fear is upon you this Day, nor will you grieve [3]». At that, humans and jinn all raise their heads, the believers and the disbelievers, because they are all His servants. Then he calls a second time: «Those who believed in Our verses and were Muslims [4]»; so the believers raise their heads, and the people of all the other religions lower their heads, and the people are silent for forty years; that is His saying: «This is a Day they will not speak, nor will they be permitted to make an excuse [5]». And His saying: «…they will not speak, except for him whom the Most Merciful permits and who says what is right [6]» — and he says: lā ilāha illā Allāh; that is what is right; and His saying: «…and voices will be humbled before the Most Merciful, so you will not hear except a murmur [7]». So God does not answer them nor speak to them, nor do they speak, for the span of forty years; after that He says to one of the angels, who is Gabriel (peace be upon him): Call the messengers, and begin «with the Ummī [8]». He said: So the angel stands and calls at that: Where is «the Ummī Prophet»? [9] So we say [sic]
records.foot_note_en:
1. Farq: fear; the meaning is «out of fear of God».
2. In F: «wa-tarʿad».
3. Sūrat al-Zukhruf: 68.
4. Sūrat al-Zukhruf: 69.
5. Sūrat al-Mursalāt: 35–46.
6. Sūrat al-Naba': 38.
7. Sūrat Ṭā Hā: 108.
8. In F: «bi-l-ʿarabī» («with the Arab»); in Ḥ: «bi-l-ummī».
9. In F: «the prophets»; in Ḥ: «the Ummī Prophet». [.....]

records.text_en: [sic: the prophets] at that: All of us are prophets and ummīs, so it is somewhere in between. Then it is said: The Arab, Ummī, Ḥaramī Prophet! So the Messenger of God ﷺ stands at that and raises his voice in supplication, and says: How many a sin have you committed and forgotten, which God has counted! Lord, do not disgrace my community. He said: He keeps drawing near to God (Exalted) until he stands before Him, the nearest of His creation to Him; he praises God and extols Him, and mentions of praise and thanks to God (Exalted) so much that the angels and the creatures marvel at him. Then God (Mighty and Majestic) says: I am «pleased [1]» with you, O Muḥammad; go and call your community. So he calls, and the first of his community he calls is ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Aswad, «Abū Salama [2]». He keeps drawing near, and God (Mighty and Majestic) brings him close to Him and reckons with him an easy reckoning — and the easy is that He does not take him to task for the sin he committed, and God (Mighty and Majestic) is not angry with him; so He places his evil deeds inside his record, and his good deeds on the outside of his record. Then a crown of gold is placed on his head, bearing ninety thousand locks, each lock a pearl worth the wealth of the East and the West, and he is clothed in seventy garments of brocade and silk, the one next to his body being white silk; that is His saying: «…and their clothing therein is silk [3]»; and he is adorned with «three [4]» bracelets: a bracelet of silver, a bracelet of gold, and a bracelet of pearl; and a wreath is placed on him, crowned with pearls and rubies, and it gleams in his face from the light of that. Then he returns to his brothers among the believers, and they look at him as he is «coming [5]»
records.foot_note_en:
1. In F: «māḍaytu» [sic]; in Ḥ: «raḍītu».
2. In A and F: «Abū Salama» (nominative form).
3. Sūrat al-Ḥajj: 23.
4. In A and F: «bi-thalātha» (the masculine form).
5. In A: «jāʾī»; in F: «jāʾa».

records.text_en: from God; and the angels, «the people [1]» and the jinn say: By God, God has honored this one! God has given this one! They look at his book, and behold, his evil deeds are inside the record and his good deeds are on the outside of his book. At that the angels say: This son of Adam never committed a sin at all! By God, this servant feared God, so it is fitting that such a servant be honored — and they do not perceive that his evil deeds are inside his book; and that is for whomever God (Exalted) wishes to honor and not disgrace. He said: Then he comes to his brothers among the Muslims, and they do not recognize him. He says: Do you recognize me? They all say: No, by God. He says: I only departed a moment ago, and you have forgotten me! He says: I am Abū Salama; rejoice at the like of this, O company of brothers; my Lord reckoned with me an easy reckoning and honored me. That is His saying: «he will be judged with an easy account» «And return to his people» — He says: to his folk — «in happiness» (9). Then he is given his book in his right hand «…and says: Here, read my record! Indeed, I was certain that I would meet my account [2]», to the end of the story. Then a caller calls «al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd al-Asad [3]», the brother [4] of ʿAbd Allāh the believer; and the wretch wants to approach, but they rebuke him, and his chest is split open until his heart comes out from behind his back, from between his shoulders, «and he is given [5]» his book; and every good deed he did in his lifetime is placed inside his record, because he did not believe in faith, and his evil deeds are placed on the outside of his record; and he is veiled from God (Mighty and Majestic) and does not see Him; but a caller calls from beside the Throne, mentioning his evil deeds, and each time his evil deeds are mentioned
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A and F: «al-nās». I say: He (Exalted) said: «from among jinn and mankind» (Sūrat al-Nās: 6).
2. Sūrat al-Ḥāqqa: 19–20.
3. In A: «bi-l-Aswad ibn ʿAbd al-Aswad»; in F: «bi-l-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Asad».
4. In A: «akhū»; in F: «akhī».
5. In A: «fa-yuʿṭīhi».

records.text_en: he says: I know this one, may God curse him! Then the curse comes from God (Mighty and Majestic) until it falls upon him, and he is smeared with the curse, so that his body becomes a month's journey in extent and, in length, a journey of three days and their nights; his head is like al-Aqraʿ — a huge mountain in Syria — his fangs like Uḥud, and his eye-sockets like Mount [234b] Ḥirāʾ, which is in Mecca; his nostrils are like «al-Wawqayn [1]», which are two mountains; his hair in abundance is like a thicket, in length like reeds, in thickness like spears; «a crown of fire is placed [2]» on his head, and he is clothed in a robe of molten copper, and hung with «a stone [3]» of sulphur like a mountain «in which fire blazes [4]»; his hands are shackled to his neck, and his face is blackened, blacker than a grave on a dark night, and his eyes turn blue. Then he returns to his brothers; and the first thing they see of him, the creatures are terrified by him, so that «they hold [5]» their noses from the severity of his stench. They say: God has humiliated this servant! God has disgraced this servant! They look at his book, and behold, his evil deeds are manifest and he has not a single good deed. They say: Did this servant have no need of God (Mighty and Majestic), «nor did he fear Him [6]» for a day or an hour ever? So it is fitting «for this [7]» servant that God «disgraced him [8]» and tormented him, «and all the angels curse him [9]». «And when he returns to the standing-place, his companions do not recognize him [10],
records.foot_note_en:
1. Al-Wariqayn: the dual of «wariq» (or «waraq»), the name of a mountain. In A: «like al-Wariqān, which are two mountains», and it contains a grammatical error, for «al-Wariqayn» is a dual, a genitive annexed term after the prefixed preposition «bi-».
2. In A: «fa-yūḍaʿu».
3. In A: «ḥajar».
4. In A: «tashʿal».  [.....]
5. In A: «yumsikūna».
6. In A: «lā ḥāja»; in F: «wa-lā khāfahu».
7. In A: «hādhā»; in F: «li-hādhā».
8. In A: «akhzāhu»; in F: «jazāʾ».
9. «And all the angels curse him»: from F; it is not in A.
10. «And when he returns to the standing-place, his companions do not recognize him»: from F; it is not in A.

records.text_en: and he says: Do you not recognize me? They say: No, by God. He says: I am al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd «al-Asad [1]». Then he cries out at the top of his voice, saying: «…Oh, I wish I had not been given my record, and had not known what my account is. Oh, I wish it had been the end [death]. My wealth has not availed me [2]». He says: I wish it had been death, that I might die and be at rest from this affliction; my argument today has perished from me; then he says: Woe! So his brother brings glad tidings to the believers, and this one brings tidings to the disbelievers. That is His saying (Exalted): «But as for he who is given his record behind his back» (10) «He will cry out for destruction» (11) «And will burn in a Blaze» (12) — He says: he cries out for woe and enters the Fire. He says: «Indeed, he used to be among his people in joy» (13) — He says: among his people honored; He said: so God (Mighty and Majestic) humiliates him on the Day of Resurrection. He said: «Indeed, he thought that he would never return» (14) — He says: that he would never be resurrected. God (Exalted) says: «Yes! «Indeed [3]» his Lord» — He says: the One who created him — «was ever of him Seeing» (15) — that He is a witness to his deed. Then the Lord (Mighty and Majestic) swore, saying: «So I swear by the twilight glow» (16) — and the twilight glow is the light that remains after the setting of the sun until it disappears. He said: «And by the night and what it envelops» (17) — He says: «what it drives [4]» of darkness — «And by the moon when it becomes full» (18) — on the nights of «the thirteenth, the fourteenth, and the fifteenth [5]», which are the white nights; in the month it is full for three nights, during which its light is intense, and it is gathered [full] from «the thirteenth [6]». So God swore
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A: «al-Aswad»; in F: «al-Asad».
2. Sūrat al-Ḥāqqa: 25–28.
3. In A: «annahu».
4. In A and F: «sāqa».
5. In A: «laylat thalātha ʿashar, wa-arbaʿa ʿashar, wa-khamsa ʿashar» (with different gender forms of the numerals).
6. In A and F: «thalātha ʿashar» (with a different gender form of the numeral).

records.text_en: (Mighty and Majestic) by the twilight glow, and the night and what it envelops, and the moon when it becomes full: «You will surely embark» — this servant — «upon stage after stage» (19) — He says: state after state; He says: created from a sperm-drop, then the sperm-drop became a clinging clot, then the clot became a lump, then it became a dead human in the womb of his mother, until the spirit was breathed into him, and then he became a living human; then God (Exalted) brought him out of his mother's womb, and he was an infant; then he reaches his full strength, then he grows old and aged, then he dies and stays in his grave [235a] until he becomes dust; then God (Mighty and Majestic) raises him after that on the Day of Resurrection. He said: «So what is [the matter] with them that they do not believe» (20) — in the resurrection — «and they were previously [as I have described] [1]» — «And when the Qur'an is recited to them, they do not prostrate» (21) — that is because the Messenger of God ﷺ recited one day «…and prostrate and draw near [2]», and he prostrated, and the believers prostrated with him; and Quraysh would clap above their heads and whistle — and the one who whistled was a close relative of the Messenger of God ﷺ — that is His saying: «And their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping [3]». So when the Messenger of God ﷺ prostrated, they did not prostrate, but mocked him; and when he recited, they harmed him with whistling and clapping. So God (Mighty and Majestic) sent down: «So what is [the matter] with them that they do not believe? And when the Qur'an is recited to them, they do not prostrate?» Then He said: «But those who disbelieve» — He says: but those who disbelieved — «deny» (22). «And God is most knowing of what they keep within themselves» (23) — He says: of what they gather upon themselves of sin and wickedness. «So give them tidings, O Muḥammad, of a painful punishment» (24) — He says: a painful punishment for all the people of Mecca; then He made an exception, on account of a knowledge that had already preceded, saying: «Except those who believe and do righteous deeds; for them is a reward uninterrupted» (25).
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A: «and they were before this which I described»; the adopted reading is from F.
2. Sūrat al-ʿAlaq: 35 [sic; the verse is Sūrat al-ʿAlaq 96:19]. [.....]
3. Sūrat al-Anfāl: 35.

records.text_en: Sūrat al-Burūj (The Constellations)

[Sūrat al-Burūj (85): verses 1 to 22] In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. By the sky containing the great stars (1) And [by] the promised Day (2) And [by] a witness and what is witnessed (3) Destroyed were the companions of the trench (4) [Containing] the fire full of fuel (5) When they were sitting by it (6) And they, to what they were doing against the believers, were witnesses (7) And they resented them not except that they believed in God, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy (8) To whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And God is, over all things, Witness (9) Indeed, those who persecuted the believing men and believing women and then did not repent will have the punishment of Hell, and they will have the punishment of the Burning (10) Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds will have gardens beneath which rivers flow. That is the great attainment (11) Indeed, the assault of your Lord is severe (12) Indeed, it is He who originates and repeats (13) And He is the Forgiving, the Affectionate (14) Owner of the Throne, the Glorious (15) Doer of what He intends (16) Has there reached you the story of the soldiers (17) Of Pharaoh and Thamūd? (18) But those who disbelieve are in denial (19) And God encompasses them from behind (20) But it is a glorious Qur'an (21) In a Preserved Slate (22)
[Sūrat al-Burūj [1]] Sūrat al-Burūj is Meccan; its number is «twenty-two» [2] verses, according to the Kufan count [3].
records.foot_note_en:
1. The main purpose of the sūra: the oath concerning the companions of the trench; the perfection of God's dominion; the explanation of the reward of the believers and the punishment of the disbelievers, and what God has prepared for the obedient and the disobedient; and the allusion to the destruction of Pharaoh and Thamūd.
2. In A: «ithnān» («two»).
3. In the muṣḥaf: (85) Sūrat al-Burūj, Meccan, its verses 22; revealed after Sūrat al-Shams.

records.text_en: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. His saying: «By the sky containing the great stars (burūj)» (1) — He says: and the sky possessing the stars; its parallel is in «Blessed is He who placed in the sky constellations [1]» — He says: He placed in the sky stars, «and placed therein a lamp» — which is the sun — «and a luminous moon [2]». And His saying (Exalted): «And [by] the promised Day» (2) — He says: it is the Day of Resurrection, on which God (Mighty and Majestic) promised His friends Paradise and His enemies the Fire; that is His saying: «And the promised Day [3]». «And [by] a witness and what is witnessed» (3) — He says: the Day of Sacrifice, «and the Day of Fast-Breaking [4]», and the day of Friday; this is an oath; «Indeed, the assault of your Lord is severe [5]». His saying: «Destroyed were the companions of the trench» (4) — that is because Yūsuf ibn «Dhī [6]» Nuwās, of the people of Najrān, had dug «a trench [7]» and kindled a fire in it; whoever of them spoke of monotheism he burned in the fire; and that was because eighty men and nine women of his people had believed, «and so [8]» he ordered them to renounce Islam, but they refused; so he informed them that he would torment them with fire, and they accepted
records.foot_note_en:
1. Thus in A and F; the more fitting would be: «its parallel is in Sūrat Tabāraka (al-Furqān): «Blessed is He who placed in the sky constellations»».
2. Sūrat al-Furqān: 61.
3. In A: (His saying: «and the day and the promised»); and in F: (that is His saying: «The promised Day»).
4. «Al-Fiṭr»: missing from A; it is from F.
5. Sūrat al-Burūj: 12.
6. In A and F: «Dhā».
7. In A: «jarfan» («a bank»); and in F: «khaddan» («a trench»).
8. In A: «annahu»; in F: «annahum».

records.text_en: to God's command (Mighty and Majestic), so he burned them all. He kept casting them one after another into the fire until a woman passed with a small nursing child of hers; when the woman looked at her child, she felt compassion for him and turned back, so «they offered [1]» her that she disbelieve, but she refused; they beat her until she returned; she kept turning back one time and feeling compassion another time, until the child spoke and said to her: O Mother [235b], before you is a fire that will never be extinguished! When she heard the child's words, «she presented herself [2]» until she threw herself into the fire. So God (Mighty and Majestic) placed their spirits in Paradise, and God (Blessed and Exalted) revealed to His Prophet «Muḥammad [3]» ﷺ: «Destroyed were the companions of the trench» — Yūsuf ibn «Dhī [4]» Nuwās and his companions. Then He mentioned their evil deeds, saying: «[Containing] the fire full of fuel» (5) «When they were sitting by it» (6) — meaning his companions sitting on the «edge [5]» of the trench — «and they, to what they were doing against the believers, were witnesses» (7). He said: they knew that Yūsuf ibn Dhī Nuwās was tormenting «only on account of faith [6]». Then He said, wondering at the evil of their deed: «And they resented them not» — He says: and what suspicion did they see in them? «They did not torment them [7]» — «except that they believed in God, the Exalted in Might» — in His vengeance — «the Praiseworthy [8]» (8) «To whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth [9]» «And God is over all things» — of the secret and the open — «Witness» (9). Then He said: «Indeed, those who persecuted the believing men and believing women»
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A: «fa-aʿraḍū» («so they turned away»).
2. Thus in A and F; the meaning is «she came, or presented herself». [.....]
3. In A and F: «Muḥammadan» (accusative form).
4. In A and F: «Dhā».
5. In A: «shabah» [sic]; in F: «shaffa» («edge»).
6. Thus in A and F; the more fitting is «illā ʿalā al-īmān»: that is, he tormented only the believers, until they abandoned their faith.
7. Thus in A and F («mā ʿadhdhabahum»); the more fitting: «mā ʿadhdhabūhum».
8. In A and F: («al-Ḥamīd» in the heavens).
9. «To whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth»: missing from A and F.

records.text_en: its parallel is in the sūra «By the scattering winds [1]», where He says: «The Day when they will be tried upon the Fire [2]» — meaning burned. Then He said: «and then did not repent» — of that — «will have the punishment of Hell, and they will have the punishment of the Burning» (10). Then He said: «Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds» — and testify that there is no god but God, for that is «the righteous deeds» — its parallel is when God (Mighty and Majestic) said: «…To Him ascends good speech [3]…» — which is: al-ḥamdu li-llāh, subḥān Allāh, lā ilāha illā Allāh, and Allāhu akbar; He says: all of that ascends to Him by the testimony that there is no god but God, and were it not for this, no deed of the son of Adam would ever rise. Then He said: «will have gardens beneath which rivers flow» — He says: orchards beneath which rivers flow, and they are springs — «abiding therein» for as long as Paradise lasts; they are everlasting forever. Then He said: «That is the great attainment» (11) — He says: this is the great deliverance; He says: whoever is removed from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has been delivered with a great deliverance. Then He returned to His oath which He had sworn at the beginning of the sūra, saying: «Indeed, the assault of your Lord is severe» (12) — He says: the punishment of your Lord is severe; He says: when He is angry He assaults, and when He assaults He destroys. Then the Lord (Mighty and Majestic) magnified Himself, saying: «Indeed, it is He who originates and repeats» (13) — He says: He began the creation of the soul from a dead sperm-drop and gave it life; then He will repeat it on the Day of Resurrection from that dust. Then He said: «And He is the Forgiving» — of the grave sins, for whoever repents of them — «the Affectionate» (14) — He says: the Appreciative of a small righteous deed when they please Him; He says: I appreciate the little deed, so that I «multiply it [4]» for the one «tenfold [5]» and upward. Then the Lord (Blessed and Exalted) magnified Himself, saying: «Owner of the Throne» — for God (Mighty and Majestic) created no creation greater than the Throne, because the heavens «and the earth [6]» «are lost [7]» beneath the Throne [236a]
records.foot_note_en:
1. Sūrat al-Dhāriyāt: 1.
2. Al-Dhāriyāt: 13.
3. Sūrat Fāṭir: 10.
4. In A and F: «uḍʿifuhu».
5. Thus in A and F («ʿashara»); the more fitting is «ʿasharan»; perhaps he had in mind the sense of «the good deed is ten».
6. From F; it is not in A.
7. In A: «qad ghāba» (dual masculine); in F: «qad ghābatā» (dual feminine). [.....]

records.text_en: like a ring in an open desert. Then He said: «the Glorious» (15) — the Bountiful, the Generous — «Doer of what He intends» (16) — He says: He intends nothing but He does it; He says: the servant fears his master's doing what he wills, and the master fears his commander who is over him, and the commander fears the king, and the king fears God (Mighty and Majestic); and God (Mighty and Majestic) does not fear anyone's doing [1]. That is His saying (Exalted): «Doer of what He intends». «Has» — meaning «there has» — «reached you the story of the soldiers» (17) in the Qur'an — «Pharaoh and Thamūd» (18) — you have known what God (Mighty and Majestic) did to the people of Pharaoh, when they set out in pursuit of Moses (peace be upon him) and the Children of Israel; and they were one million five hundred thousand; so God (Exalted) drove them, by their appointed terms, to the sea, and God drowned them all. So who is it who comes to dispute with Me about them? He said: «and Thamūd» — and they are the people of Ṣāliḥ, when they hamstrung the she-camel and denied Ṣāliḥ, «and then [2]» enjoyed themselves in their abode for three days; and the punishment came upon them on Saturday in the early morning, when the sun had risen: «…so their Lord crushed [3] them» «(for their sin [4])» — and Gabriel (peace be upon him) is the one who crushed [them], because he cried out one cry, and their houses fell upon them and leveled them; He says: He leveled the houses over their graves; for when they were certain of destruction they set about digging graves in their dwellings and embalmed themselves with myrrh and aloes; He said: «and leveled it [5]» — He says: it was leveled over their graves. He said: has anyone come to dispute with Me about them? That is His saying: «And He does not fear its consequence [6]». He said: So beware, O people of Mecca, for I am the Glorious, the Truth, above whom there is no one; then
records.foot_note_en:
1. Thus in A and F; the meaning is: «from doing what He wills».
2. «Thumma» («and then»): an addition required by the context.
3. That is: the messenger of their Lord.
4. «(For their sin)»: missing from A and F.
5. Sūrat al-Shams: 14.
6. Sūrat al-Shams: 15.

records.text_en: He resumed, saying: «But those who disbelieve are in denial» (19) — He says: but, O Muḥammad, those who disbelieve do not believe. When the Messenger of God ﷺ said that and recited it to them, a man from among his companions asked him about the knowledge of God (Mighty and Majestic) regarding His servants: Is it «something [1]» that occurred to Him after He created them, or was it before they were created? So God (Mighty and Majestic) sent down: «And God encompasses them from behind [2]» (20) «But it» — meaning rather it — «is a glorious Qur'an» (21) — He says: it is a glorious Qur'an, «He says: it is a glorious book [3]» — «in a Preserved Slate» (22) — before they were created; and God (Mighty and Majestic) has finished with the knowledge of His servants, and knew what they would do before He created them, and did not compel them to disobedience.
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A: «sāʾiran»; in F: «shayʾ»; the more fitting would be: «hal huwa shayʾ» («is it something»).
2. Verse (20) is missing from A and F, together with its commentary; in al-Jalālayn: («muḥīṭ»: there is no protector for them from Him); and in al-Qurṭubī: («muḥīṭ»: He does not miss them, just as the encompassed does not escape the encompasser).
3. «He says: it is a glorious book»: from F; and in A: «He says: it was firmly established (muḥkam)»; I say it is a corruption.

records.text_en: Sūrat al-Ṭāriq (The Night-Comer)

[Sūrat al-Ṭāriq (86): verses 1 to 17] In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. By the sky and the night-comer (1) And what can make you know what the night-comer is? (2) It is the piercing star (3) There is no soul but that over it is a protector (4) So let man observe from what he was created (5) He was created from a fluid, ejected (6) Emerging from between the backbone and the ribs (7) Indeed, He is able to return him [to life] (8) On the Day when secrets are put to trial (9) Then he will have no power and no helper (10) By the sky containing the return (11) And [by] the earth containing the split (12) Indeed, it is a decisive word (13) And it is not amusement (14) Indeed, they are planning a plan (15) But I am planning a plan (16) So allow time for the disbelievers; leave them awhile (17)
[Sūrat al-Ṭāriq [1]] Sūrat al-Ṭāriq is Meccan; its number is «seventeen» [2] verses, according to the Kufan count [3].
records.foot_note_en:
1. The purpose of the sūra: the oath concerning the preservation of the states of man; the report on his state at the beginning and the end; the disclosure of secrets on the Day of Recompense; the oath that the words of the Qur'an are weighty, not jest, without any doubt; and the command to give the disbelievers respite, in His saying: « …. leave them awhile» (Sūrat al-Ṭāriq: 17).
2. In A: «nineteen».
3. In the muṣḥaf: (86) Sūrat al-Ṭāriq, Meccan, its verses 17; revealed after Sūrat al-Balad. Tafsīr Muqātil ibn Sulaymān, vol. 4 – part 42

records.text_en: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. «By the sky and the night-comer» (1) «And what can make you know», O Muḥammad, «what the night-comer is?» (2) — explain it for him!
