So He said: «It is the piercing star» (3) — meaning the shining one. «There is no soul but that over it is a protector» (4) — that is because God (Mighty and Majestic) [236b] created the stars as three [kinds of] «stars [1]»: stars by which one is guided, stars as missiles against the devils, and stars as lamps of the earth; and God (Mighty and Majestic) swore by them, saying: «There is no soul» — no soul — «but that [2] over it is a protector» from among the angels, who write down its good deeds and its evil deeds. He said: so if this human being «does not [3]» believe in the resurrection, «let man observe from what he was created» (5). He said: «He was created from a fluid, ejected» (6). Then He explained the 'ejected fluid', saying: he was created from the fluid of the man and the woman, «and [it] clung [4]» one part to another, and he was created from it; «that fluid emerges from between the backbone and the ribs» (7) — He says: from between the backbone of the man and the ribs of the woman, and the tarāʾib is the place of the necklace; as for the man's fluid, it is white and thick, from which come the sinews and the bone, «and as for [5]» the woman's fluid, it is yellow and thin, from which come the flesh, the blood and the hair. «Indeed, He» — the Lord (Blessed and Exalted) who created him from an ejected fluid — «is able to return him [6]» (8) — able to resurrect him on the Day of Resurrection. «On the Day when secrets are put to trial»
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A: «nujūman»; in F: «najm»; and that is repeated for the other two.
2. In A and F: «illā»; and in the verse: «lammā».
3. «Lā»: missing from A; it is from F. [.....]
4. In A and F: «iltazaqa».
5. «Wa-ammā»: missing from A and F.
6. «ʿAlā rajʿihi laqādir»: missing from A and F.

records.text_en: (9) — the Day on which the secrets are tested: every secret deed of sin that the son of Adam did, which no one knew of except God — [as well as secret acts] of fasting, prayer, ritual washing after sexual impurity, and «al-riyy» in secret [as printed; possibly «al-riyāʾ», ostentation, or quenching one's thirst] — so He informs [of it], and its doer is disgraced on that Day. «Then he will have no power» — by which to defend himself against God with his power — «and no» — for him — «helper» (10) to help him against God (Exalted). Then God (Exalted) swore, saying: «By the sky containing the return» (11) — containing the rain — «And [by] the earth containing the split» (12) — with plants. «Indeed, it is a decisive word» (13) — He says: what I have described in this sūra is a decisive word; He says: it is the word of truth. Then He said: «And it is not amusement» (14) — He says: and it is not play. Then the speech broke off. As for His saying: «Indeed, they are planning a plan» (15) «But I am planning a plan» (16) «So allow time for the disbelievers; leave them awhile» (17) — when they saw that the Prophet ﷺ had made faith manifest, and ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (may God be pleased with him) believed — when ʿUmar believed, some of them said to others: We see the affair of Muḥammad only increasing day by day, while we are in decline, without doubt; for by God, he outnumbers our gathering and our group, and he grows many while we become few, without doubt; only that he will overcome us and drive us out of our land. But rise with us, so that we may take counsel regarding him. So they entered the Dār al-Nadwa; among them were ʿUtba ibn Rabīʿa, Abū Jahl ibn Hishām, al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, Abū al-Bakhtarī ibn Hishām, and ʿAmr ibn ʿUmayr ibn Masʿūd al-Thaqafī. When they entered, Iblīs entered with them in the form of an old man; they looked at him and said: O Shaykh, who let you in among us? And who are you? You know that we have entered here on a matter we do not want anyone to know of. Iblīs said: By God, I am not from the land of Tihāma; I am a man of al-Azd — and it is said, of Najd — who came from Yemen, and I am headed for Iraq in pursuit of a need; but I saw that your faces are handsome and your scent is pleasant, so I wished to rest and to listen to your conversations [237a]. They said to one another: There is no harm to us from him; by God, he is not from the land of Tihāma. They said:

O Shaykh, close the door and sit down. Abū Jahl ibn Hishām said: What do you say about this man who has opposed our religion and reviled our gods and calls to a religion other than ours, and whose affair only grows in number while we are few? We ought to devise a scheme. Then he said: O ʿAmr ibn ʿUmayr, what do you say of him? ʿAmr said: My opinion is that we mount him behind us on a camel, bind his bonds tight, and expel him from the Sanctuary, so that his evil falls upon others. Iblīs said at that: A bad opinion you have seen, O Shaykh! You go to a man who has committed among you what he has committed — a grave matter — and you expel him! There is no doubt that he will go and gather armies and drive you out of your land. They said: What do you say, Abū al-Bakhtarī? He said: By God, my opinion about him is firm. They said: What is it? He said: We put him in a house and shut its door on him, leaving an opening just big enough for him to take «from it [1]» his food and drink, and we wait for him until he dies. «Iblīs said [2]» at that: By God, a bad opinion you have seen, O Shaykh! You go to a man who is your enemy and «you rear him [3]»; there is no doubt that his people will become angry for his sake and fight you until they take him out of your hands; what have you to do with evil? They said: By God, he spoke truly. What do you say, Abū Jahl? He said: Go to every clan of Quraysh and choose from them men, and give them swords, and they all walk
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A and F: «minhu», meaning from what is left [the opening]; the more fitting: «minhā».
2. From the preceding «Iblīs said» up to this one is missing from F; it is from A.
3. That is: you busy yourselves with feeding him and rearing him.

records.text_en: all together as a group and strike him until they kill him, «so that Banū Hāshim are not able [1]» «to be hostile to [2]» all of Quraysh, and you pay his blood-money. Iblīs said: By God, the young man spoke truly. So they went out upon that statement, content with killing him. His uncle Abū Ṭālib, whose name was ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, heard it, but did not tell Muḥammad, lest he be alarmed by the killing and flee, which would bring disgrace upon them. So God (Mighty and Majestic) sent down: «Or have they planned a matter? Then indeed, We are planners [3]» — He says: or have they agreed upon a matter, to kill Muḥammad ﷺ? Then We are agreed upon a matter, to kill them at Badr. And He said: «Or do they intend a plot? But those who disbelieve — they are the ones plotted against [4]». And He said: «Indeed, they are planning a plan, and I am planning a plan; so allow time for the disbelievers; leave them awhile». He said: Abū Ṭālib heard what he heard; he said: O son of my brother, what is this murmuring? He said: Do we not know, O uncle, what Quraysh intended? He said: I have heard what you have heard, O son of my brother. He said: Yes. He said: And who told you of that? He said: My Lord. He said: By God, O son of my brother, your Lord is surely your Guardian; so proceed with what you have been commanded, O son of my brother; there is no disgrace upon you [5].
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A: «fa-lā yastaṭīʿūna» («so they are not able»).
2. In A: «yuʿādū».
3. Sūrat al-Zukhruf: 79.
4. Sūrat al-Ṭūr: 42.
5. The commentary on the sūra ends in A; in F there is an addition: «No, by God, Quraysh with all their numbers will not reach you until I am laid in the dust, buried.»

records.text_en: Sūrat al-Aʿlā (The Most High)

[Sūrat al-Aʿlā (87): verses 1 to 19] In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Exalt the name of your Lord, the Most High (1) Who created and proportioned (2) And who destined and guided (3) And who brought out the pasture (4) And made it black stubble (5) We will make you recite, and you will not forget (6) Except what God wills. Indeed, He knows what is declared and what is hidden (7) And We will ease you toward ease (8) So remind, if the reminder should benefit (9) He who fears [God] will be reminded (10) But the wretched one will avoid it (11) [He] who will burn in the greatest Fire (12) Then he will neither die therein nor live (13) He has certainly succeeded who purifies himself (14) And mentions the name of his Lord and prays (15) But you prefer the worldly life (16) While the Hereafter is better and more enduring (17) Indeed, this is in the former scriptures (18) The scriptures of Abraham and Moses (19)
[Sūrat al-Aʿlā [1]] Sūrat al-Aʿlā is Meccan; its number is «nineteen» [2] verses, according to the Kufan count [3].
records.foot_note_en:
1. The purpose of the sūra: the explanation of the loftiness of the Essence and the Attributes; the mention of creation; the praise of fruits and plants; security from the abrogation of verses; the explanation of the ease of acts of obedience; the humiliation of disbelief in the depths of the abysses; the exhortation to prayer and almsgiving; and the explanation of the loftiness of the Hereafter and its permanence, in His saying: «While the Hereafter is better and more enduring» (Sūrat al-Aʿlā: 17).
2. In A: «tisʿata ʿashar»; the correct form is what I have adopted. [.....]
3. In the muṣḥaf: (87) Sūrat al-Aʿlā, Meccan, its verses 19; revealed after Sūrat al-Takwīr.

records.text_en: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. His saying: «Exalt the name of your Lord, the Most High» (1) — He (Glorified) says: declare the name of your Lord, the Most High, to be free of imperfection — He says: declare Him free of polytheism by the testimony that there is no god but God; that is His saying: «the Most High». He said: «Who created» the human being in the womb of his mother from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot, then from a lump; He said: «and proportioned» (2) — He says: He proportioned his creation. «And who destined and guided» (3) — He says: the One who destined the child in the womb of his mother for nine months, and when the time reached him, guided him to come out of his mother's womb; and also His saying: «destined and guided» means: He destined male and female and taught him how to come to her and how she comes to him. And as for His saying: «And who brought out the pasture» (4) «And made it black stubble» (5) by His making — He says: the One who brought out the herbage and the grass in winter, so you see it fresh, then He makes it, after the freshness and the greenness, into dryness [1]. His saying: «We will make you recite» the Qur'an, O Muḥammad — We gather it in your heart — «and you will not forget» (6) — you will never forget it. Then He made an exception, saying: «Except what God wills» — meaning except what God wills, so He abrogates it and brings one better than it. Then He said: «Indeed, He knows what is declared and what is hidden [2]» (7) — «He knows what is declared» of speech and deed, «and what is hidden» of both. «And We will ease you toward ease» (8) — He says: and We will exchange for you, in place of a verse, one easier than it. Then He said: «So remind», O Muḥammad — He says: remind with the testimony that there is no god but God — «if» — meaning «indeed» — «the reminder benefits» (9) — the testimony that there is no [sic: «lā an lā»] god but God, [as it benefited] those before you. He said: «He who fears [God] will be reminded
records.foot_note_en:
1. In al-Jalālayn: (ghuthāʾ): dry, crumbled; (aḥwā): black, dry.
2. «Indeed, He knows what is declared and what is hidden»: missing from A, and its commentary is taken from al-Jalālayn.

records.text_en: (10) — He says: he who fears Him will profess God's Oneness; He says: whoever fears Him, He forgives him and does not take him to task. «The wretched one will avoid it» (11) — He says: he will treat it lightly, meaning monotheism — the wretched one — he «in whom [1]» God's knowledge of wretchedness has preceded — «who will burn in the greatest Fire» (12) — and it is the Fire of Hell. He said: «Then he will neither die therein nor live» (13) — He says: he will not die in the Fire so as to find rest, nor will he live a good life, but he is in affliction «for as long as he is in the Fire [2]»: death comes to him from every place, yet he is not dead; «and he burns [3]» seven times every day, then is returned to the torment; «he has no food [4]» except from his own flesh; that is His saying: «nor any food except from ghislīn [5]»; he eats the Fire and it eats him, and he is in the Fire; his clothing is fire, upon his head is fire, on his neck is fire, and in every joint of him are seven kinds of the kinds of torment; he is not shown mercy ever, nor is he ever satisfied, nor does he ever die, nor does he ever live a good life; God is wrathful at him, the angels are wrathful, and Hell is wrathful. His saying: «He has certainly succeeded who purifies himself» (14) «And mentions the name of his Lord and prays» (15) — He says: he has succeeded who paid the zakāt, testified that there is no god but God, and prayed the five prayers. His saying: «But you prefer the worldly life» (16) — He says: but you choose the worldly life; «While the Hereafter is better and more enduring» (17); «Indeed, this is in the former scriptures» (18) — He says: the former books — «the scriptures [6]» of Abraham: the books of Abraham, «and the book of Moses» (19) — which is the Torah. As for the scriptures of Abraham, they have been raised up.
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A: «fīhim».
2. From F; and in A: «He made him remain in the Fire».
3. In A: «wa-yuḥayyih»; in F: «wa-yaḥtariq».
4. In A: «laysa lahum ṭaʿām»; and in F: «wa-lā ṭaʿām», which is the correct form.
5. Sūrat al-Ḥāqqa: 36.
6. In A: «kutub»; and in the margin of the verse: «ṣuḥuf».

records.text_en: Sūrat al-Ghāshiyah (The Overwhelming)

[Sūrat al-Ghāshiyah (88): verses 1 to 26] In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Has there reached you the report of the Overwhelming? (1) [Some] faces, that Day, will be humbled (2) Working, weary (3) Burning in an intensely hot Fire (4) Given drink from a boiling spring (5) For them there will be no food except from a bitter thorny plant (ḍarīʿ) (6) Which neither nourishes nor avails against hunger (7) [Other] faces, that Day, will be joyful (8) With their effort, satisfied (9) In an elevated Garden (10) Wherein they will hear no unsuitable speech (11) Within it is a flowing spring (12) Within it are couches raised high (13) And cups set in place (14) And cushions lined up (15) And carpets spread around (16) Then do they not look at the camels — how they were created? (17) And at the sky — how it was raised? (18) And at the mountains — how they were erected? (19) And at the earth — how it was spread out? (20) So remind, [O Muḥammad]; you are only a reminder (21) You are not over them a controller (22) However, he who turns away and disbelieves (23) Then God will punish him with the greatest punishment (24) Indeed, to Us is their return (25) Then indeed, upon Us is their account (26)
[Sūrat al-Ghāshiyah [1]] Sūrat al-Ghāshiyah is Meccan; its number is «twenty-six» [2] verses [3].
records.foot_note_en:
1. The main purpose of the sūra: the warning by the appearance of the Resurrection; the explanation of the state of those who deserve punishment; the mention of the state of those who deserve reward; the establishing of the proof for the existence of the Real [God]; the Messenger's ﷺ exhortation of the community out of compassion; and that the return is to God (Exalted) in the final outcome, in His saying (Exalted): «Then indeed, upon Us is their account» (Sūrat al-Ghāshiyah: 26).
2. In A: «sana» («a year») [sic].
3. In the muṣḥaf: (88) Sūrat al-Ghāshiyah, Meccan, its verses 26; revealed after Sūrat al-Dhāriyāt.

records.text_en: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. «Has there reached you the report of the Overwhelming?» [1] (1) — meaning: the report of the people of «the Fire [2]» has reached you, from His saying: «The Fire will scorch their faces, and they therein will be disfigured [3]»; and everything in the Qur'an of «Has there reached you», He means: it has reached you. Then He reported their state, saying: «[Some] faces, that Day, will be humbled» (2) — meaning abased — «Working, weary» (3) — meaning working in the Fire; the Fire eats him and he eats from the Fire; meaning «weary» with torment, humbled. «Burning in an intensely hot Fire» (4) «Given drink from a boiling spring» (5) — meaning from a spring whose heat has reached its limit; that is because Hell has been stoked against them from the day it was created until the day they enter it; and it is a spring that issues from the base of a mountain, its length a journey of «seventy years [4]», «its water [5]» black like the dregs of oil, murky, thick, with many maggots; «the angels [6]» give it to drink in a vessel of iron, of fire, «and he drinks it [7]»; and when the vessel is brought near his mouth, it burns his jaws, and his fangs and molars scatter; when it reaches his chest, his heart «is cooked [8]»; when it reaches his belly, it «boils [9]»
records.foot_note_en:
1. «Al-Ghāshiya»: the calamity that overwhelms people with its hardships, meaning the Day of Resurrection, or the Fire (al-Qurṭubī).
2. «The Fire»: missing from A and F; it is from L. [.....]
3. Sūrat al-Muʾminūn: 104; and in A: «overwhelms» (taghshā) in place of «scorches» (talfaḥ); I have corrected the error.
4. In A: «ninety years»; and in F and L: «seventy years».
5. «Its water»: an addition required by the context; missing from A, F and L.
6. In A and L: «the angels»; and in F: «the angel».
7. «Fa-yashrabuhu»: thus in A, F and L; the more fitting: «fa-yashrabuhu al-shaqī» («and the wretch drinks it»).
8. In A: «shajja»; in F and L: «naḍija».
9. In A, F and L: «yaghlī» («it boils», in the imperfect); the more fitting is what I have adopted.

records.text_en: as boiling water boils from the intensity of the heat, until he melts as lead melts when fire touches it; «so the wretch cries out [1]» for woe; that is His saying: «Given drink from a boiling spring». Then He informed [us] about the food of the wretched, saying: «For them there will be no food except from ḍarīʿ» (6) — and it is a tree found in Mecca, very thorny; no beast on earth approaches it because of its thorns, and no one can touch it because of the abundance of its thorns; and Quraysh call it, when it is fresh in the spring, «al-shibraq [2]»; and the camels get some of its leaves in the spring for as long as it is fresh; when it dries, the camels do not approach it; and there is no beast on earth — of the vermin and the predators and whatever harms the children of Adam — but the like of it is in the Fire, which God (Mighty and Majestic) has set upon its people; but it is of fire, for God created nothing in the Fire except from fire. Then He said: «Which neither nourishes nor avails against hunger» (7) — «for they are not fed because of hunger, but because of the torment [3]». Then He mentioned the friends from among the people of His obedience, saying: «[Other] faces, that Day, will be joyful» (8) — meaning happy; God (Mighty and Majestic) likened their faces to the faces of a people who are happy, who when they get a drink, their souls become cheerful, and the blood gathers in their faces; so the joy of the hearts and the joy of the drink combine, and he is laughing of face, «smiling [4]», good of soul. Then He said: «With their effort, satisfied» (9) — meaning God is pleased with his deed, so God (Mighty and Majestic) rewarded him for it, on account of his deed. He said: «In an elevated Garden» (10) — and He named it elevated only because Hell is lower than it, and comprises levels [darakāt], while Paradise comprises degrees [darajāt]. Then He said: ««You will not hear [5]» therein any unsuitable speech» (11) — He says: they will not hear
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A: «fa-yashrabuhu» («and he drinks it»); in F and L: «fa-yadʿū» («and he cries out»).
2. In A: «al-yasbar»; in F: «al-shibraq».
3. In A, F and L: «for they are not fed [because] of hunger, except because of the torment, that they be tormented»; and it contains errors, as you see.
4. In A: «mubtasiman» (accusative form).
5. In A: «lā yasmaʿu» («one will not hear»); and the reading of Ḥafṣ is «lā tasmaʿu» («you will not hear»).

records.text_en: one another's backbiting, nor lying, nor cursing. His saying: «Within it is a flowing spring» (12) — meaning in Paradise, because rivers flow in it; «Within it are couches raised high» (13) — woven with rods of pearl and gold, upon which are seventy mattresses, each mattress the size of a chamber of the chambers of the world; that is His saying: «couches raised high»; «And cups set in place» (14) — meaning arranged in rows; they are cups of silver, in their clarity like glass flasks, round at the «rims [1]», without handles «and without spouts [2]»; «And cushions lined up» (15) — meaning the large, great pillows, arranged in rows on the carpets (ṭanāfis), in the language of Quraysh in particular [3]. Then He said: «And carpets spread around» (16) — meaning ṭanāfis spread out one over another. God (Mighty and Majestic) reminds them of what He has made, so that His servants may take heed, and be eager for it and desire it, and beware of the Fire; for His punishment is in proportion to His authority, and His honour is in proportion to His authority. Then He mentioned His wonders, saying: «Then do they not look at the camels» — because the Arabs had not seen the elephant, and He only mentioned to them what they had seen; had He said: Do they not look at the elephants, «how they were created?» (17), they would not have marveled at them, because they had not seen them — «And at the sky — how it was raised?» (18) — above them by five hundred years' distance — «And at the mountains — how they were erected?» [4] (19) — on the earth as pegs, lest it shake with its people. Then He said: «And at the earth — how it was spread out?» (20) — meaning how it was spread out from beneath the Kaʿba, a journey of five hundred years. Then He said: «So remind», O Muḥammad, the people of Mecca — «you are only a reminder» (21) like those before you — «You are not over them a controller» (22) — He says: you are not a king over them; then the Verse of the Sword abrogated it
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A: «al-raʾs» («the head»); in F: «al-ruʾūs» («the heads»).
2. «And without spouts»: from F; it is not in A. [.....]
3. From F and L; and in A: «And cushions lined up», meaning the ṭanāfis, and that is in the language of Quraysh in particular.
4. Verse 19 together with its commentary are both missing from A, and are supplied from F.

records.text_en: in Barāʾa [1]. Then He said: «However, he who turns away» — meaning turns aside — «and disbelieves» (23) — in faith — «then God will punish him in the Hereafter [2] with the greatest punishment» (24) — and God named it 'the greatest' only because God had threatened them with killing and hunger in this world, so He said 'the greatest' because it is greater than hunger and killing; and it is the punishment of Hell. Then He said: «Indeed, to Us is their return» (25) — meaning their destination — «Then indeed, upon Us is their account» (26) — meaning their requital is easy for God.
records.foot_note_en:
1. Sūrat al-Tawba: and it is His saying (Exalted): «Then when the sacred months have passed, kill the polytheists wherever you find them, take them, besiege them, and sit in wait for them at every ambush; but if they repent and establish prayer and give zakāt, then let them go their way. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.»
2. «(Fa-yuʿadhdhibuhu) in the Hereafter»: missing from A; it is from F.

records.text_en: Sūrat al-Fajr (The Dawn)

[Sūrat al-Fajr (89): verses 1 to 30] In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. By the dawn (1) And by ten nights (2) And by the even and the odd (3) And by the night when it passes (4) Is there in that an oath [sufficient] for one of perception? (5) Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with ʿĀd (6) [With] Iram — those of the lofty pillars (7) The likes of whom had never been created in the land (8) And Thamūd, who carved out the rocks in the valley (9) And Pharaoh, owner of the stakes (10) Who transgressed in the lands (11) And increased therein the corruption (12) So your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment (13) Indeed, your Lord is in observation (14) And as for man, when his Lord tries him and [thus] honors him and favors him, he says: My Lord has honored me (15) But when He tries him and restricts his provision, he says: My Lord has humiliated me (16) No! Rather, you do not honor the orphan (17) And you do not encourage one another to feed the poor (18) And you consume inheritance, devouring [it] altogether (19) And you love wealth with immense love (20) No! When the earth is leveled, pounded and crushed (21) And your Lord arrives, and the angels, rank upon rank (22) And brought forth, that Day, is Hell — that Day man will remember, but how will the remembrance [benefit] him? (23) He will say: Oh, I wish I had put forth [good] for my life (24) So on that Day none will punish [as severely as] His punishment (25) And none will bind [as severely as] His binding (26) [To the righteous it will be said:] O reassured soul (27) Return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him] (28) And enter among My servants (29) And enter My Paradise (30)
[Sūrat al-Fajr [1]] Sūrat al-Fajr is Meccan; its number is thirty verses, according to the Kufan count [2]
records.foot_note_en:
1. The main purpose of the sūra: the honoring of the festival ('īd), of ʿArafa, and of the ten [days] of al-Muḥarram [as printed]; the allusion to the destruction of ʿĀd, Thamūd and their like; the variation in the state of man with regard to blessing, and his eagerness to amass the world and abundant wealth; the explanation of the state of the earth at the Resurrection, the coming of the angels, and man's regret on that Day over his shortcoming and disobedience; and that the return of the believer at death is to mercy, good pleasure, and the bliss of the Gardens, in His saying: «And enter My Paradise» (Sūrat al-Fajr: 30).
2. In the muṣḥaf: (89) Sūrat al-Fajr, Meccan, its verses 30; revealed after Sūrat al-Layl.

records.text_en: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. «By the dawn» (1) — meaning the morning of Jamʿ, the Day of Sacrifice [1]; «And by ten nights» (2) — they are the ten nights before al-Aḍḥā; and God (Mighty and Majestic) called them «ten nights» only because they are nine days and ten nights; «And by the even and the odd» (3) — as for the even: it is Adam and Eve (peace be upon them both); and as for the odd: it is God (Mighty and Majestic); «And by the night when it passes» (4) — meaning when it approaches, which is the night of al-Aḍḥā. So God swore by the Day of Sacrifice, and by the ten, and by Adam and Eve, and He swore by Himself; and when He had finished with these, He said: «Is there in that an oath [sufficient] for one of perception?» (5) — meaning: in that oath there is sufficiency for one of intellect, meaning one who possesses reason, so that he recognizes the greatness of this oath. Then God swore: «Indeed, your Lord is in observation [2]». And as for His saying: «Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with ʿĀd» (6) — meaning with the people of Hūd; and He called them «the people of Hūd» only because their father's name was Ibn «Samal [3]» ibn Lumlak ibn Sām ibn Nūḥ, just as the Arabs say Rabīʿa and Muḍar and Khuzāʿa and Sulaym [239a]; and likewise ʿĀd and Thamūd. Then He mentioned a tribe of the people of ʿĀd, saying: «Iram» — a tribe among their tribes, named Iram — then He said: «those of the lofty pillars» (7) — meaning those of the columns, and they are the columns of «the monks [4]» that are in the wilds and the sands; so God (Mighty and Majestic) likened their height
records.foot_note_en:
1. He interpreted the dawn as the dawn of ʿArafa, or of the Sacrifice (al-Bayḍāwī); and the meaning of «ghadāt Jamʿ» is the morning of the day following the Day of ʿArafāt, which is the Day of Sacrifice; and the Day of ʿArafāt was called «Jamʿ» because people gather on it on Mount ʿArafāt.
2. Sūrat al-Fajr: 14.
3. In A: «Samak»; and in F: «Samak»; I say: God called them the people of Hūd because Hūd was sent to them.
4. In A: «al-ruhbāniyyīn»; and in F: «al-ruhhābīn».

records.text_en: when they were standing in the wilderness to that of «a [1]» column; the height of one of them was eighteen cubits, and it is said twelve «cubits [2]» into the sky, like the greatest column that exists. He said: «The likes of whom had never been created in the land» (8) — He says: God did not create the like of the people of ʿĀd among human beings, nor the like of «Iram [3]» among the people of ʿĀd. Then He mentioned Thamūd, saying: «And Thamūd» — he is their father, and by that He named them — they are the people of Ṣāliḥ; He said: «who carved out the rocks in the valley» (9) — He says: those who hollowed out the rock «in the valley [4]»; and that is because they would set about the greatest mountain «and bore into it [5]» and make it a house, and make its door from it and its lock from it [6]; that is His saying: «And you carve out of the mountains homes, skilled [7]». Then He mentioned Pharaoh, whose name was Muṣʿab ibn Jabr — and it is said al-Walīd ibn Muṣʿab — saying: «And Pharaoh, owner of the stakes» (10) — and that is because he bound the hairdresser to four stakes, lying on her back, and then loosed upon her snakes and scorpions, and they did not cease stinging and biting her [8], entering by her «front [9]» and coming out of her mouth, until she melted as lead melts, because she had spoken of monotheism; and that was because she was combing the hair of Hayjal, the daughter of Pharaoh, when the comb fell from her hand, and she said: In the name of God, and ruin «[10]» to whoever disbelieves in God! So Pharaoh's «daughter [11]» said: And what is this God whom
records.foot_note_en:
1. «Bi-annahu» («as, that it was»): not in A.
2. In A: «ʿashara» (with a different gender form of the numeral).
3. In A: «al-Iram»; and in F: «Aram».
4. In A and F: «bi-l-wād».  [.....]
5. In A: «fa-yathqubūnahā».
6. Thus in A and F: the pronoun is repeated in the feminine, referring to the mountain (jabal).
7. Sūrat al-Shuʿarāʾ: 149.
8. In A and F there is an addition: «the scorpions».
9. In A: «fīhā» («in her»); in F: «qubulihā» («her front»).
10. In A: «raḥṣa»; in F: «khayna» [both as printed].
11. In A and F: «ibnat».

records.text_en: do you mention? She said: The God of Moses. So she went and told her father, and what happened to her happened; that is His saying: «And Pharaoh, owner of the stakes» — He says: he bound a woman to four stakes, because she knew Me. Then He combined «ʿĀd [1]», Thamūd and Pharaoh, saying: «Who transgressed in the lands» (11) — meaning those who committed acts of disobedience in them — «And increased therein the corruption» (12) — He says: they multiplied acts of disobedience therein; and when their disobedience multiplied, «so [2] your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment» (13) — meaning His vengeance, «and His vengeance was [3]» punishment. Then He returned to His first oath, saying: «Indeed, your Lord is in observation» (14) — meaning at the Ṣirāṭ [the Bridge]; and that is because over Hell are seven bridges, each bridge a journey of seventy years; on each bridge stand angels, their faces like embers and their eyes like lightning, «in their hands [4]» «the maḥāsir [5]» «and the maḥājin [6]» [hooked staffs] and the grapnels; at the first bridge they are questioned about faith; at the second they are questioned about the five prayers; at the third they are questioned about zakāt; at the fourth they are questioned about the fast of Ramaḍān; at the fifth they are questioned about the pilgrimage to the House; at the sixth they are questioned about ʿumra; and at the seventh they are questioned about people's wrongs; that is His saying: «Indeed, your Lord is in observation». And as for His saying: «And as for man [239b], when his Lord tries him and [thus] honors him and favors him, he says: My Lord has honored me» (15) — the verse was revealed about Umayya ibn Khalaf al-Jumaḥī and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Nufayl; the latter came to him, enjoining the right and forbidding the wrong, and reminding him
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A: «ʿĀd» (without the tanwīn); and in F: «ʿĀdan».
2. In A: «fa-ṣabba»; and in F: «ṣabba».
3. In A: «wa-kāna».
4. In A: «bi-awāʾilihim» («with their first ones»); and in the margin of A: «perhaps: bi-aydīhim» («in their hands»); and in F: «bi-aydīhim».
5. In A: «al-maḥāsir»; and in F: «al-maḥāsik».
6. In A: «al-maḥājir»; and in F: «al-maḥājin». Tafsīr Muqātil ibn Sulaymān, vol. 4 – part 44.

records.text_en: of that. Umayya ibn Khalaf said to him: Woe to you! Does God not say: «(That [1]) is because God is (the Protector [2]) of those who believe, and because the disbelievers have no protector [3]»? ʿAbd Allāh ibn Nufayl said: Yes. He said: Then why did He enrich me and impoverish you? He said: So did God will. Umayya said: Rather, God enriched me because of my honor with Him, and impoverished you because of your lowliness with Him. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Khaṭal said at that: It is fitting that God has «done [4]» that! So God (Exalted) sent down: «And as for man, when his Lord tries him and honors him and favors him, he says: My Lord has honored me» «But when He tries him and restricts his provision, he says: My Lord has humiliated me» (16). He says [5]: No! I did not enrich this rich man because of his honor, nor impoverish this poor man because of his lowliness with Me; rather, so I willed: to be good to this rich man in the world, and to make easy for this poor man his reckoning on the Day of Resurrection. Then He said in another sūra: «So indeed, with hardship comes ease; indeed, with hardship comes ease [6]» — He says: there is no hardship but ease comes after it, and no ease but hardship comes after it; then the speech broke off. Then He mentioned Umayya ibn Khalaf al-Jumaḥī and mentioned his evil conduct, saying: «No!» — the matter is not as Umayya ibn Khalaf said — «Rather» — meaning but — «you do not honor the orphan» (17) «And you do not encourage one another to feed the poor» (18) — because they do not hope for the Hereafter through it — «And you consume inheritance, devouring [it] altogether» (19) — meaning you eat the inheritance with ravenous eating — «And you love wealth with immense love» (20) — they gather wealth in great amounts, and it is in the language of Mālik ibn Kināna. Then He said: «No!» — they do not believe in the Hereafter, and it is a threat. And as for His saying: «When the earth is leveled, pounded and crushed» (21) — meaning when it is left [flattened] and the mountains become level with the stretched-out earth. Then He said:
records.foot_note_en:
1. «(That)»: missing from F and A. [.....]
2. In A: «(walī)»; in F: «(mawlā)».
3. Sūrat Muḥammad: 11.
4. In A: «yaqul»; and in F: «faʿala».
5. «He says» — the commentator, or Muqātil, says; «he says», that is, God says.
6. Sūrat al-Sharḥ: 5–6.

records.text_en: «And your Lord arrives, and the angels, rank upon rank» (22) — and that is because the heavens and the earth split, and the angels of each heaven descend, and the angels of each heaven stand separately; then God (Blessed and Exalted) comes, as He said: «Do they await «[1]» except that the angels come to them or your Lord comes… [2]», and as He said: «Do they await except that God comes to them in canopies of cloud, and the angels [3]…», «standing in ranks [4]». He said: «And brought forth, that Day, is Hell» — it is brought «from [5]» a distance of five hundred years, «with seventy thousand reins [6]» upon it, on each rein seventy thousand angels, hanging on to it, restraining it from the creatures, their faces like embers and their eyes like lightning; when one of them speaks, «fire scatters [7]» from his mouth; in the hand of each angel of them is a mace on which are two thousand and seventy heads like mountains, «and it is [8]» lighter «in his hand [9]» than feathers; and it has «seven [10]» heads like the heads of vipers, and their eyes are blue, «looking [11]» at the creatures out of intensity of rage, wishing to break loose upon the creatures out of the wrath of God (Mighty and Majestic); and it is brought until it is set up at the leg of the Throne. Then He said: «that Day man will remember» — meaning Umayya ibn Khalaf al-Jumaḥī, when he beholds the «ghār» [sic; probably «al-nār», the Fire] and the angels. Then He said: «but how will the remembrance [benefit] him?»
records.foot_note_en:
1. «Yanẓurūna» («await»): missing from A; it is from F.
2. Sūrat al-Anʿām: 158.
3. Sūrat al-Baqara: 210.
4. In A: «qiyām ṣufūf»; and in F: «qiyāman ṣufūfan».
5. «Min» («from»): not in A or F.
6. «ʿAlayhā sabʿūn alf zimām»: from F; it is not in A.
7. In A: «tanāthara»; and in F: «tanāthrat».
8. In A: «hiya»; and in F: «wa-hiya».
9. In A: «yadihi»; and in F: «aydīhim» («their hands»). [.....]
10. In A and F: «sabʿ» (with a different gender form of the numeral).
11. In A: [as printed]; and in F: «naẓarat tanẓur»; and I say the pronoun refers back to Hell.

records.text_en: (23) — meaning: and from where [240] will he have the remembrance in the Hereafter, when he had disbelieved in it in the world? Then He said, reporting their state and what they say in the Hereafter when they behold the Fire: «He will say: Oh, I wish I had put forth [good] for my life» (24) — in the world, for my Hereafter. God (Exalted) says: «So on that Day none will punish [as severely as] His punishment» — meaning: none will punish like the punishment of God — «anyone» (25) — meaning there is none greater than God (Exalted); His authority is in proportion to His greatness, and His punishment is like His authority. Then He said: «And none will bind [as severely as] His binding» (26) — meaning: and none will bind like the binding of God (Mighty and Majestic). His saying: «O reassured soul» (27) — meaning reassured by faith — «Return to your Lord, well-pleased» with your deed — «and pleasing [to Him]» (28) with what God (Mighty and Majestic) gave you of good and recompense — «And enter among My servants» (29) — meaning into My mercy — «And enter My Paradise» (30) — and enter, out of My mercy, into My Paradise. Its parallel is in «Ṭā-Sīn [1]» al-Naml: the saying of Sulaymān ibn Dāwūd (peace be upon them both): «…and admit me, by Your mercy, among Your righteous servants [2]». This verse was revealed about Ḥubayb ibn ʿAdī, whom the people of Mecca crucified, placing his face toward Medina; he said: O God, if I have any «good [3]» with You, turn my face toward «its qibla [4]»; so God (Mighty and Majestic) turned his face toward this qibla, without anyone turning it, «and no one was able to turn him away from it [5]».
records.foot_note_en:
1. Sūrat al-Naml: 3.
2. Sūrat al-Naml: 19.
3. In A and F: «khayran» (accusative form).
4. In A: «qiblataka» («your qibla»); and in F: «qiblatahā» («its qibla»); and the meaning is: toward the qibla of Medina.
5. From F; and in A: «and no one was able that anyone turn him away from it».

records.text_en: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Thābit narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to me, he said: al-Hudhayl narrated to us, he said: Muqātil ibn Sulaymān narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: God created the lowest heaven from «water, [ḥaraj,] restrained [1]», and the second from iron, and the third from silver, and the fourth from brass, and the fifth from gold, and the sixth from red ruby, and the seventh from light; upon it are angels of light, standing rank upon rank; that is His saying: «By those lined up in rows [2]» — and they are the people of the seventh heaven.
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A: «from a restrained wave»; and in F: «from restrained water, ḥaraj».
2. Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt: 1.

records.text_en: Sūrat al-Balad (The City)

[Sūrat al-Balad (90): verses 1 to 20] In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. I swear by this city (1) and you are a resident (ḥill) of this city (2) and by a begetter and what he begot (3) We have certainly created man in hardship (kabad) (4) Does he think that no one will ever have power over him? (5) He says: I have squandered wealth in abundance (lubad) (6) Does he think that no one has seen him? (7) Did We not make for him two eyes (8) and a tongue and two lips (9) and guide him to the two ways (najdayn) (10) But he has not attempted the steep ascent (11) And what will make you know what the steep ascent is? (12) It is the freeing of a neck (13) or feeding on a day of severe hunger (14) an orphan of near relationship (15) or a needy person in misery (16) Then he is among those who believed and enjoined one another to patience and enjoined one another to compassion (17) Those are the companions of the right (18) And those who disbelieved in Our verses — they are the companions of the left (19) Over them will be a fire closed in (20)
[Sūrat al-Balad [1]] Sūrat al-Balad is Meccan; its number is twenty verses, according to the Kufan count [2].
records.foot_note_en:
1. The main purpose of the sūra: ennobling Mecca through the ruling of the oath sworn by it; the severity of the state of the denier; the report of his secret and his public conduct; the favour upon him with various blessings; the awe of the steep ascent of the Path (al-ʿaqaba) and the explanation of salvation from it; praise of the believers, their patience in affliction, and their mercy toward one another; and the eternity of the disbelievers in the Fire, in His saying: «Over them will be a fire closed in» (Sūrat al-Balad: 20).
2. In the muṣḥaf: (90) Sūrat al-Balad, Meccan, its verses (20); revealed after Sūrat Qāf.

records.text_en: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. His saying: «I swear by this city» (1) — meaning Mecca. «and you are a resident (ḥill) of this city» (2) — meaning: I did not make it lawful for anyone before you «nor after you» [1]; I made it lawful for you only for an hour of the day. That is because God (Mighty and Majestic) did not open Mecca for anyone other than him, and did not make killing lawful in it for anyone — apart from what the Prophet ﷺ killed of Miqyas ibn Ṣubāba al-Kinānī and others when he conquered Mecca. God (Blessed and Exalted) said: «and by a begetter and what he begot» (3) — meaning Adam and his offspring (peace be upon him) until the Hour arises. So God (Mighty and Majestic) swore by Mecca and by Adam and his offspring. [240b] «We have certainly created man in hardship» (4) — upright, standing; that is because God (Blessed and Exalted) created everything on four legs, except the son of Adam, who walks on two legs. This verse was revealed about al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAmr ibn Nawfal ibn ʿAbd Manāf al-Qurashī. That is because he committed a sin while he was in Medina, so he came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and said: What is its expiation? The Messenger of God ﷺ said: Go and free a slave, or feed sixty poor persons. He said: Is there nothing other than this? The Messenger of God ﷺ said: It is what I have told you. So he returned from the Messenger of God ﷺ, worried and grieved, until he «came» [2] to his companions and said: By God, I know only that if I enter the religion of
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A: «wa-lā baʿdaka» (without «min»).
2. «Atā» («came»): from F; it is not in A.

records.text_en: Muḥammad, my wealth will be «in» [1] diminution through expiations and spending in the way of «God» [2]; Muḥammad thinks only that we found this wealth on the road! I have spent wealth in abundance (lubad) — meaning much wealth. So God (Mighty and Majestic) revealed: «We have certainly created man in hardship». «Does he think that no one will ever have power over him?» (5) — by «no one» (aḥad) He means God (Mighty and Majestic), meaning Himself: does this man think that God (Mighty and Majestic) will not be able to take away his wealth, even if he has secured it [3]? «He says: I have squandered wealth in abundance» [4] (6). Then God (Exalted) said — while He promises him good [text: yaʿiduhu al-khayr — reading uncertain]: «Does he think that no one has seen him?» (7) — or does this man think that God (Exalted) does not see what he spends and does not count it [5]? Whereas He will replace it for him [6]. Then He mentioned the blessings, saying: «Did We not make for him two eyes» (8) «and a tongue and two lips» (9) «and guide him to the two ways» (10) — He says: We made clear to him the path of good and of evil. Then He turned him toward the expiation, saying: «But he has not attempted the steep ascent» (11) — and it is a parable that God (Mighty and Majestic) struck for him; He says: sins are before you like a mountain; so if you free a slave, that [act] storms through those sins until they melt and vanish — like a man who has a steep ascent before him and he charges through it, so that it is levelled out before him [7]; and likewise whoever commits a sin and seeks forgiveness of his Lord and expiates it with almsgiving, his sins are stormed through until they are shattered utterly [8], like a mountain when it falls and becomes level with the earth,
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A: «fī» (without the emphatic lām).
2. In A: «Allāh (Mighty and Majestic)». [.....]
3. In A: «aḥrazahu» (without «wa-in»).
4. «He says: I have squandered wealth in abundance» and its exegesis are missing from A, F; it was mentioned at the beginning of the sūra within the exegesis of the fourth verse.
5. In A, F: «yuḥṣīhā» (feminine pronoun).
6. In A: «ʿalayhā».
7. Thus in A, F; the meaning: so that the road is levelled before him.
8. In A, F: «ḥaṭman»; the more suitable is: «taḥṭīman».

records.text_en: That is His saying: «But he has not attempted the steep ascent». He said: «And what will make you know what the steep ascent is?» (12) — magnifying it. He said: «It is the freeing of a neck» (13) «or feeding on a day of severe hunger» (14) — meaning famine; «an orphan of near relationship» (15) — meaning one with kinship; «or a needy person in misery» (16) — meaning a poor man whose back has stuck [1] to the dust from nakedness and extreme need, and who is ashamed to go out and ask people. And all that is in response to the saying of the Messenger of God ﷺ: «Free a slave or feed sixty poor persons» [2]. God (Mighty and Majestic) says: Was he unable to do one of these two things? And he thought that God (Exalted) did not see him when he spent, so that He would replace that expenditure for him; that is His saying: «Does he think that no one has seen him?» [3] — meaning God (Mighty and Majestic). «Then he is among those who believed» in God (Exalted), His angels, [241a] His books, His messengers, His Paradise and His Fire — «and enjoined one another to patience» — meaning upon the obligations of God (Exalted), what He made obligatory upon them in the Qur'an; for if [4] they do not believe in God, do not do righteous deeds and are not patient upon the obligations, I will not accept from them their expiations and their charities [5]. Then He mentioned the womb-tie, saying: «and enjoined one another to compassion» (17) — meaning by «compassion» [6] the womb-tie, so that they do not sever it. Then He said: «Those»
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A, F: «iltazaqa» (variant form of the verb).
2. Thus in A, F. All of that was revealed in connection with the saying of al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAmr ibn Nawfal ibn ʿAbd Manāf al-Qurashī: «If I enter the religion of Muḥammad my wealth will be in diminution» — deeming it too much to free a slave or feed sixty [text: «years» (sinīn) — sic] poor persons.
3. Sūrat al-Balad: 7.
4. «In» («if»): an addition required by the context.
5. The exegesis is from F; it is defective in A.
6. In A, F: «bi-l-raḥma».

records.text_en: meaning those who believed and did righteous deeds and enjoined one another to patience and enjoined one another to compassion — they are «the companions of the right» (18) — those who will be given their books in their right hands on the Day of Resurrection. He said: «And those who disbelieved in Our verses» — meaning the Qur'an — «they are the companions of the left» (19) — meaning those who are given their books in their left hands; and «al-mashʾama» is in the language of «Banū Ghuṭayf» [1] — a clan of Murād. And all of that is a warning to al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAmr ibn Nawfal ibn ʿAbd Manāf. «Over them will be a fire closed in» (20) — meaning sealed, and it is Hell.
records.foot_note_en: 1. In A: «Ghuṭayf»; in F: «Banū Ghuṭayf». [.....]

records.text_en: Sūrat al-Shams (The Sun) [Running mark:] Tafsīr Muqātil ibn Sulaymān, vol. 4 – m. 45

[Sūrat al-Shams (91): verses 1 to 15] In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. By the sun and its brightness (1) and the moon when it follows it (2) and the day when it displays it (3) and the night when it covers it (4) and the heaven and He who built it (5) and the earth and He who spread it (6) and the soul and He who proportioned it (7) and inspired it with its wickedness and its righteousness (8) He has succeeded who purifies it (9) and he has failed who corrupts it (dassāhā) (10) Thamūd denied through their transgression (11) when the most wretched of them was sent forth (12) And the Messenger of God said to them: The she-camel of God, and her drink! (13) But they denied him and hamstrung her, so their Lord crushed them for their sin and levelled it (14) and He does not fear its consequence (15)
[Sūrat al-Shams [1]] Sūrat al-Shams is Meccan; its number is «fifteen» [2] verses, according to the Kufan count [3]
records.foot_note_en:
1. The purpose of the sūra: various successive kinds of oaths, [sworn] upon the inspiration of creation toward obedience and disobedience, and success and failure; the report of the destruction of Thamūd; and a warning to the people of Mecca, in His saying: «and He does not fear its consequence» (Sūrat al-Shams: 15).
2. In A: «khamsa» (feminine form); and the correct is what I established.
3. In the muṣḥaf: (91) Sūrat al-Shams, Meccan, its verses (15); revealed after Sūrat al-Qadr.

records.text_en: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. His saying: «By the sun and its brightness (ḍuḥā)» (1) — meaning and its heat; «and the moon when it follows it» (2) — meaning when it follows it, moving behind it, and its light is faint in the sky; «and the day when it displays it» (3) — meaning the Lord (Blessed and Exalted) displayed it from the darkness of night; «and the night when it covers it» (4) — meaning its darkness covers the light of the day [1]; «and the heaven and He who built it» (5) — meaning and by the One who built it. Then He said: «and the earth and He who spread it» (6) — meaning: I swear by the earth and by the One who spread it, meaning the Lord (Exalted) Himself. Then He said: «and the soul and He who proportioned it» (7) — meaning Adam; «and He who proportioned it» — meaning and by the One who created it, meaning Himself, who proportioned the two hands and the two legs, the two eyes and the two ears; «and inspired it with its wickedness and its righteousness» (8) — meaning and taught it error and guidance. Then the Lord magnified Himself, saying: «He has succeeded who purifies it» (9) — meaning God has made it happy, meaning God (Exalted) has set it right; for whoever God sets right has succeeded; «and he has failed who corrupts it» (10) — meaning he has perished whom God (Mighty and Majestic) made wretched. Then He mentioned Thamūd, saying: «Thamūd denied through their transgression» (11) — meaning transgression and wretchedness carried it to denial, because wretchedness overcame them twice: once when they denied God (Mighty and Majestic) and were blind to belief in Him, and the other when they hamstrung the she-camel; that is His saying: «Thamūd denied through their transgression»
records.foot_note_en: 1. From A; and in F there is an addition: «and this is an oath».

records.text_en: «when the most wretched of them was sent forth» (12). As for His saying: «And the Messenger of God said to them: The she-camel of God, and her drink!» (13) — by «the Messenger» He means Ṣāliḥ (peace be upon him); he explained to them the matter of the she-camel and her turn of drinking, and what God (Mighty and Majestic) would do to them if they denied and hamstrung the she-camel; that is His saying: «And the Messenger of God said to them: The she-camel of God, and her drink!» «But they denied him» in what he brought, «and hamstrung her» — meaning they killed the she-camel — so [241b] the punishment befell them. He said: «so their Lord crushed them (damdama)» — then He said: «for their sin» — He says: it was only for their sin; for when they hamstrung the she-camel, her foal withdrew far [1] until it climbed a mountain and cried out three times: O Ṣāliḥ, «my mother» has been killed [text: qutilat ayyim — probably ummī]! And all the people of the city were alarmed [2] and went to Ṣāliḥ and said: What can we do? He said: What you can do is take the foal; perhaps God will withhold the punishment from you for the sake of the foal. When they climbed the mountain to take it, it fled from before them and hid and was not seen, and vanished. They said: O Ṣāliḥ, what will God do to us? He said: How many cries [3] did the foal cry out? They said: Three times. He said: Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days — that is the promise [4] that the foal's crying [signified]: «… a promise not to be denied» [5] — He says: there is no lying in it. They said: And what is the sign of that, O Ṣāliḥ? He said: Your faces will turn yellow [6]
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A: «ishtadda»; in F: a smudged word close to «ibtaʿada».
2. In A: «wa-faziʿū».
3. Thus in A, F; the more suitable is: «kam ṣayḥa».
4. In A: «waʿd»; in F: «al-waʿd».
5. This occurs in Sūrat Hūd, verse 65; and the whole story occurs in verses 61–68 of Sūrat Hūd.
6. In A, F: «taṣfār».

records.text_en: on the second day, and your faces will turn black on the third day; he said: then [1] the punishment will come to you on the fourth day. When the first day came [2], the faces of the people turned yellow [3], but they «did not» [4] believe, and said: This yellowness is only from fear and dread. When the second day came their faces turned red [5], and they became certain of the punishment. Then they set about digging graves for themselves, «embalmed themselves» [6] with myrrh and aloes, and shrouded themselves in leather mats. When the third day came, their faces turned black, until they did not recognize one another because of the intensity of the blackness and the change. When the fourth day came, they rose in the morning and «entered» [7] their pits; and when the sun rose and the day was high, the punishment did not come to them, «and they thought» [8] that God would have mercy on them, and they came out of their graves and called to one another; then Gabriel (peace be upon him) descended and blocked the light of the sun, so that they entered into their graves. Gabriel (peace be upon him) cried out at them; and when they saw Gabriel (peace be upon him) and looked at «the light of the sun» [9], they ran until they entered their graves and slept. Then Gabriel cried out at them with a cry — [that] [10] — Rise, upon you be the curse of God! So their souls flowed out of their bodies and their houses were shaken
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A: «thumma qāla» («then he said»).
2. In A, F: «wa-ṣfārrat» [sic]. [Translator's note: footnotes 2 and 3 appear transposed in the edition; they are given here as printed.]
3. In A: «yawm al-awwal»; in F: «al-yawm al-awwal».
4. In A: «wa-lam». [.....]
5. In A, F: «iḥmārrat».
6. In A: «wa-takaffanū» («and shrouded themselves»); in the margin of A: «perhaps wa-taḥannaṭū» («embalmed themselves»).
7. In A: «dakhalū».
8. In A: «fa-ẓannū»; in F: «ẓannū».
9. In A: «ḍawʾuhā»; in F: «ḍawʾ al-shams».
10. «Anna» («that»): an addition required by the context.

records.text_en: until they fell upon their graves, until the Day of Resurrection; and they became as though there had never been anything in their city. That is His saying: «as if they had never prospered therein …» [1]; and that is His saying: «so their Lord crushed them for their sin» «and levelled it» (14) — meaning He levelled their houses upon their graves. His saying: «and He does not fear its consequence» (15). He said, in the order [of the verses]: «when the most wretched of them was sent forth» — «and He does not fear its consequence» — the hamstringer of the she-camel — from God (Mighty and Majestic). And the «companions of the drink» (aṣḥāb al-sharāb) were nine persons, among them Qudār ibn Qudayra [2], who was the hamstringer of the she-camel, and Sālif, Jadaʿ, Qīl, Ḥurayl, Hudhayl, Jamāl ibn Mālik, «Ḥubāba» [3] ibn «Adhādh» [4], and «Jamīl ibn Jawād» [5]. That is His saying (Exalted): «And there were in the city nine individuals spreading corruption in the land and not setting things right» [6]. Abū Ṣāliḥ said: [242a] Some of these «named ones» [7] agree with the naming of the hamstringers of the she-camel in Sūrat al-Naml [8]; and this is the saying of one group and that is the saying of another group; and God knows best.
records.foot_note_en:
1. Sūrat Hūd: 68, the whole of which is: «as if they had never prospered therein. Unquestionably, Thamūd disbelieved in their Lord; unquestionably, away with Thamūd».
2. In A: «Qudhār ibn Qudhayra» with the dhāl dotted; in F: «Qudār ibn Qudayra» with the dāl undotted, and it is more correct.
3. In A: «wa-ḍabāba»; in F: «wa-ṣabāba».
4. In A: «radhādh»; in F: «adhādh».
5. In A: «wa-Jahbal ibn Qarāra»; in F: «wa-Jamīl ibn Jawād».
6. Sūrat al-Naml: 48.
7. In A: «al-musammīn»; in F: «al-muslimīn».
8. He refers to what is in verse 48 of Sūrat al-Naml, that their number was nine: some hold that these are their names, and some hold that some of these names agree with their names; and God knows best. [.....]

records.text_en: Sūrat al-Layl (The Night)

[Sūrat al-Layl (92): verses 1 to 21] In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. By the night when it covers (1) and the day when it appears (2) and He who created the male and female (3) Indeed, your efforts are diverse (4) As for he who gives and fears God (5) and believes in the best [reward] (6) We will ease him toward ease (7) But as for he who is stingy and considers himself free of need (8) and denies the best [reward] (9) We will ease him toward difficulty (10) And his wealth will not avail him when he falls (11) Indeed, upon Us is guidance (12) and indeed, to Us belong the Hereafter and the first [life] (13) So I have warned you of a Fire blazing (14) None will burn in it except the most wretched (15) who denied and turned away (16) And the righteous one will be kept away from it (17) who gives his wealth to purify himself (18) and not for anyone with him is any favour to be rewarded (19) but only seeking the face of his Lord, the Most High (20) And he is going to be satisfied (21)
[Sūrat al-Layl [1]] Sūrat al-Layl is Meccan; its number is «twenty-one» [2] verses [3].
records.foot_note_en:
1. The purpose of the sūra: the oath on the disparity in the state of creation in evil-doing and good-doing, and their guidance to the matter of the Qur'an; frightening some with the Fire and encouraging others with the Gardens; and the command to hasten to almsgiving as expiation for sins and in seeking the pleasure of the All-Merciful, in His saying: «And he is going to be satisfied» (Sūrat al-Layl: 21).
2. In A: «aḥad» [sic].
3. In the muṣḥaf: (92) Sūrat al-Layl, Meccan, its verses (21); revealed after Sūrat al-Aʿlā.

records.text_en: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. His saying: «By the night when it covers» (1) «and the day when it appears» (2) — God (Mighty and Majestic) swore by the night when its darkness covers the light of day, and by the day when it appears from the darkness of night; then He said: «Indeed, your efforts» — your deeds — «are diverse» [1], O people of Mecca. His saying: «and He who created the male and female» (3) — meaning Adam and Eve; and «mā» here is redundant (ṣila); so God (Mighty and Majestic) swore by Himself and by these signs, saying: «and by Him who created the male and female»; its parallel is in «By the sun and its brightness» [2]. «Indeed, your efforts are diverse» (4), O people of Mecca — He says: your deeds differ in good and evil [3]. Then He said: «As for he who gives» — of wealth in the right of God (Mighty and Majestic) — «and fears God» (5) — this verse was revealed about Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq (may God have mercy on him). That is because he passed by Abū Sufyān — he is Ṣakhr ibn Ḥarb — and behold, he was tormenting Bilāl for his Islam, having placed a stone upon his chest and tormenting him with severe torment. Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq (may God have mercy on him) said to him: Do you torment a servant for knowing his Lord? Abū Sufyān said: By God, no one has corrupted this black slave except you, you and your companion — meaning the Messenger of God ﷺ. Abū Bakr (may God be pleased with him) said to him: Would you sell him to me? He said: Yes. Abū Bakr said: By God, I do not find a price worthy of this slave. Ṣakhr ibn Ḥarb said to him: By God, a mountain of hair [text: jabalan min shaʿr] is dearer to me
records.foot_note_en:
1. Sūrat al-Layl: 4.
2. Sūrat al-Shams: 1; and he refers to His saying: «and the soul and He who proportioned it» (7).
3. In A there is an addition: «lashattā» («diverse»). [Running mark:] Tafsīr Muqātil ibn Sulaymān, vol. 4 – m. 46.

records.text_en: than he. Al-Ṣiddīq Abū Bakr said to him: By God, he is better than the whole earth filled with gold. Abū Sufyān said to him: Buy him from me! Abū Bakr said to him: I have bought this slave, who is on my religion, for a slave like him who is on your religion. Abū Sufyān agreed; so Abū Bakr bought Bilāl (may God be pleased with him) and freed him. Abū Sufyān said to Abū Bakr (may God be pleased with him): You have ruined your wealth and the wealth of Abū Quḥāfa. He said: By that I hope for forgiveness from my Lord. He said: When is this? Abū Bakr (may God be pleased with him) said: The day you enter Saqar, to be tormented. He said: Do you not promise me this after death? He said: Yes. He said: The disbeliever laughed and fell on his back, and said: O ʿAtīq, do you promise me resurrection after death? And do you order me to «abandon» [1] my wealth until that day? By al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā, you have lost; your wealth is gone, and you will never get the like of it. Abū Bakr (may God be pleased with him) said to him — [242b] — By God, I will remind you of this day, O Abū Sufyān. So God (Mighty and Majestic) revealed: «As for he who gives and fears God» «and believes in the best [reward]» (6) — He says: in the promise of God (Mighty and Majestic) that He will replace it with better in the Hereafter, if he gives in the right of God (Mighty and Majestic) — «We will ease him toward ease» (7) — meaning We will ease him to return to giving; so We will ease him toward good. «But as for he who is stingy and considers himself free of need» (8) — of God (Exalted), in himself — «and denies the best» (9) — meaning the promise of God that He will replace it with better than it — «We will ease him toward difficulty» (10) — He says: We will make it hard for him to give good. «And his wealth will not avail him» — which he was stingy with in the world — «when he falls» (11) — meaning when he dies and falls headlong into the Fire — meaning Abū Sufyān. God (Exalted) says: «Indeed, upon Us is guidance» (12) — meaning the clarification of guidance — «and indeed, to Us belong the Hereafter and the first [life]» (13) — meaning the world and the Hereafter
records.foot_note_en: 1. «Arfuḍ»: thus in A; perhaps its origin is «afriḍ».

records.text_en: «So I have warned you», O people of Mecca, «of a Fire blazing» (14) — meaning flaming and kindled; «none will burn in it» — meaning the Fire — «except the most wretched» (15) — «meaning these persons from the people of Mecca» [1] — «who denied and turned away» [2] (16) — those who denied the Qur'an; «and turned away» — meaning and turned from belief. «And the righteous one will be kept away from it» — meaning the Fire; He says: God will keep the Fire away from «the most righteous» (17) — meaning Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq; «who gives his wealth to purify himself» (18) — meaning «to make himself righteous» [3]; «and not for anyone with him is any favour to be rewarded» (19). And also — [that] [4] is because Abū Bakr (may God be pleased with him and make him pleased) passed by Bilāl the muezzin while his master Umayya ibn Khalaf al-Jumaḥī was tormenting him for Islam and saying: I will not leave you until you abandon the religion of Muḥammad; and Bilāl would say: One, One! Abū Bakr (may God have mercy on him) said: Do you torment a servant of God for believing in God (Mighty and Majestic)? His master Umayya said: Only you and your companion — meaning the Prophet ﷺ — have corrupted him for me; so buy him from me. He said: Yes. His master Umayya said: With what? Abū Bakr said: With a slave like him, on your religion. He agreed. So Abū Bakr (may God be pleased with him) went and bought a slave, took Bilāl (may God have mercy on them both) and freed him. Umayya said to Abū Bakr (may God be pleased with him): If you had insisted on buying him for an ounce of gold, I would have given [him] to you «for it» [5]. Abū Bakr (may God be pleased with him) said: And if you had insisted on forty ounces of gold, I would have given [them] to you,
records.foot_note_en:
1. «Yaʿnī hāʾulāʾi l-nafar min ahl Makka»: from F; the sentence is effaced in A.
2. «Alladhī kadhdhaba wa-tawallā»: missing from A, and corrupted in F.
3. In A: «yuṣliḥ»; in F: «yataṣallaḥ».
4. «Wa-dhālika»: thus in A, F.
5. In A: «labiʿtuka» («I would have sold you»); in F: «laʾaʿṭaytukahā» («I would have given it to you»).

records.text_en: and Abū Quḥāfa disliked his freeing him [Bilāl], and said to Abū Bakr: Do you not know that the client of a people is of them? So if you free, free one who has presence and «strength» [1] — and Bilāl [2] was black of face. So God (Mighty and Majestic) revealed regarding Abū Bakr (may God be pleased with him): «and not for anyone with him is any favour to be rewarded» — He says: He will recompense him for that; but he only gives his wealth «except» [3] «seeking the face of his Lord, the Most High» (20) — the Exalted above His creation — «And he is going to be satisfied» (21) — this servant, meaning Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq (may God be pleased with him). And Abū Bakr (may God be pleased with him) bought nine persons who were being tormented for Islam, among them Bilāl the muezzin, ʿĀmir ibn Fuhayra and his sister, «Zinnīra» [4] and her daughter, «Ḥāritha» [5] ibn ʿUmar, Umm Kuyās, and al-Nahdiyya [6] and her daughter, who belonged to a woman of Banū ʿAbd al-Dār who used to beat her for Islam; and Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq freed them (peace be upon him).
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A: «wa-fiqh» («and understanding»); in F: «wa-quwwa» («and strength»).
2. In A: «Bilālan»; in F: «Bilāl». [.....]
3. «Illā» («except»): missing from A.
4. In A: «wa-waʾīda»; in F: «wa-Zinnīra».
5. In A: «wa-jāriya»; in F: «wa-Ḥāritha».
6. In A: «al-Nahriyya»; in F: «al-Nahdiyya».

records.text_en: Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā (The Morning Brightness)

[Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā (93): verses 1 to 11] In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. By the morning brightness (ḍuḥā) (1) and the night when it grows still and dark (sajā) (2) Your Lord has not taken leave of you, nor has He detested [you] (3) And the Hereafter is better for you than the first [life] (4) And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied (5) Did He not find you an orphan and give [you] refuge? (6) And find you lost and guide [you] (7) And find you in need and make [you] self-sufficient? (8) So as for the orphan, do not oppress [him] (9) And as for the petitioner, do not repel [him] (10) But as for the favour of your Lord, report [it] (11)
[Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā [1]] Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā is Meccan; its number is eleven verses, according to the Kufan count [2].
records.foot_note_en:
1. The main purpose of the sūra: explaining the honour and distinction of the Messenger ﷺ; His promise to him of intercession on the Day of Resurrection; the mention of the kinds of honour [shown] to him; the favour, and the safeguarding of [him in] poverty and orphanhood from deprivation and humiliation; and the command to give thanks for the blessing, in His saying: «But as for the favour of your Lord, report [it]» (Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā: 11).
2. In the muṣḥaf: (93) Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā, Meccan, its verses (11); revealed after Sūrat al-Fajr.

records.text_en: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. His saying: «By the morning brightness (ḍuḥā)» (1) «and the night when it grows still and dark (sajā)» (2) — God (Mighty and Majestic) swore, saying: «By the ḍuḥā» — meaning the heat of the sun, which is the first hour of the day when the sun rises; and by the night «when it grows still», meaning when its blackness covers the light of the day. So God (Mighty and Majestic) swore by the onset of night and day, saying: «Your Lord has not taken leave of you», O Muḥammad, «nor has He detested [you]» (3) — meaning nor has He loathed you. That is because Gabriel (peace be upon him) did not descend to Muḥammad ﷺ for forty days — and it is said, three days. So the polytheists of the Arabs from the people of Mecca said: If it were from God, «revelation would follow upon him in succession, as was done with the prophets who came before him» [1]; God has taken leave of him and his companion has left him, so he does not come to him. The Muslims said: O Messenger of God, why has revelation not come down upon you? He said: How can revelation come down upon me, when you do not clean your knuckles (barājim) [2] and do not trim your nails? He said: God swore by the two of them, meaning by the night and the day, saying: «Your Lord has not taken leave of you», O Muḥammad, so as to leave you, «nor has He detested [you]» — He says: nor has He loathed you — in response to their saying: His Lord has taken leave of him and detested him. When Gabriel (peace be upon him) came down to him, the Prophet ﷺ said to him: O Gabriel, you did not come until I had begun to yearn for you. Gabriel (peace be upon him) said: I was even more intensely yearning for you, because of your honour with God (Mighty and Majestic); but I am a servant under command: «And we do not descend except by command of your Lord; to Him belongs what is before us
records.foot_note_en:
1. From F; and in A: «so that revelation would follow, as was done with those before him of the prophets».
2. Cleaning the barājim: it is cleaning the dirt that is between the nails and the tips of the fingers.

records.text_en: of the world, and what is behind us» of the Hereafter, «and what is between that» — meaning between the world and the Hereafter, between the two blowings [of the Trumpet], which is «forty» [1] years. Then He said: «and your Lord was never forgetful» [2] — He says: your Lord has not forgotten you, O Muḥammad. «And the Hereafter» — meaning Paradise — «is better for you than «the first»» [3] (4) — meaning than the world; meaning that the Resurrection has drawn near, and the Hereafter is better for you than the world [4]. «And your Lord is going to give you» in the Hereafter «— and it is the good —» [5] «so that you will be satisfied» [6] (5) — meaning until you are satisfied, and you will be satisfied with what He gives you. Then God (Mighty and Majestic) informed him of his state in which he had been, «and reminded him» [7] of the blessings; so Gabriel (peace be upon him) said to him: «Did He not find you an orphan and give [you] refuge?» (6) — He says: He joined you to your uncle Abū Ṭālib, «and spared you the burden» [8]. The Prophet ﷺ said: My Lord has bestowed a favour upon me, and He is the One worthy of bestowing favour. Gabriel (peace be upon him) said: «And find you lost» — astray from the guidance — «and guide [you]?» (7) — so He guided you to His religion. The Prophet ﷺ said: My Lord has bestowed a favour upon me, and He is the One worthy of bestowing favour. Gabriel (peace be upon him) said: «And find you in need» — meaning poor — «and make [you] self-sufficient?» (8) The Prophet ﷺ said: My Lord has bestowed a favour upon me, and He is the One worthy [243b] of bestowing favour. Then God (Mighty and Majestic) gave him instructions, saying:
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A: «arbaʿīn»; in F: «arbaʿīn».
2. Sūrat Maryam: 64.
3. In A: «al-dunyā».
4. The exegesis of the verse is from F; it is missing from A.
5. In A, F: «wa-huwa l-khayr»; the more suitable is: «min al-khayr» («of the good»).
6. In F: «ḥattā tarḍā»; in A: «fa-tarḍā». [.....]
7. In A, F: «wa-yudhakkiruhu».
8. In A: «yaksāl al-tawba» [unintelligible]; in F: «fa-kafāka l-muʾūna».

records.text_en: «So as for the orphan, do not oppress [him]» (9) — He says: do not rebuke him and do not frown in his face, for you were an orphan; «and as for the petitioner» — meaning the poor, needy person — «do not repel [him]» (10) — do not rebuke him when he asks you, for you were poor; «and as for the favour of your Lord, report [it]» (11) — meaning: give thanks to God «for» [1] what is mentioned in this sūra, and for the good that God (Mighty and Majestic) has done for you, when He said: Were you not such-and-such, and I did to you such-and-such. These two sūras were both revealed in Mecca: «By the ḍuḥā» [2], «By the night» [3], and «Did We not expand for you your breast» [4]; so the Prophet ﷺ began to report them in secret to those in whom he felt confidence. Then Gabriel (peace be upon him) [5] came to him at the upper part of Mecca and pushed the ground with his hands, and a spring of water [6] gushed forth; so Gabriel (peace be upon him) performed the ablution, in order to show the Prophet ﷺ the ablution for prayer; then the Prophet ﷺ performed the ablution, and Gabriel (peace be upon him) prayed with him. When he left, he informed Khadīja, and then she prayed with the Prophet ﷺ [7].
records.foot_note_en:
1. «ʿAlā» («for»): an addition required by the context [text: «al-sibāq», sic, for «al-siyāq»]; it is not in A, F.
2. Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā: 1.
3. Sūrat al-Layl: 1.
4. Sūrat al-Sharḥ: 1.
5. In A: «ʿalayhimā»; in F: «ʿalayhi». [Translator's note: the footnote number is missing from the printed text at this point; it is placed here after «ʿalayhi l-salām» as the nearest fit.]
6. In A: «ʿaynan min māʾ»; in F: «ʿayn māʾ».
7. From F; and in A it is deficient.

records.text_en: Sūrat al-Sharḥ (The Expansion)

[Sūrat al-Sharḥ (94): verses 1 to 8] In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Did We not expand for you your breast (1) and remove from you your burden (2) which weighed upon your back (3) and raise high for you your repute (4) For indeed, with hardship comes ease (5) Indeed, with hardship comes ease (6) So when you have finished, then strive (fanṣab) (7) and to your Lord turn in longing (8) [Running mark:] Tafsīr Muqātil ibn Sulaymān, vol. 4 – m. 47
[Sūrat al-Sharḥ [1]] Sūrat «Did We not expand» — its number is «eight» [2] verses, according to the Kufan count [3]:
records.foot_note_en:
1. The main purpose of the sūra: explaining the expansion of the breast of the Chosen One ﷺ and the raising of his rank and his repute; the replacement of hardship in his affair with ease, his affair [four illegible characters in the printed text] in awaiting His command, and longing toward God (Exalted) and turning to His remembrance, in His saying: «and to your Lord turn in longing» (Sūrat al-Sharḥ: 8).
2. In A, F: «thamān».
3. In the muṣḥaf: (94) Sūrat al-Sharḥ, Meccan, its verses (8); revealed after Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā.

records.text_en: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. His saying: «Did We not expand for you your breast» (1) — He says: Did We not widen your breast after it had been narrow, so that faith did not enter into it, until God (Mighty and Majestic) guided him; and that is «His saying» [1]: «And He found you lost and guided [you]» [2], and His saying: «You did not know what the Book is, nor faith» [3]. And that is because four hundred men «of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, of the People of the Bench (aṣḥāb al-ṣuffa)» [4] were Muslim people, «and when [people] gave them something in charity, they ate it» [5], and they gave some of it as charity to the poor, and they used to take shelter in the mosque of the Messenger of God ﷺ, and they had in Medina neither tribe nor clan. Then they went out, «seeking reward with God» [6], to fight the polytheists — and they were Banū Sulaym, between whom and the Muslims there was war — so they went out to fight them, and seventy men of them were killed. That weighed heavily upon the Prophet ﷺ and upon the Muslims. Then the Messenger of God ﷺ used to invoke «against them» [7] after every morning prayer (ṣalāt al-ghadāh) [8], «reciting the qunūt in it» [9], and invoking «that God destroy them» [10].
records.foot_note_en:
1. «Qawluhu» («His saying»): from F; it is not in A.
2. Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā: 7. [.....]
3. Sūrat al-Shūrā: 52.
4. From F; and in A: «of the People of the Bench, of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ».
5. In A: «ṣaddaqū»; in F: «taṣaddaqū»; the more suitable is: «fa-idhā taṣaddaqa l-muslimūna ʿalayhim bi-shayʾ» («when the Muslims gave them something in charity»).
6. In A: «mujayyishīn»; in F: «muḥtasibīn».
7. In A there is an addition: «that is, against Banū Sulaym, who killed his companions».
8. Thus in A, F; what is meant is the dawn prayer (ṣalāt al-ṣubḥ): he used to invoke against them at the end of the dawn prayer every day.
9. In F: «qanata fīhā».
10. In A: «yadīhim», which contradicts what is established in the Ṣaḥīḥ; the correct is what appears in F: «an yuhlikahum».

records.text_en: So God (Exalted) said: «You have no part in the matter — whether He relents toward them or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers» [1]. Then the Lord (Exalted) magnified Himself, saying: «And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and God is Forgiving and Merciful» [2] — in delaying the punishment from them, because of a knowledge that had already preceded concerning them, that they would become Muslims. And God (Mighty and Majestic) revealed [3]: «Did We not expand for you your breast» — meaning: Did We not widen your breast; meaning with faith, He says: with tawḥīd, so that you say it — the saying: «There is no god but God»; «and remove from you your burden» (2) — He says: and We lowered from you your sin [244a] «which weighed upon your back» (3) — He says to the Prophet ﷺ: it had made your back heavy, and We removed it from you, in accordance with His saying: «Indeed, We have given you a clear conquest, that God may forgive you what preceded of your sin and what will follow, and complete His favour upon you and guide you to a straight path» [4], O Muḥammad; «and raise high for you your repute» (4) — among the people, as a banner (ʿalaman) [unvocalised; possibly ʿilman, «knowledge»]: whenever God (Exalted) is mentioned, the Messenger of God ﷺ is mentioned with Him, even in the marriage address (khuṭbat al-nisāʾ). «For indeed, with hardship comes ease» (5) «Indeed, with hardship comes ease» (6) — He says: with hardship there is relief. The Prophet ﷺ said at that: One hardship will never overcome two eases, God willing.
