Then He said: «So when you have finished», O Muḥammad, the obligatory prayer — after the tashahhud, and the recitation, and the bowing and the prostration, while you are sitting [text: wa-abta, sic, for wa-anta] before you say the salām — «then strive (fanṣab)» (7) «and to your Lord» in supplication «turn in longing» (8) to Him in asking. So He forbade him from the qunūt in the morning prayer (ṣalāt al-ghadāh) [5].
records.foot_note_en:
1. Sūrat Āl ʿImrān: 128.
2. Sūrat Āl ʿImrān: 129.
3. In A, F: «fa-anzala» («so He revealed»).
4. Sūrat al-Fatḥ: 1–2.
5. To this Muqātil holds; and among the jurists are those who held that God did not forbid him from that, and they mentioned that the qunūt in the dawn prayer is legislated, especially in times of hardship and calamities (nawāzil).

records.text_en: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Thābit narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: al-Hudhayl narrated to us, saying: Muqātil [text: Muqātilin, with the genitive ending] narrated to us, from ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, who said: My intimate friend (khalīlī) parted from me with four practices: he would give the adhān twice, and give the iqāma twice, and give the salām twice, until the whiteness of his right cheek and his left became visible; and he would not perform the qunūt in the morning prayer (ṣalāt al-ghadāh) [1]; and he would delay the dawn prayer until it was quite light (yusfiru jiddan) [2], ﷺ.
records.foot_note_en:
1. The Ḥanafīs held that the qunūt in the morning prayer (ṣalāt al-ghadāh) occurs only in times of calamity (nāzila). [.....]
2. Yusfiru jiddan: that is, he delays the dawn prayer until the day becomes light and clear. He said: «and by the dawn when it brightens (asfara)» (Sūrat al-Muddaththir: 34).

records.text_en: Sūrat al-Tīn (The Fig)

[Sūrat al-Tīn (95): verses 1 to 8] In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. By the fig and the olive (1) and Mount Sinai (Ṭūr Sīnīn) (2) and this secure city (3) We have certainly created man in the best of stature (taqwīm) (4) Then We returned him to the lowest of the low (5) except those who believed and did righteous deeds, for they will have a reward uninterrupted (ghayr mamnūn) (6) So what causes you to deny the Judgement (al-dīn) after [this]? (7) Is not God the most judicious of judges (aḥkam al-ḥākimīn)? (8)
[Sūrat al-Tīn [1]] Sūrat al-Tīn is Meccan; its number is «eight» [2] verses, according to the Kufan count [3]
records.foot_note_en:
1. The purpose of the sūra: the oath upon the beauty of the creation of man, and the return of the disbeliever to the Fires, and the honouring of the believers with the greatest of fair rewards, and the explanation that God is Wise and the Wisest, in His saying: «Is not God the most judicious of judges?» (Sūrat al-Tīn: 8).
2. In A, F: «thamān».
3. In the muṣḥaf: (95) Sūrat al-Tīn, Meccan, its verses (8); revealed after Sūrat al-Burūj.

records.text_en: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. His saying: «By the fig and the olive» (1) — God (Mighty and Majestic) swore by the fig which is eaten, and the olive from which oil is extracted; «and Mount Sinai (Ṭūr Sīnīn)» (2) — meaning the beautiful mountain, which is in Nabatean; it is the mountain upon which God (Exalted) spoke to Moses (peace be upon him) on the day he took the Torah; and any mountain that does not bear fruit is not called «Sīnāʾ»; «and this secure city» (3) — meaning Mecca, in which every fearful person is secure, and everyone, in the Jāhiliyya and in Islam, and the ḥudūd penalties are not carried out in it. So God (Mighty and Majestic) swore by these four signs, saying: «We have certainly created man in the best of stature» (4) — meaning walking on two legs while others walk on four; and the best of stature is youth and beauty of form; «then We returned him» after youth and beautiful form «to the lowest of the low» (5) — meaning in form, because his eyebrows fall, and his youth goes, and his intellect, his strength, his voice and his form, so that there is «nothing» [1] uglier than he; and God did not create anything more beautiful than youth. Then He made an exception, saying: «except those who believed and did righteous deeds, for they will have a reward uninterrupted» (6) [244b] — meaning not diminished, nor held over them as a favour — He says: there is no reward in old age (haram) [2] except for the believers; for when a believer grows old and falls ill, his good deeds are recorded for him in his old age, together with what he used to do in his youth and health, without it being diminished, or being held against him as a favour; but as for the disbeliever,
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A: «shayʾ»; in F: «shayʾan».
2. In A: «al-qawm» («the people»); in F: «al-haram» («old age»).

records.text_en: when he grows old and aged, [his life] is sealed for him with polytheism, and the Fire becomes obligatory for him, so he dies while God (Blessed and Exalted) is angry with him, and the angels, and the heavens and the earth [1]. His saying: «So what causes you to deny the Judgement after [this]?» — He says: What causes you to deny, O man — meaning ʿAdī ibn Rabīʿa — the Judgement (al-dīn), meaning the resurrection, after the beautiful form and youth, and after old age; and it was about him that this verse was revealed. He says: he denies you regarding the Resurrection; so «God» [2] says: The One who did that to him is able to resurrect him and call him to account. Then He said: «Is not God the most judicious of judges?» (8) — to judge between you and the people of Mecca. The Messenger of God ﷺ said: Yes, and I am, to that, among the witnesses, O most judicious of judges. Meaning: O most decisive of the decisive. He says: He will decide between you, O Muḥammad, and the people of denial. And every instance in the Qur'an of «Is not God…?» means «I am God». ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us: my father narrated to me: al-Hudhayl narrated to us: Muqātil [text: Muqātilin] narrated to us, from Abū ʿUbayda, from Anas ibn Mālik, who said: Whoever's head and beard turn grey in Islam, for every hair there is a good deed for him, and every hair «becomes» [3] «in it» [4] a light on the Day of Resurrection. ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: al-Hudhayl narrated to us, from Khālid al-Zayyāt, from one who narrated it to him, from Anas ibn Mālik, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: The newborn, until he reaches the age of liability (al-ḥinth), whatever good deed he does is recorded for his parents, and whatever evil deed he does is not recorded against him, nor against his parents; then when he reaches the age of liability and the pen runs upon him, the two angels who are with him are commanded
records.foot_note_en:
1. From A; and it is not in F.
2. «Allāh»: an addition required by the context.
3. In A: «wa-kānat»; in F: «wa-ṣārat».
4. In A: «fīhi»; in F: «minhu».

records.text_en: to be vigilant and to «keep him on the right course» [1]; then when he reaches forty years in Islam, God (Mighty and Majestic) secures him from the three afflictions: madness, leprosy and vitiligo; when he reaches fifty, his reckoning is lightened for him; when he reaches sixty, God (Mighty and Majestic) grants him turning back (inābah) to Him; when he reaches seventy, «the people of heaven love him» [2]; when he reaches eighty, his good deeds are recorded for him and his evil deeds are overlooked; when he reaches ninety, what preceded of his sin and what will follow is forgiven him, and he is allowed to intercede for the people of his household, and he is named with God «the captive of God in His earth»; and when he reaches the most abject [stage] of life — «… so that he knows nothing after having knowledge» [3] — there is recorded for him «the like of» [4] what he used to do in his health of good, and if he does an evil deed, it is not recorded against him.
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A: «yusaddidā»; in F: «yatashaddadā».
2. In A: «ḥubbahu»; in F: «aḥabbahu».
3. Sūrat al-Ḥajj: 5.
4. «Mithl»: from A; it is not in F. [Running mark:] Tafsīr Muqātil ibn Sulaymān, vol. 4 – m. 48 [.....]

records.text_en: Sūrat al-ʿAlaq (The Clot)

[Sūrat al-ʿAlaq (96): verses 1 to 19] In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Read in the name of your Lord who created (1) Created man from a clot (ʿalaq) (2) Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous (3) Who taught by the pen (4) Taught man that which he knew not (5) No! Indeed, man transgresses (6) because he sees himself self-sufficient (7) Indeed, to your Lord is the return (8) Have you seen the one who forbids (9) a servant when he prays? (10) Have you seen if he is upon guidance (11) or enjoins righteousness (taqwā)? (12) Have you seen if he denies and turns away? (13) Does he not know that God sees? (14) No! If he does not desist, We will surely seize [him] by the forelock (15) a lying, sinning forelock (16) Then let him call his associates (nādiyah) (17) We will call the guards of Hell (zabāniyah) (18) No! Do not obey him, but prostrate and draw near (19)
[Sūrat al-ʿAlaq [1]] Sūrat al-ʿAlaq is Meccan; its number is «nineteen» [2] verses, according to the Kufan count [3].
records.foot_note_en:
1. The main purpose of the sūra: beginning all matters with the name of the Creator, the Lord (Exalted), may His majesty be glorified; the favour upon creation of teaching writing and wisdom; the complaint against the people of misguidance; the threatening of the people of disbelief and disobedience; the frightening of the disbelievers with punishment; and the glad tidings to those who prostrate of nearness, in His saying: «… but prostrate and draw near» (Sūrat al-ʿAlaq: 19).
2. In A: «tisʿata ʿashar»; and the correct is what I established.
3. In the muṣḥaf: (96) Sūrat al-ʿAlaq, Meccan, its verses (19); and it is the first of what was revealed of the Qur'an.

records.text_en: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. His saying: «Read in the name of your Lord» — meaning the One — «who created» (1) — meaning man. And the first thing revealed of the Qur'an was five verses, «the beginning of» [1] this sūra: «Created man from a clot» (2) — which is the nuṭfa that remains twenty nights, then becomes water and blood; that is the ʿalaq. His saying: «Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous» (3) «Who taught by the pen» (4). That is because the Messenger of God ﷺ entered the Sacred Mosque, and behold, Abū Jahl was placing upon his god, whom he worshipped, a collar of gold, which he had perfumed with musk, and he was saying: O Hubal, for everything there is a place of repose (sakan), and for every good a recompense; by your might, I will surely gladden you next year [unvocalised: la-asurrannaka; or perhaps la-asirannaka]. That was because in that year a thousand camels had been born to him, and a caravan had come to him from Syria and he had profited «ten thousand mithqāls» [2] «of gold» [3]; so he made that a thanksgiving «(shukr)» [4] to Hubal, an idol which was inside the Kaʿba, whose height was eighteen cubits. The Messenger of God ﷺ said: Woe to you! Your god gave to you and you give thanks to another! By God, God has a vengeance upon you; so look when it will be. Woe to you, «O uncle» [5], I call you to God alone; for He is your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers, and He created you and provided for you; and if you follow me
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A: «dūna»; in F: «awwal».
2. In A: «ʿashar alf mithqāl»; in F: «ʿasharat ālāf mithqālan».
3. In A: «min al-dhahab»; in F: «min dhahab».
4. In A: «al-sakan»; in F: «al-shukr».
5. In A: «yā ʿAmr»; in F: «yā ʿamm».

records.text_en: you will gain the world and the Hereafter. He [Abū Jahl] said to him: By al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā «and the Lord of this edifice (al-bunayya)» [1], if you do not desist from this saying of yours, and I find you here worshipping other than our gods, I will surely seize you by your forelock — he says: I will surely drag you out [2] upon your face. Are not these his daughters? He said: And how could He have a child? So God (Mighty and Majestic) revealed: «Taught man that which he knew not» (5) — and the Prophet ﷺ was on that day at al-Arāk in the forenoon — «then» [3] He clarified, saying: «Created man from a clot (ʿalaq)» — meaning from blood, until the nuṭfa turned into blood; «Read», O Muḥammad; then He began anew, saying: «and your Lord is the Most Generous, Who taught» writing «by the pen, taught man» of the Qur'an «that which he knew not». Then He said: «No!» — he does not know, even if you teach him; then He began anew, saying: «Indeed, man transgresses» (6) in the blessings of God (Mighty and Majestic) — meaning Abū Jahl ibn Hishām; and when he gained wealth he became exultant (ashir) — meaning insolent (baṭir) — in his clothing, in his mounts, in his food and drink; that is his transgression: «because he sees himself self-sufficient» — when he saw himself well-off and he was wealthy, he transgressed. So God frightened him with the return to Him, saying: «because he sees himself self-sufficient (7) Indeed, to your Lord is the return» (8) — He frightened him with the Resurrection, in the taqdīm (the transposed order of the text), «after He had said» [4]: «and your Lord is the Most Generous». Then He threatened him afterwards with His saying: «If he does not desist, We will surely seize [him] by the forelock» [5]; then He mentioned the forelock, saying: «a lying, sinning forelock» [6] [7].
records.foot_note_en:
1. From A; and in the margin of A: «al-bunayya — with fatḥa on the bāʾ and kasra on the nūn after it, and with a doubled yāʾ — is the Kaʿba, may God ennoble it». And in F: «wa-rabb al-bunayya».
2. In F there is an addition: «so look what you see! The Prophet of God ﷺ said: Indeed, God will show you a sign»; and it is not in A.
3. In A there is an addition: «thumma»; it is not in F.
4. In A, F: «thumma qāla» («then He said»).
5. Sūrat al-ʿAlaq: 15.
6. Sūrat al-ʿAlaq: 16. [.....]
7. In A, F: («that he sees himself self-sufficient, indeed to your Lord is the return» He frightened him with the Resurrection in the taqdīm, so He said: «and your Lord is the Most Generous» «if he does not desist, We will surely seize [him] by the forelock» in the Fire, then He mentioned the forelock, saying: «a lying, sinning forelock»). I say: it contains obvious errors, and I have tried to correct it within the narrowest limits.

records.text_en: Then He said: «Have you seen the one who forbids» (9) «a servant when he prays?» (10) — and that is because prayer was made obligatory upon the Prophet ﷺ in Mecca, so Abū Jahl said: If I see Muḥammad praying, I will surely strike his neck. So God (Mighty and Majestic) said: «Have you seen» [245b] «the one who forbids a servant when he prays?» — meaning the Prophet ﷺ. God (Exalted) says: «Have you seen if he» — meaning Muḥammad — «is upon guidance» (11) «or enjoins righteousness (taqwā)?» (12) — meaning sincerity (ikhlāṣ) — «Have you seen if he denies» — Abū Jahl, the Qur'an — «and turns away?» (13) — meaning and turns aside — «Does he not know» — Abū Jahl — «that God sees?» (14) — [He sees] the Prophet ﷺ alone, and sees the gathering of Abū Jahl. Then He said: «No!» — he does not know that God (Mighty and Majestic) sees all that. Then He frightened him, saying: «If he does not desist» — meaning Abū Jahl, from Muḥammad, through denial and turning away — «We will surely seize [him] by the forelock» (15) — He says: We will surely take hold of the forelock with a severe seizing. Then He informed that he is a wicked one, saying: «a lying, sinning forelock» (16) — He says: the angel will drag him upon his face in the Fire only because of his sin. Then He said: «Then let him call his associates (nādiyah)» (17) — meaning the Banū Makhzūm, meaning his supporters — «We will call «(sa-nadʿu)» [1] the guards of Hell (zabāniyah)» (18) — and they are more intensely angry at him than Banū Makhzūm are at Muḥammad ﷺ; because he had said to the Messenger of God ﷺ: If you do not desist and I see you here, I will surely drag you upon your face — by that he wanted «to» [2] humiliate the Messenger of God ﷺ; so there was revealed concerning him «that He would humiliate him» [3], saying: if he does not desist from you and from his statement of polytheism, «We will surely seize [him] by the forelock». The Messenger of God ﷺ said: I saw Abū Jahl in
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A: «sandʿuwā».
2. «An» («to»): from F; it is not in A.
3. In A: «an yudhillahu»; in F: «yudhilluhu».

records.text_en: «a ṭamṭām» [1] of fire [meaning uncertain: a great mass or surge], being dragged upon his face in the Fire of Hell over mountains of burning coals, and thrown into its valleys; and he says: May my father and mother be Muḥammad's ransom! He was sincere in his counsel to me, and wished good for me, but I was one who wronged himself, and I wished evil for him. My Lord, return me to my people, that I may believe in him and command Banū Makhzūm to believe in him [2]. He said: «No! Do not obey him, but prostrate and draw near» (19) — because they used to begin with prostration, then after the prostration the bowing, then after the bowing the standing; so they would stand and seek their requests from their gods; so God (Exalted) commanded that they prostrate and draw near; and the Messenger of God ﷺ used to prostrate, then bow, then stand, and then call upon God (Exalted) and praise Him; so God (Exalted) set Himself against the polytheists after that, and commanded the Prophet ﷺ to begin with standing, then bowing, then prostration. He said: «Then let him call his associates» — meaning his supporter — «We will call the guards of Hell» — meaning the keepers of Hell, their feet in the lowest earths and their heads in the heaven — «No! Do not obey him» — He says to the Prophet ﷺ: do not obey Abū Jahl in abandoning prayer — «and prostrate» — He says: and pray to God (Mighty and Majestic) — «and draw near» to Him by obedience. When Abū Jahl heard the mention of the Zabāniyah, he said: The promise of God has come; and he turned away from the Prophet ﷺ, though he had intended [harm] to him. When he returned, they said to him: O Abū l-Ḥakam, were you afraid of him? He said: No, but I feared the Zabāniyah.
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A: «ṭīṭām»; in F: «ṭamṭām».
2. The noble Prophetic ḥadīth is from F; in A it contains [text: «nafs», probably «naqṣ»] omission and misreading (taṣḥīf).

records.text_en: Sūrat al-Qadr (The Decree)

[Sūrat al-Qadr (97): verses 1 to 5] In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Indeed, We sent it down on the Night of Decree (1) And what will make you know what the Night of Decree is? (2) The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months (3) The angels and the Spirit descend therein by permission of their Lord, with every matter (4) Peace it is until the emergence of dawn (5)
[Sūrat al-Qadr [1]] Sūrat al-Qadr is Medinan; its number is five verses, according to the Kufan count [2]
records.foot_note_en:
1. The main purpose of the sūra: explaining the honour of the Night of Decree in the text of the Qur'an; the descent of the angels brought near from the All-Merciful; and the continuity of their greeting of peace throughout the night upon the people of faith, in His saying: «… until the emergence of dawn» (Sūrat al-Qadr: 5).
2. In the muṣḥaf: (97) Sūrat al-Qadr, Meccan, its verses (5); revealed after Sūrat ʿAbasa. [Running mark:] Tafsīr Muqātil ibn Sulaymān, vol. 4 – m. 49. [Translator's note: the main text above says «Medinan» (madaniyya), whereas this footnote says «Meccan» (makkiyya).]

records.text_en: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. His saying: «Indeed, We sent it down» — meaning the Qur'an — God (Mighty and Majestic) sent it down from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven, to the safara — who are the scribes among the angels; and there would come down on that night, of the revelation, as much as Gabriel (peace be upon him) would bring down to the Prophet ﷺ during the whole year until the like of it the next year, until the entire Qur'an was sent down «on the Night of Decree» (1) in the month of Ramaḍān from the heaven. Then He said: «And what will make you know what the Night of Decree is?» (2) — magnifying it. Then He informed about it, saying: «The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months» (3) — He says: deeds in it are better than deeds in a thousand months other than it, in which there is no Night of Decree [1]. «The angels and the Spirit descend therein» — on that night at sunset — «by permission of their Lord» — meaning by command of their Lord — «with every matter» (4) — they descend in it with mercy, and with every matter that God has decreed and ordained in that year; they bring down in it what will be in that year until the like of it the next year. Then He informed about that night, saying: «Peace it is» [2] — it is wholly peace, blessing and goodness — «until the emergence of dawn» (5). ʿAbd Allāh ibn Thābit narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: al-Hudhayl narrated to us, saying: Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān informed me, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Muzāḥim, from Anas ibn Mālik, from Muqātil
records.foot_note_en:
1. In the exegesis of verse (3) there is a deficiency in A, F; what is established is selected from both together.
2. In A, F: «hiya salām»; and in the margin of A: «the verse: «Peace it is»».

records.text_en: ibn Sulaymān, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Spirit is in the form of a human being of immense stature; and he is the one about whom God (Mighty and Majestic) said: «And they ask you about the Spirit …» [1] and he is the angel (al-malak), and he stands with the angels in rows [2].
records.foot_note_en:
1. Sūrat al-Isrāʾ: 85.
2. He refers to verse 22 of Sūrat al-Fajr, which is: «and your Lord comes, and the angel, rank upon rank».

records.text_en: Sūrat al-Bayyina (The Clear Proof)

[Sūrat al-Bayyina (98): verses 1 to 8] In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Those who disbelieved among the People of the Book and the polytheists were not to be separated [from their disbelief] until there came to them the clear proof (1) a Messenger from God reciting purified scrolls (2) within which are correct writings (3) And those who were given the Book did not become divided until after the clear proof had come to them (4) And they were not commanded except to worship God, [being] sincere to Him in religion, inclining to truth, and to establish prayer and give zakāh; and that is the correct religion (5) Indeed, those who disbelieved among the People of the Book and the polytheists will be in the fire of Hell, abiding eternally therein. Those are the worst of creatures (6) Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds — those are the best of creatures (7) Their reward with their Lord is Gardens of Eden, beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. God is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him. That is for whoever fears his Lord (8)
[Sūrat al-Bayyina [1]] Sūrat «Lam yakun» [2] … is Medinan; its number is «eight» [3] verses, according to the Kufan count [4].
records.foot_note_en:
1. The main purpose of the sūra: explaining the rebelliousness of the People of the Book; the report of the soundness of the rulings of the Qur'an; the mention of the function of creation in the service of the All-Merciful; praise of the best of creatures among human beings; the recompense of each of them according to obedience and disobedience; and the explanation that what is promised to those who fear God is [His] pleasure and good pleasure, in His saying: «… that is for whoever fears his Lord» (Sūrat al-Bayyina: 8).
2. Sūrat al-Bayyina: 1. [.....]
3. In A, F: «thamān».
4. In the muṣḥaf: (98) Sūrat al-Bayyina, Medinan, its verses (8); revealed after Sūrat al-Ṭalāq.

records.text_en: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. His saying: «Those who disbelieved among the People of the Book» — meaning the Jews and Christians — «and the polytheists» — meaning the polytheists of the Arabs — «were not to be separated (munfakkīn)» — meaning desisting from disbelief and polytheism. That is because the People of the Book «said» [1]: «When will the one be sent whom we find in our Book?» [2] and the Arabs «said» [3]: «If we had a reminder from the former peoples, we would have been the chosen servants of God» [4]. So it was revealed: «Those who disbelieved among the People of the Book» — meaning the Jews and Christians — «and the polytheists» — meaning the polytheists of the Arabs — «were not munfakkīn» — meaning desisting from disbelief and polytheism — «until there came to them the clear proof» (1) — Muḥammad ﷺ — and he made clear to them their misguidance and their polytheism. Then God (Mighty and Majestic) informed about the Prophet ﷺ, saying: «a Messenger from God reciting [246b] purified scrolls» (2) — meaning he recites purified scrolls, meaning a book, because it is a collection containing many qualities (khiṣāl) [5], of every kind, purified
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A, F: «annahu qāla ahl al-kitāb» («that the People of the Book said»).
2. From F; and in A: «matā yubʿathu llāhu najiduhu fī kitābinā». I say: «what is meant is: when will God send the Prophet whom we find in our Book?»
3. In A, F: «wa-naqūlu».
4. Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt: 168–169.
5. In F: «khayāl»; in L: «khiṣāl»; and it is missing from A.

records.text_en: from disbelief and polytheism — he says: he recites a book in which there is no disbelief and no polytheism; and everything in which there is a book «is called» [1] scrolls (ṣuḥuf) [2]. Then He said: «within which» [3] — meaning in the scrolls of Muḥammad ﷺ — «are correct writings (kutub qayyima)» (3) — meaning a book (kitāb) upright upon the truth, with no crookedness and no discord; and they were only called «kutub» [4] because they contain many varied matters of what God (Mighty and Majestic) mentioned in the Qur'an. Then He said: «And those who were given the Book did not become divided» — meaning the Jews and Christians — about the affair of Muḥammad ﷺ «until after the clear proof had come to them» (4) — meaning the explanation. God (Exalted) says: Those who disbelieved did not cease to be united upon believing in Muḥammad ﷺ until he was sent, because his description was with them in their books; so when God (Mighty and Majestic) sent him from other than the descendants of Isaac, they differed about him: some of them believed — ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām and his companions from the people of the Torah, and from the people of the Gospel forty men, among them Baḥīrā — and the rest of the People of the Book denied him. God (Mighty and Majestic) says: «And they were not commanded» — He says: Muḥammad ﷺ did not command them «except to worship God, sincere to Him in religion» — meaning by it tawḥīd — «inclining to truth (ḥunafāʾ)» — meaning Muslims, not polytheists — and he commanded them «to establish prayer» — the five obligatory ones — «and to give zakāh» — the prescribed — «and that is the correct religion» (5) — meaning the upright creed (milla). Then God (Mighty and Majestic) mentioned the polytheists on the Day of Resurrection, saying:
records.foot_note_en:
1. In L: «fa-innahā tusammā»; in F: «annahu yusammā».
2. The exegesis of verse (2) is from F, L; most of it has dropped out of A.
3. Verse (3) is missing from A.
4. In A: «kutub»; in F: «kitāban»; in L: «kutub».

records.text_en: «Indeed, those who disbelieved among the People of the Book and the polytheists will be in the fire of Hell, abiding therein» — He says: they will remain in it, and will not die. Then He said: «Those are the worst of creatures» (6) — meaning the worst of creation among the people of the earth. Then He mentioned the abode of him who believed the Prophet ﷺ, saying: «Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds — those are the best of creatures» (7) — meaning the best of creation among the people of the earth — «Their reward» — meaning their recompense — «with their Lord» in the Hereafter «is Gardens of Eden, beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever» — they will not die. «God is pleased with them» for obedience, «and they are pleased with Him» for the reward. «That is for whoever fears his Lord» (8) in the world. And everything created from dust is called «al-bariyya» (creature).
Sūrat al-Zalzala (The Earthquake)

[Sūrat al-Zalzala (99): verses 1 to 8] In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. When the earth is shaken with its [final] earthquake (1) and the earth brings out its burdens (2) and man says: What is [wrong] with it? (3) That Day it will report its news (4) because your Lord has inspired it (5) That Day the people will proceed in separate groups to be shown their deeds (6) So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it (7) and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it (8) [Running mark:] Tafsīr Muqātil ibn Sulaymān, vol. 4 – m. 50.
[Sūrat al-Zalzala [1]] Sūrat al-Zalzala is Meccan; its number is «eight» [2] verses, according to the Kufan count [3].
records.foot_note_en:
1. The main purpose of the sūra: explaining the states of the Resurrection and its terrors; the mention of the recompense of obedience and the punishment of disobedience; and the mention of the weighing of deeds in the balance of justice, in His saying: «So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it» (Sūrat al-Zalzala: 7–8).
2. In A, F: «thamān».
3. In the muṣḥaf: (99) Sūrat al-Zalzala, Medinan, its verses (8); revealed after Sūrat al-Nisāʾ. [.....] [Translator's note: the main text above says «Meccan», whereas this footnote says «Medinan».]

records.text_en: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. His saying: «When the earth is shaken with its [final] earthquake» (1) — He says: it will quake on the Day of Resurrection from the severity of the voice of Isrāfīl (peace be upon him) — meaning it will move and split asunder, until everything upon it is shattered by its quaking, from the severity of the quake; and it will not become still until it casts up what is on its back, of mountain, building or tree; so everything that came out from it will enter into it; «and the world will be shaken» [1] and it will not wait until it settles [2]. «And the earth brings out its burdens» (2) — He says: «it moves» [3] and trembles, and brings out what is in its belly, of people, beasts and jinn, and what is on it of devils; so it becomes empty, with nothing in it; and the earth will be spread out anew, white [4] [247a] like silver, or like khāma [meaning uncertain: perhaps «raw/undyed cloth» or «a fresh sprout»], and it has a radiance like the radiance of the sun; no sin has been committed upon it, and no blood has been shed [5] in it. And that is «that» [6] when the first blowing comes, all creation «dies» [7], «then the second blowing comes» [8].
records.foot_note_en:
1. In F: «wa-zalzala»; in A: «wa-zulzilat».
2. Thus in F; the sentence is deficient in (A).
3. In A, F: «taḥarraka» [sic].
4. The sūra has many errors in (A), and I have relied mostly on (F) in this sūra.
5. In A: «yuhraq»; in F: «yuhrāq».
6. In A, F: «annahā».
7. In A, F: «qaymūn» [sic].
8. In A: «thumma l-nafkha l-thāniya tajīʾu»; in F: «thumma tajīʾu l-nafkha l-thāniya».

records.text_en: As for the first, [the call] is made from beneath the Throne, from above the seventh heaven; and as for the other, from Bayt al-Maqdis — «Isrāfīl sits upon the rock of Bayt al-Maqdis» [1] — and he says: O decayed bones, and severed veins, and torn flesh, come forth to the judgement of decision, that you be recompensed for your deeds. He said: So they come forth from their graves to the new earth, which is called al-sāhira; that is His saying (Exalted): «And behold, they will be on the sāhira» [2]; and also «And the earth brings out its burdens» — it brings out what is in it of the dead and of wealth. «And man says: What is [wrong] with it?» [3] (3) — the disbeliever says, in distress: What is [wrong] with it, that it speaks of what was done upon it? «That Day it will report its news» (4) — He says: the earth will inform of what was done upon it of good or evil; the earth says: [So-and-so] affirmed the oneness of God upon my back, and prayed upon me, and fasted, and made the pilgrimage, and performed the ʿumra, and fought in jihād, and obeyed his Lord; and the believer rejoices at that. And it says of the disbeliever: he associated [others with God] upon my back, and committed adultery, and stole, and drank wine, and did this, and did that; so it rebukes him to his face; and the limbs also bear witness against him, and the recording angels, together with God's (Mighty and Majestic) knowledge of him; and that is the great disgrace. When the denying human heard his deeds, he said in distress: «What is [wrong] with it» — meaning with the earth, that it reports what was done upon it. That is His saying: «And man says: What is [wrong] with it?» in the taqdīm (the transposed order of the text); He says to him: «That Day it will report its news» — He says: it bears witness against its people of what they did upon it of good or evil. When the disbeliever heard «that Day», he said: What is [wrong] with it, that it speaks? The angel who had been entrusted with him in the world, recording his good deeds and his evil deeds, said: This
records.foot_note_en:
1. «Isrāʾīl [sic] sits upon the rock of Bayt al-Maqdis»: from F; it is not in A.
2. Sūrat al-Nāziʿāt: 14.
3. In A, F, L, verse (3) is mentioned out of its place and its exegesis is not mentioned; I have extracted it from speech in the context of the exegesis of verse (4).

records.text_en: is the speech which you hear; «it only» [1] bore witness against its people «because your Lord has inspired it» (5) — «And man says: What is [wrong] with it?» — meaning the disbeliever; He says: God inspires it to report its news; and also: that your Lord inspired it with speech; that is His saying: «inspired it». «That Day the people will proceed» [2] «in separate groups (ashtāt)» — meaning the people return, after the presentation and the reckoning, to their abodes in Paradise and the Fire, in separation, as in His saying: «… That Day they will be divided (yaṣṣaddaʿūn)» [3] — meaning they will be separated: a party in Paradise and a party in the blaze. (And it was mentioned earlier: «and the earth brings out its burdens»; then He mentioned here that the people were brought out) [4] «to be shown their deeds» (6) — good and evil — meaning so that they will witness their deeds. And also «That Day the people will proceed in separate groups» — He says: «the people will be divided» [5] into two parties; and the ashtāt are those who never meet again. He said: to be shown their deeds. Then He said: «So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it» (7) — He says: whoever does in the world the weight of an atom — meaning the weight of an ant, the smallest of the red ants, which we can hardly see because of its smallness — of good, in the taqdīm, will see it that [247b] Day: the Day of Resurrection, in his book; and also «So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it»; «and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it» (8) in his record. That is because the Arabs did not give charity of a small thing
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A: «annahā»; in L: «annamā»; and in general there is confusion in all the copies, and I choose the correct one by selection.
2. «Yawmaʾidhin yaṣduru l-nās» is missing from A, L; it is from F.
3. Sūrat al-Rūm: 43. [.....]
4. In A, F, L: «then He said in the taqdīm: And the earth brings out its burdens; He says: they brought out»; the phrase has an error in meaning, and the correct is what I established.
5. In F: «tatasarrafu»; in L: «tataṣaddaru»; in A: «intaṣafa».

records.text_en: with the small thing, and they did not see any harm in the small sin; so God (Mighty and Majestic) made them averse to the paltry sin, and made them desire the «small» [1] charity, saying: «So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it» in his book. And the dharra is the smallest ant, the small ant; and also: whoever does in the world the weight of a dharra — the measure of an ant — of evil will see it on the Day of Resurrection in his book. It was revealed regarding two men in Medina: one of them, when the beggar came to him, would consider it too little «(yastaqillu)» [2] to give him a crust or a date, and he would say: This is nothing; we are rewarded only for «what we give while loving it» [3]. And God (Mighty and Majestic) has said: «And they give food in spite of love for it …» [4]. He says: This is not of what is loved; so he would belittle it and consider that he is not rewarded for it, and would send the poor man back empty-handed. And the other would take lightly the minor sin: the lie, the glance, backbiting and the like, and say: Nothing is upon the one who does this; God has only promised the Fire to the people of the major sins. So God (Mighty and Majestic) revealed [this], encouraging them regarding the small good, to give it for God's sake, for it is about to «multiply, and warning them against the small evil, for it is about to multiply» [5]. So the small sin, in the eye of its doer on the Day of Resurrection, is greater than the firm mountains; and all his virtuous deeds which he did in the abode of the world are smaller in his eye than a single good deed [text as printed; the sense is unclear].
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A: «al-qalīl»; in F: «al-qalīla».
2. In A: «fa-yastaqillu».
3. In A: «ʿalā mā naẓara wa-nukhrijuhu»; in F: «ʿalā mā nuʿṭī wa-naḥnu nuḥibbuhu».
4. Sūrat al-Insān: 8.
5. The passage from «yukthir» to «yukthir» is missing from A; it is from F.

records.text_en: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Thābit narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, saying: al-Hudhayl narrated to us, from Abū Rawq, concerning His saying: «And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice …» [1] — He said: to the one who came with the laws (sharāʾiʿ) of Islam, there is Paradise; «and justice» upon the people of denial, for them is the Fire. Names of those of the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ — and the mercy of God be upon them — who are buried in Basra [2]: ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn, Ṭalḥa, al-Zubayr, Zayd ibn Ṣūḥān, and Anas ibn Mālik. Names of those of the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ who memorised the Qur'an: Abū l-Dardāʾ, Ibn Masʿūd, Muʿādh ibn Jabal, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, Zayd ibn Thābit, and Abū Zayd. Muqātil — may God have mercy on him — said: Shuʿayb ibn Nuwayb ibn Madyan ibn Ibrāhīm; Ayyūb ibn Tāraḥ ibn ʿĪṣū; Dāwūd ibn Ashī ibn ʿUwaydh ibn Qāriṣ ibn Yahūdhā ibn Yaʿqūb; Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm; Hūd, who is ʿĀbir; Ṣāliḥ ibn Arfaḥshad ibn Sām ibn Nūḥ; Ibrāhīm, whose name is Ibrakhīm, and in the Gospel «father of the nations»; Lūṭ ibn Ḥārān ibn Āzar, who is the son of Ibrāhīm's brother, and Ḥarrān was named after him
records.foot_note_en:
1. Sūrat al-Anʿām: 115.
2. [The passage] is in A, and it is not in F, nor in L here, though it is in L in another place.

records.text_en: Sāra, the sister of Lūṭ, the daughter of Ḥārān, the brother of Ibrāhīm, and she is his wife. Muqātil said: Beauty is ten parts: five for Eve (Ḥawwāʾ), three for Sāra, one for Yūsuf, and one for the rest of the people. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Thābit narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: al-Hudhayl narrated to us, saying: al-Musayyab ibn Sharīk narrated to me, from Hishām ibn Saʿd, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, who said: The angels «said» [1]: Among us are the near ones, those who bear the Throne, and among us are the noble guardians, «the scribes» [2]. You made the world for the children of Adam, to eat and drink and rejoice; so make Paradise for us. So God revealed to them: I will not make the righteous of the offspring of him whom I created with My hand like him to whom I said «Be» and he was. Al-Musayyab said: That is in the Book of God (Mighty and Majestic): «Those [3] — they are the best of creatures» [4] — meaning creation (al-khalīqa). «ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us» [5], saying: my father narrated to me, saying: al-Hudhayl said: Khālid al-Ḥadhdhāʾ narrated to me, from Shaybān, from Bishr ibn Saʿāf, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām, who said: God (Mighty and Majestic) did not create a creation more honoured to Him than Adam (peace be upon him). He said: So I said: Not even Gabriel and Michael, peace be upon them? He said: Yes; they are only a people borne upon something, like the sun and the moon. And [there is] another ḥadīth: that the one prostrated to is more honoured to God (Mighty and Majestic) than the one who prostrates.
records.foot_note_en:
1. «Qālat» («said»): from A, F.
2. In A: «al-kātibīn»; in F: «al-kātibūn».
3. The story is in A, F.
4. Sūrat al-Bayyina: 7.
5. «Ḥaddathanā ʿAbd Allāh»: from A; it is not in F. [.....]

records.text_ar: ‌ ‌سورة العاديات
records.text_en: Sūrat al-ʿĀdiyāt (The Racers)

records.text_ar: ‌ ‌[سورة العاديات (100) : الآيات 1 الى 11] بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم وَالْعادِياتِ ضَبْحاً (1) فَالْمُورِياتِ قَدْحاً (2) فَالْمُغِيراتِ صُبْحاً (3) فَأَثَرْنَ بِهِ نَقْعاً (4) فَوَسَطْنَ بِهِ جَمْعاً (5) إِنَّ الْإِنْسانَ لِرَبِّهِ لَكَنُودٌ (6) وَإِنَّهُ عَلى ذلِكَ لَشَهِيدٌ (7) وَإِنَّهُ لِحُبِّ الْخَيْرِ لَشَدِيدٌ (8) أَفَلا يَعْلَمُ إِذا بُعْثِرَ مَا فِي الْقُبُورِ (9) وَحُصِّلَ مَا فِي الصُّدُورِ (10) إِنَّ رَبَّهُمْ بِهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ لَخَبِيرٌ (11)
records.text_en: [Sūrat al-ʿĀdiyāt (100): verses 1 to 11] In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. By the racers, panting (1) and the strikers of sparks, striking (2) and the raiders at dawn (3) stirring up thereby a cloud of dust (4) and penetrating thereby into the midst of a host (5) Indeed man, to his Lord, is ungrateful (6) and indeed he is a witness to that (7) and indeed he is, in love of good, intense (8) Does he not know, when what is in the graves is scattered (9) and what is in the breasts is brought out (10) Indeed their Lord, concerning them, on that Day, is All-Aware (11)

records.text_ar: [سورة العاديات «1» ] سورة العاديات مكية عددها «إحدى عشرة «2» » آية كوفى «3» :
records.text_en: [Sūrat al-ʿĀdiyāt [1]] Sūrat al-ʿĀdiyāt is Meccan; its number of verses is eleven [2], according to the Kufan count [3]:
records.foot_note_ar:
1. (1) معظم مقصود السورة: بيان شرف الغزاة فى سبيل الرحمن، وذكر كفران الإنسان، والخبر عن اطلاع الملك الديان، على الإسرار والإعلان، وذم محبة ما هو فان، والخبر عن إحياء الأموات بالأجساد والأبدان، وأنه- تعالى- خبير بما للخلق من الطاعة والعصيان. 
2. فى أ: «أحد عشرة» . 
3. فى المصحف: (100) سورة العاديات مكية وآياتها (11) نزلت بعد سورة العصر.
records.foot_note_en:
1. The main purpose of the sūra: explaining the honour of those who fight in the way of the All-Merciful; mentioning man's ingratitude; the report that the Divine King, the Judge, is aware of what is secret and what is public; condemning love of what is perishable; the report of the revival of the dead in body and frame; and that He — Exalted — is All-Aware of the creatures' obedience and disobedience.
2. In A: «aḥada ʿashara» [sic].
3. In the muṣḥaf: (100) Sūrat al-ʿĀdiyāt, Meccan, its verses (11); revealed after Sūrat al-ʿAṣr.

records.text_ar: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمنِ الرَّحِيمِ قوله وَالْعادِياتِ ضَبْحاً- 1- وذلك أن النبي- صلى الله عليه وسلم بعث سرية إلى «حنين «1» » من كنانة، واستعمل عليهم المنذر بن عمرو الأنصاري أحد النقباء، فغابت فلم يأت النبي- صلى الله عليه وسلم خبرها، فأخبره الله- عز وجل عنها فقال: «وَالْعادِياتِ ضَبْحاً» يعني الخيل، «وقيل «2» » إن رسول الله- صلى الله عليه وسلم بعث سرية إلى أرض تهامة، وأبطأ عليه الحبر فجعلت اليهود والمنافقون إذا رأوا رجلا من الأنصار أو من المهاجرين تناجوا يأمره، فكان الرجل يظن أنه قد مات، أو قتل أخوه، أو أبوه، أو عمه، وكان يجد من ذلك أمرا عظيما، فجاءه جبريل- عليه السلام يوم الجمعة عند وقت الضحى، فقال: «وَالْعادِياتِ ضَبْحاً» يقول غدت الخيل إلى الغزوة حتى أصبحت فعلت أنفاسها بأفواهها، فكان لها ضباح كضباح الثعلب، ثم قال: فَالْمُورِياتِ قَدْحاً- 2- يقول يقدحن بحوافرهن في الحجارة نارا كنار «أبي حباحب «3» » ، وكان «شيخا «4» »
records.text_en: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. His saying: «By the racers, panting» (1) — That is because the Prophet ﷺ sent a raiding party to Ḥunayn [1] of Kināna and appointed over them al-Mundhir ibn ʿAmr al-Anṣārī, one of the chieftains (naqībs). They were gone, and no news of them reached the Prophet ﷺ, so God (Mighty and Majestic) informed him about them and said: «By the racers, panting» — meaning the horses. «It is also said» [2] that the Messenger of God ﷺ sent a raiding party to the land of Tihāma, and the news was slow to reach him, so the Jews and the hypocrites, whenever they saw a man of the Anṣār or of the Muhājirūn, would whisper together about the matter [text: tanājaw yaʾmuruhu — reading uncertain], so that the man would think that [his relative] had died, or that his brother, or his father, or his uncle had been killed, and he would feel great distress over this. Then Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to him on Friday at the time of forenoon (ḍuḥā) and said: «By the racers, panting» — He says: the horses ran out at dawn to the expedition until morning came and their breaths rose from their mouths, so that they had a panting like the panting of the fox. Then He said: «and the strikers of sparks, striking» (2) — He says: they strike with their hooves on the rocks, producing fire like the fire of Abū Ḥubāḥib [3], who was an old man [4]
records.foot_note_ar:
1. (1) فى أ: «جبر» ، وفى ف: «حنين» ، وفى ل: «حين» . 
2. فى أ، ف، ل: «وذلك» ، وهو تكرير لما سبق فعدلته إلى: «وقيل» ، ليفهم أنه رواية أخرى فى سبب النزول، ولعل النبي كان قد بعث سريتين وأبطأ عليه خيرهما. أخرج البزار وابن أبى حاتم، والحاكم عن ابن عباس، قال: بعث رسول الله (ص) خيلا ولبث شهرا لا يأتيه خيرها، فنزلت «وَالْعادِياتِ ضَبْحاً» (لباب النقول للسيوطي: 241) . 
3. فى ف: «أبى حباحب» ، وفى أ: «أبى صاحب» . 
4. فى أ، ف: «شيخ» . تفسير مقاتل بن سليمان ج 4- م 51
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A: «Jabr», in F: «Ḥunayn», in L: «Ḥīn».
2. In A, F, L: «and that was» (wa-dhālika). This repeats what came before, so I amended it to «and it is said» (wa-qīla), so that it is understood as another report on the occasion of revelation. Perhaps the Prophet had sent two raiding parties and news of both was delayed. Al-Bazzār, Ibn Abī Ḥātim and al-Ḥākim narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The Messenger of God (ṣ) sent cavalry and stayed a month without any news of them reaching him, so «By the racers, panting» was revealed (Lubāb al-nuqūl by al-Suyūṭī: 241).
3. In F: «Abī Ḥubāḥib», in A: «Abī Ṣāḥib».
4. In A, F: «shaykhun» (nominative, indefinite) [instead of «shaykhan»]. [Running mark:] Tafsīr Muqātil ibn Sulaymān, vol. 4 – m. 51.

records.text_ar: من مصر فى الجاهلية له نويرة نقدح مرة وتخمد مرة لكيلا يمر به ضيف فشبه الله- عز وجل ضوء وقع حوافرهن في أرض حصباء بنويرة أبي حباحب، وأيضا «فَالْمُورِياتِ قَدْحاً» قال كانت تصيب حوافرهن الحجارة فتقدح منهن النار، ثم قال: فَالْمُغِيراتِ صُبْحاً- 3- وذلك أن الحيل صبحت العدو بغارة يقول غارت عليهم صبحا فَأَثَرْنَ بِهِ نَقْعاً- 4- يقول فأثرن بجريهن يعني بحوافرهن «نقعا «1» » في التراب. «حدثنا عبد الله بن ثابت، قال الفراء «2» » : النقع: الغبار، فَوَسَطْنَ بِهِ جَمْعاً- 5- يعني بعدوهن، يقول حين تعدو الخيل جمع القوم يعني العدو، فأقسم الله- عز وجل «بالعاديات ضبحا «3» » وحدها: إِنَّ الْإِنْسانَ لِرَبِّهِ لَكَنُودٌ- 6- وأيضا «فَوَسَطْنَ بِهِ جَمْعاً» يقول فوسطن بذلك «الغبار «4» » جمعا، يقول حمل المسلمون عليهم، فهزموهم، فضرب بعضهم بعضا، حتى ارتفع الوهج «الذي كان ارتفع «5» » من حوافر الحيل إلى السماء، فهزم الله المشركين وقتلهم، فأخبره الله- عز وجل بعلامات الخيل، والغبار، وكيف فعل بهم؟ فقال رسول الله- صلى الله عليه وسلم: يا جبريل، ومتى كان هذا؟ قال: اليوم. فخرج رسول الله- صلى الله عليه وسلم فأخبر المسلمين بذلك، وقرأ عليهم كتاب الله- عز وجل ففرحوا واستبشروا، وأخرى الله- عز وجل
records.text_en: of Miṣr in the pre-Islamic era, who had a little fire (nuwayra) that he would kindle at times and let die down at times, so that no guest would pass by him; so God (Mighty and Majestic) likened the light made by the striking of their hooves on pebbly ground to the little fire of Abū Ḥubāḥib. And also «and the strikers of sparks, striking»: he said: their hooves would strike the stones and sparks would fly from them. Then He said: «and the raiders at dawn» (3) — that is because the horses raided the enemy at dawn; He says: they raided them in the morning. «stirring up thereby a cloud of dust» (4) — He says: they stirred up by their running, that is, by their hooves, «a cloud of dust» [1] in the soil. [ʿAbd Allāh ibn Thābit narrated to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ said] [2]: naqʿ is dust. «and penetrating thereby into the midst of a host» (5) — meaning by their galloping; He says: when the horses gallop, they split the host of the people, meaning the enemy. So God (Mighty and Majestic) swore by «the racers, panting» [3] alone: «Indeed man, to his Lord, is ungrateful» (6). And also «and penetrating thereby into the midst of a host»: He says: they penetrated with that dust [4] into the midst of a host; He says: the Muslims charged at them and routed them, and they struck one another, until the heat-glow «that had risen» [5] from the hooves of the horses rose to the sky; and God routed the polytheists and killed them. So God (Mighty and Majestic) told him of the signs of the horses and of the dust, and how He had dealt with them. The Messenger of God ﷺ said: O Gabriel, and when was this? He said: Today. So the Messenger of God ﷺ went out and told the Muslims of this and recited to them the Book of God (Mighty and Majestic), and they rejoiced and were glad; and further, God (Mighty and Majestic) [text: wa-ukhrā — probably akhzā, «put to shame»]
records.foot_note_ar:
1. (1) فى أ، ف: «نقع» . 
2. حدثنا عبد الله بن ثابت، «قال الفراء» : من أ، وفى ف: «قال أبو محمد، قال الفراء» ، أقول: «وأبو محمد هو عبد الله بن ثابت» . 
3. فى أ، ف: «بو العاديات» . 
4. فى أ: «المغار» ، وفى ف: «الغبار» . 
5. «الذي كان ارتفع» : كذا فى أ، ف، والأنسب: «الذي يرتفع» .
records.foot_note_en:
1. In A, F: «naqʿun» (indefinite).
2. «ʿAbd Allāh ibn Thābit narrated to us, al-Farrāʾ said»: from A; in F: «Abū Muḥammad said, al-Farrāʾ said». I say: Abū Muḥammad is ʿAbd Allāh ibn Thābit.
3. In A, F: «bw al-ʿādiyāt ḍabḥan» [sic].
4. In A: «al-mighār», in F: «al-ghubār».
5. «alladhī kāna irtafaʿa»: thus in A, F; the more suitable reading is «alladhī yartafiʿu».

records.text_ar: اليهود والمنافقين «إِنَّ الْإِنْسانَ لِرَبِّهِ لَكَنُودٌ» يعني لكفور نزلت في قرط بن عبد الله بن عمرو بن نوفل القرشي، وهو الرجل الذي أكل وحده، وأشبع بطنه وأجاع عبده، ومنع رفده، ولم يعط قومه شيئا، يسمى بلسان بني مالك بن كنانة «الكنود» ثم قال: وَإِنَّهُ عَلى ذلِكَ لَشَهِيدٌ- 7- يقول إن الله- عز وجل على كفر قرط لشهيد، ثم أخبر عنه فقال: وَإِنَّهُ لِحُبِّ الْخَيْرِ لَشَدِيدٌ- 8- يعني المال، ثم خوفه فقال: أَفَلا يَعْلَمُ يعني فهلا يعلم إِذا بُعْثِرَ يعني «بعث «1» » ما فِي الْقُبُورِ- 9- من الموتى وَحُصِّلَ ما فِي الصُّدُورِ- 10- من الخير والشر، يعني تميز ما في القلوب إِنَّ رَبَّهُمْ بِهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ يعني يوم القيامة لَخَبِيرٌ- 11- بالصالح منهم والطالح.
records.text_en: the Jews and the hypocrites. «Indeed man, to his Lord, is ungrateful» — meaning very ungrateful (kafūr). It was revealed about Qurṭ ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn Nawfal al-Qurashī, the man who ate alone and filled his belly while starving his servant, withheld his gift, and gave his people nothing; in the tongue of Banū Mālik ibn Kināna he is called «al-kanūd». Then He said: «and indeed he is a witness to that» (7) — He says: God (Mighty and Majestic) is witness to Qurṭ's ingratitude. Then He told about him and said: «and indeed he is, in love of good, intense» (8) — meaning wealth. Then He warned him, saying: «Does he not know» — meaning, why does he not know — «when what is in the graves is scattered» — meaning raised [1] — «what is in the graves» (9) of the dead, «and what is in the breasts is brought out» (10) of good and evil — meaning what is in the hearts is distinguished. «Indeed their Lord, concerning them, on that Day» — meaning the Day of Resurrection — «is All-Aware» (11) — of the righteous among them and of the wicked.
records.foot_note_ar: 1. (1) فى أ، ف: «بحث» ، والأنسب: «بعث» ، وفى الجلالين: (بعثر) أثير وأخرج» .
records.foot_note_en: 1. In A, F: «baḥatha», but the more suitable is «baʿatha». In al-Jalālayn: «(buʿthira): was stirred up and brought out».

records.text_ar: ‌ ‌سورة القارعة
records.text_en: Sūrat al-Qāriʿa (The Striking Calamity)

records.text_ar: ‌ ‌[سورة القارعة (101) : الآيات 1 الى 11] بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الْقارِعَةُ (1) مَا الْقارِعَةُ (2) وَما أَدْراكَ مَا الْقارِعَةُ (3) يَوْمَ يَكُونُ النَّاسُ كَالْفَراشِ الْمَبْثُوثِ (4) وَتَكُونُ الْجِبالُ كَالْعِهْنِ الْمَنْفُوشِ (5) فَأَمَّا مَنْ ثَقُلَتْ مَوازِينُهُ (6) فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ راضِيَةٍ (7) وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَفَّتْ مَوازِينُهُ (8) فَأُمُّهُ هاوِيَةٌ (9) وَما أَدْراكَ ما هِيَهْ (10) نارٌ حامِيَةٌ (11)
records.text_en: [Sūrat al-Qāriʿa (101): verses 1 to 11] In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. The Striking Calamity (1) What is the Striking Calamity? (2) And what will make you know what the Striking Calamity is? (3) On the Day when people will be like scattered moths (4) and the mountains will be like fluffed wool (5) Then as for him whose scales are heavy (6) he will be in a pleasant life (7) and as for him whose scales are light (8) his mother will be the Abyss (9) And what will make you know what it is? (10) A blazing Fire (11)

records.text_ar: [سورة القارعة «1» ] سورة القارعة مكية عددها «إحدى عشرة «2» » آية كوفى «3»
records.text_en: [Sūrat al-Qāriʿa [1]] Sūrat al-Qāriʿa is Meccan; its number of verses is eleven [2], according to the Kufan count [3]
records.foot_note_ar:
1. (1) معظم مقصود السورة: بيان هيبة العرصات، ومواقف القيامة وتأثيرها فى الجمادات والحيوانات، وذكر وزن الحسنات والسيئات، وشرح عيش أهل الدرجات، وبيان حال أصحاب الدركات، فى قوله: «نارٌ حامِيَةٌ» سورة القارعة: 11. [.....] 
2. فى أ: «أحد عشر» ، والصواب ما أثبت. 
3. فى المصحف: (101) سورة القارعة مكية وآياتها (11) نزلت بعد سورة قريش.
records.foot_note_en:
1. The main purpose of the sūra: explaining the awe of the plains and stations of the Resurrection and its effect on inanimate things and animals; mentioning the weighing of good and evil deeds; describing the life of the people of the (high) ranks; and explaining the state of the people of the (lowest) depths, in His saying: «A blazing Fire» (Sūrat al-Qāriʿa: 11). [.....]
2. In A: «aḥada ʿashar»; the correct is what I established.
3. In the muṣḥaf: (101) Sūrat al-Qāriʿa, Meccan, its verses (11); revealed after Sūrat Quraysh.

records.text_ar: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمنِ الرَّحِيمِ قوله: الْقارِعَةُ- 1- ثم بين لهم: مَا الْقارِعَةُ- 2- فقال يقرع الله- عز وجل أعداءه بالعذاب، ثم قال للنبي- صلى الله عليه وسلم وَما أَدْراكَ مَا الْقارِعَةُ- 3- تعظيما لها لشدتها، وكل شيء [249 أ] في القرآن «وَما أَدْراكَ» فقد أخبر به النبي- صلى الله عليه وسلم، وكل شيء فى القرآن، «وَما يُدْرِيكَ» فما لم يخبر به، وفي الأحزاب « … وَما يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّ السَّاعَةَ تَكُونُ قَرِيباً «1» » وقال فى هذه السورة «وَما أَدْراكَ مَا الْقارِعَةُ» ، ثم أخبر عنها فقال: يَوْمَ يَكُونُ النَّاسُ كَالْفَراشِ الْمَبْثُوثِ- 4- يقول إذا خرجوا من قبورهم «تجول «2» » بعضهم في بعض، فشبههم بالفراش المبثوث، وشبههم في الكثرة بالجراد المنتشر، فقال: « … كَأَنَّهُمْ جَرادٌ مُنْتَشِرٌ «3» » ، ثم قال: وَتَكُونُ الْجِبالُ كَالْعِهْنِ الْمَنْفُوشِ- 5- يقول تكون الجبال يومئذ بعد القوة والشدة كالصوف المندوف عرقها في الأرض السفلى، ورأسها في السماء، يقول هو جبل فإذا مسسته فهو لا شيء من شدة الهول: فما حالك يومئذ يا بن آدم، قال: كالصوف المنفوش في الوهن، أوهن ما يكون الصوف إذا نفش فَأَمَّا مَنْ ثَقُلَتْ مَوازِينُهُ- 6- يقول من رجحت موازينه بحسناته فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ راضِيَةٍ- 7- ولا يثقل الميزان إلا قول: لا إله إلا الله بقلوب المخلصين في الأعمال وهم «الموحدون «4» » يعنى فى عيش فى
records.text_en: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. His saying: «The Striking Calamity» (1) — then He made clear to them: «What is the Striking Calamity?» (2) — He says: God (Mighty and Majestic) strikes His enemies with punishment. Then He said to the Prophet ﷺ: «And what will make you know what the Striking Calamity is?» (3) — magnifying it for its severity. Everywhere in the Qur'an where it says «wa-mā adrāka» («and what will make you know»), the Prophet ﷺ was informed of it; and everywhere in the Qur'an where it says «wa-mā yudrīka» («and what would make you perceive»), he was not informed of it. In al-Aḥzāb: «… And what would make you perceive? Perhaps the Hour is near» [1]; and He said in this sūra: «And what will make you know what the Striking Calamity is?» Then He told about it, saying: «On the Day when people will be like scattered moths» (4) — He says: when they come out of their graves they will swirl [2] into one another; so He likened them to scattered moths, and likened them in multitude to dispersed locusts, saying: «… as if they were locusts spread about» [3]. Then He said: «and the mountains will be like fluffed wool» (5) — He says: the mountains on that Day, after strength and hardness, will be like carded wool — its roots in the lowest earth and its head in the sky; He says: it is a mountain, yet if you touch it, it is nothing, because of the severity of the terror. So what will be your state that Day, O son of Adam? He said: Like fluffed wool in feebleness — the feeblest that wool can be is when it is fluffed. «Then as for him whose scales are heavy» (6) — He says: he whose scales outweigh with his good deeds, «he will be in a pleasant life» (7); and nothing makes the scale heavy except the saying «There is no god but God» from the hearts of those who are sincere in their deeds, and they are the monotheists [4] — meaning in a life in
records.foot_note_ar:
1. (1) سورة الأحزاب: 63. 
2. فى ف: «تجول» ، وفى ل: «تحول» ، وفى أ: «يخرجون» . 
3. سورة القمر: 7. 
4. فى ف، أ: «الموحدين» .
records.foot_note_en:
1. Sūrat al-Aḥzāb: 63.
2. In F: «tajūl», in L: «taḥūl», in A: «yakhrujūn».
3. Sūrat al-Qamar: 7.
4. In F, A: «al-muwaḥḥidīn» (accusative).

records.text_ar: الجنة برضاه وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَفَّتْ مَوازِينُهُ- 8- «بسيئاته «1» » وهو الشرك لأنه لا يرى شيئا مما كسب إلا صار كالرماد، فاشتدت به الريح في يوم شديد الريح «2» ، وكما أنه ليس في الأرض شيء «أخبث «3» » من الشرك فهكذا ليس شيء أخف من الشرك في الميزان، ولا إله إلا الله «ثقيلة «4» » «وصاحبها «5» » ثقيل كريم رزين عند الله- عز وجل فيأتي صاحب التوحيد بأعماله الصالحة فيثقل ميزانه، ويأتي صاحب الشرك بأعماله الطالحة فلا تكون له حسنة توزن معه فهو خفيف «6» «فَأَمَّا مَنْ ثَقُلَتْ مَوازِينُهُ فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ راضِيَةٍ» وهي الجنة، يعني براضية أنه لا يسخط بعد دخولها أبدا، «وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَفَّتْ مَوازِينُهُ» وهو الشرك فَأُمُّهُ هاوِيَةٌ- 9- يقول لا تحمله الأرض، ولا تظله السماء، ولا شيء إلا النار، فذلك قوله: «فَأُمُّهُ هاوِيَةٌ» يعنى أصله هاوية، كقوله: « … أُمَّ الْقُرى «7» … » يعني أصل القرى يعني مكة، ثم قال: وَما أَدْراكَ ما هِيَهْ- 10- نارٌ حامِيَةٌ- 11- يقول نار حامية تحمي ستة أبواب من جهنم، «وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَفَّتْ مَوازِينُهُ» يقول خفت موازينه «بسيئاته «8» » وحق لميزان لا يقع فيه الحق أن يخف لأن الحق ثقيل مرئ، والباطل خفيف «وبيء «9» » «وَما أَدْراكَ مَا هِيَهْ» تعظيما لشدتها، ثم أخبر عنها، فقال هي: «نارٌ حامِيَةٌ» يقول انتهى حرها.
records.text_en: Paradise, by His good pleasure. «And as for him whose scales are light» (8) — «by his evil deeds» [1] — and that is polytheism — because he sees nothing of what he earned except that it has become like ashes upon which the wind blew fiercely on a stormy day [2]; and just as there is nothing on earth fouler [3] than polytheism, so there is nothing lighter than polytheism in the scale; and «there is no god but God» is weighty [4], and its owner [5] is weighty, noble and dignified before God (Mighty and Majestic). So the man of monotheism comes with his righteous deeds and his scale becomes heavy, and the polytheist comes with his corrupt deeds and has no good deed to be weighed with him, so he is light [6]. «Then as for him whose scales are heavy, he will be in a pleasant life» — and it is Paradise; by «pleasant» He means that he will never be displeased after entering it. «And as for him whose scales are light» — and that is polytheism — «his mother will be the Abyss» (9) — He says: the earth will not bear him, nor the sky shade him, and nothing but the Fire; that is His saying «his mother will be the Abyss», meaning his origin is the Abyss, like His saying «… the Mother of Cities [7] …», meaning the origin of the cities, that is, Mecca. Then He said: «And what will make you know what it is?» (10) «A blazing Fire» (11) — He says: a Fire made hot, heating six gates of Hell. «And as for him whose scales are light» — He says: his scales are light «by his evil deeds» [8]; and rightly so, for a scale into which no truth falls, to be light — for truth is heavy and wholesome, while falsehood is light and noxious «wabīʾ» [9]. «And what will make you know what it is» — magnifying its severity. Then He told about it and said: it is «a blazing Fire» — He says: its heat has reached the utmost.

records.text_ar: ‌ ‌سورة التّكاثر
records.text_en: Sūrat al-Takāthur (Competition in Worldly Increase)

records.text_ar: ‌ ‌[سورة التكاثر (102) : الآيات 1 الى 8] بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم أَلْهاكُمُ التَّكاثُرُ (1) حَتَّى زُرْتُمُ الْمَقابِرَ (2) كَلَاّ سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ (3) ثُمَّ كَلَاّ سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ (4) كَلَاّ لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عِلْمَ الْيَقِينِ (5) لَتَرَوُنَّ الْجَحِيمَ (6) ثُمَّ لَتَرَوُنَّها عَيْنَ الْيَقِينِ (7) ثُمَّ لَتُسْئَلُنَّ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَنِ النَّعِيمِ (8)
records.text_en: [Sūrat al-Takāthur (102): verses 1 to 8] In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Competition in worldly increase diverts you (1) until you visit the graves (2) No! You are going to know (3) Then, no! You are going to know (4) No! If you only knew with knowledge of certainty (5) You will surely see the Hellfire (6) Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty (7) Then, on that Day, you will surely be asked about the pleasure (8)

records.text_ar: [سورة التكاثر «1» ] سورة التكاثر مكية عددها «ثمان «2» » آيات.
records.text_en: [Sūrat al-Takāthur [1]] Sūrat al-Takāthur is Meccan; its number is «eight» [2] verses.
records.foot_note_ar:
1. (1) معظم مقصود السورة: ذم المقبلين على الدنيا، والمفتخرين بالمال، وبيان أن عاقبة الكل الموت والزوال، وأن نصيب الغافلين العقوبة والنكال، وأعد للمشمولين المذلة والسؤال والحساب والوبال، فى قوله: «ثُمَّ لَتُسْئَلُنَّ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَنِ النَّعِيمِ» سورة التكاثر: 8. 
2. فى المصحف: (102) سورة التكاثر مكية وآياتها (8) نزلت بعد سورة الكوثر. تفسير مقاتل بن سليمان ج 4- م 52
records.foot_note_en:
1. The main purpose of the sūra: condemning those who turn toward the world and boast of wealth; explaining that the end of everything is death and perishing, and that the lot of the heedless is punishment and retribution; and that humiliation, interrogation, reckoning and ruin are prepared for those who are included [among them] — in His saying: «Then, on that Day, you will surely be asked about the pleasure» (Sūrat al-Takāthur: 8).
2. In the muṣḥaf: (102) Sūrat al-Takāthur, Meccan, its verses (8); revealed after Sūrat al-Kawthar. [Running mark:] Tafsīr Muqātil ibn Sulaymān, vol. 4 – m. 52.

records.text_ar: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمنِ الرَّحِيمِ أَلْهاكُمُ التَّكاثُرُ يعني شغلكم التكاثر، وذلك أن حيين من قريش من بني عبد مناف بن قصي، وبني سهم بن عمرو بن مرة بن كعب كان بينهم لحاء فافتخروا، «فتعادى «1» » السادة والأشراف فقال بنو عبد مناف: نحن أكثر سيدا، وأعز عزيزا، وأعظم شرفا، وأمنع جانبا، وأكثر عددا، فقال بنو سهم لبني عبد مناف: مثل ذلك، «فكاثرهم «2» » بنو عبد مناف بالأحياء، ثم قالوا: تعالوا نعد أمواتنا حتى أتوا المقابر «يعدونهم «3» » فقالوا: هذا قبر فلان، وهذا قبر فلان «فعد «4» » هؤلاء وهؤلاء موتاهم، «فكاثرهم «5» » بنو سهم بثلاثة أبيات، لأنهم كانوا أكثر عددا «6» في الجاهلية من بني عبد مناف، فأنزل الله في الحيين «أَلْهاكُمُ التَّكاثُرُ» يقول شغلكم التكاثر عن ذكر الآخرة، فلم تزالوا كذلك، حَتَّى زُرْتُمُ الْمَقابِرَ- 2- كلكم يقول إلى أن أتيتم المقابر، ثم أوعدهم الله- عز وجل فقال: كَلَّا سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ- 3- هذا وعيد: «ما نحن «7» » فاعلون بذلك إذا نزل بكم الموت، ثم قال: ثُمَّ كَلَّا سَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ- 4-
records.text_en: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. «Competition in worldly increase diverts you» — meaning rivalry in multiplying distracted you. That is because two clans of Quraysh, Banū ʿAbd Manāf ibn Quṣayy and Banū Sahm ibn ʿAmr ibn Murra ibn Kaʿb, had a quarrel among them and boasted, so the chiefs and nobles became hostile to one another [1]. Banū ʿAbd Manāf said: We have more chiefs, more mighty men, greater honour, a more protected side, and greater numbers. Banū Sahm said the same to Banū ʿAbd Manāf. Banū ʿAbd Manāf outdid them [2] in the living; then they said: Come, let us count our dead — until they came to the graves, counting them [3], saying: This is the grave of so-and-so, and this is the grave of so-and-so. So these and those counted [4] their dead, and Banū Sahm outdid them [5] by three households (abyāt), because they had been more numerous [6] in the pre-Islamic era than Banū ʿAbd Manāf. So God revealed about the two clans «Competition in worldly increase diverts you» — He says: rivalry in multiplication distracted you from the remembrance of the Hereafter, and you continued so, «until you visit the graves» (2) — each of you says [it]: until you came to the graves. Then God (Mighty and Majestic) threatened them, saying: «No! You are going to know» (3) — this is a threat: [that is,] what we shall do [7] to you for that when death comes upon you. Then He said: «Then, no! You are going to know» (4)

records.text_ar: وهو وعيد: إذا دخلتم قبوركم، ثم قال: كَلَّا لا يؤمنون بالوعيد، ثم استأنف فقال: لَوْ تَعْلَمُونَ عِلْمَ الْيَقِينِ- 5- لا شك فيه «لَتَرَوُنَّ الْجَحِيمَ» «1» - 6- لعلمتم أنكم سترون الجحيم في الآخرة ثُمَّ لَتَرَوُنَّها عَيْنَ الْيَقِينِ- 7- لا شك فيه، يقول لترون الجحيم في الآخرة معاينة، «والجحيم «2» » ما عظم من النار، يقينها رؤية العين،: سنعذبهم مرتين «مرة عند الموت، ومرة عند القبر «3» » ثم يردون إلى عذاب عظيم ثُمَّ لَتُسْئَلُنَّ فى الآخرة يَوْمَئِذٍ عَنِ النَّعِيمِ- 8- يعني كفار مكة كانوا في الدنيا في الخير والنعمة، فيسألون يوم القيامة عن شكر ما كانوا فيه، وأيضا فذلك قوله: « … أَذْهَبْتُمْ طَيِّباتِكُمْ فِي حَياتِكُمُ الدُّنْيا وَاسْتَمْتَعْتُمْ بِها.. «4» » وقال: «ثُمَّ لَتُسْئَلُنَّ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَنِ النَّعِيمِ» وذلك أن الله- عز وجل إذا جمع الكفار فى النار صرخوا: يا مالك، أنضجت لحومنا وأحرقت جلودنا، «وجاعت «5» » وأعطشت أفواهنا، وأهلكت أبداننا، فهل إلى خروج يوم واحد من سبيل من النار، فيرد عليهم مالك فيقول: لا، قالوا: ساعة من النهار. «قال «6» » : لا. قالوا: فردنا إلى الدنيا، فنعمل غير الذي كنا نعمل، قال فينادي مالك- خازن النار-[250 أ] بصوت غليظ جهير، قال: فإذا نادى حسرت النار من فرقه، وسكن أهلها، فيقول: أبشروا فيرجون أن تكون عافية قد أتتهم، ثم
records.text_en: which is a threat: when you enter your graves. Then He said: «No!» — they do not believe in the threat — then He began anew, saying: «If you only knew with knowledge of certainty» (5) — about which there is no doubt — «you would surely see the Hellfire» [1] (6) — you would know that you will see the Hellfire in the Hereafter; «Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty» (7) — about which there is no doubt; He says: you will see the Hellfire in the Hereafter by direct sight; and al-jaḥīm [2] is what is great of fire; its certainty is sight with the eye. «We shall punish them twice» — [once at death and once in the grave] [3] — «then they will be returned to a great punishment.» «Then you will surely be asked», in the Hereafter, «on that Day about the pleasure» (8) — meaning the disbelievers of Mecca, who in the world were in prosperity and bounty; so on the Day of Resurrection they will be asked about thanks for what they had. And also this is His saying: «… You exhausted your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them …» [4]; and He said: «Then, on that Day, you will surely be asked about the pleasure». That is because when God (Mighty and Majestic) gathers the disbelievers in the Fire they cry out: O Mālik, our flesh is cooked and our skins are burnt, and we hunger [5] and our mouths thirst, and our bodies are destroyed; is there any way out of the Fire for one day? Mālik replies to them, saying: No. They say: An hour of the day. He said [6]: No. They say: Then send us back to the world, and we shall do other than what we used to do. He said: Then Mālik, the keeper of the Fire, calls out — [250a] in a harsh, loud voice — and when he calls out, the Fire recedes in awe of him and its inhabitants fall silent; and he says: Rejoice! — so they hope that relief has come to them. Then

records.text_ar: يناديهم: يا أهل النار، فيقولون: لبيك، فيقول: يا أهل البلاء، فيقولون: لبيك. فيقول: « … أَذْهَبْتُمْ طَيِّباتِكُمْ فِي حَياتِكُمُ الدُّنْيا وَاسْتَمْتَعْتُمْ بِها، (فَالْيَوْمَ «1» ) تُجْزَوْنَ عَذابَ الْهُونِ بِما كُنْتُمْ تَسْتَكْبِرُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ بِغَيْرِ الْحَقِّ وَبِما كُنْتُمْ تَفْسُقُونَ … «2» » يا أهل الفرش والوسائد والنعمة في دار الدنيا، كيف تجدون مس سقر؟ قالوا: يأتينا العذاب من كل مكان، فهل إلى أن نموت ونستريح، قال فيقول: وعزة ربي لا أزيدكم إلا عذابا، قال فذلك قوله: «ثُمَّ لَتُسْئَلُنَّ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَنِ النَّعِيمِ» يعني الشكر للنعيم الذي أعطاه الله- عز وجل، فلم يهتد ولم يشكر، يعني الكافر.
records.text_en: he calls out to them: O people of the Fire! They say: At Your service. He says: O people of affliction! They say: At Your service. He says: «… You exhausted your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them; so today [1] you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation because you were arrogant on earth without right and because you were defiantly disobedient …» [2] O people of beds, cushions and comfort in the abode of the world, how do you find the touch of Saqar? They say: Punishment comes to us from every place; is there any way for us to die and be at rest? He says: By the might of my Lord, I will increase you only in punishment. He said: So that is His saying «Then, on that Day, you will surely be asked about the pleasure» — meaning thanks for the bounty that God (Mighty and Majestic) gave, and he was not guided and did not give thanks — meaning the disbeliever.
